Why You’ll Love This Role
WoodmenLife is seeking an experienced Cloud Engineer III to help design, build, and evolve our Azure cloud platform. This senior technical role is highly impactful—driving platform engineering maturity, advancing our Azure Landing Zone, and enabling secure, scalable cloud solutions across the enterprise.
You will partner closely with our Cloud Architect and Enterprise Architecture teams to operationalize cloud standards and deliver reusable engineering patterns. This role combines hands-on engineering with platform ownership, mentorship, and influence on the future direction of our cloud environment.
This is a platform engineering role focused on building and evolving the Azure foundation—not just supporting individual application workloads.
At WoodmenLife, you’ll also enjoy a culture that values people as much as technology. With Friday afternoons off year-round, a collaborative environment, and a focus on outcomes rather than hours, you’ll find a workplace designed to support both professional impact and personal well-being.

About the Team
This role is a core contributor of WoodmenLife’s Cloud Center of Excellence (CoE) as part of the Systems Engineering organization.
The Cloud CoE (led by the Cloud Architect) defines standards, guardrails, and platform direction, while the Systems Engineering team provides the delivery and operational foundation for the Azure platform.
As a Cloud Engineer III, you will bridge strategy and execution—owning platform engineering outcomes while helping operationalize the enterprise cloud model.

Role Summary
The Cloud Engineer III is a senior platform engineer responsible for designing, building, and evolving WoodmenLife’s Azure cloud platform. This role owns key platform domains, operationalizes cloud standards and guardrails, and delivers secure, scalable, and automated solutions that support enterprise modernization.

What You’ll Do
Cloud Engineering & Platform Delivery

Lead design and engineering of complex Microsoft Azure platform solutions aligned with enterprise architecture standards
Own and evolve one or more Azure platform domains such as identity, networking, governance, or DevOps pipelines
Integrate hybrid cloud environments leveraging Azure networking and identity services
Lead Infrastructure as Code development using Bicep (primary), PowerShell, and Azure CLI
Advance Azure Landing Zone components (governance, identity, network, security) to support enterprise-scale, secure-by-default environments
Collaborate with Cloud Architects, Enterprise Architects, and cross-functional stakeholders to implement and operationalize approved platform standards, engineering patterns, and cloud guardrails

Monitoring, Cost Optimization & Observability

Enhance cloud observability using Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and App Insights to improve proactive detection and response
Implement cost optimization and financial transparency practices aligned to business outcomes, including tagging, budgeting, and usage analytics
Lead efforts to monitor, analyze, and optimize cloud resource utilization and platform performance

Automation, DevOps & Enablement

Lead development of CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps and modern Git-based workflows
Build automation frameworks that streamline provisioning, monitoring, and operational tasks, leveraging AI-assisted engineering tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Azure AI services) to improve development efficiency and code quality
Develop reusable templates, scripts, and modules to support scalable, self-service platform capabilities and enable development teams through standardized patterns
Embed governance controls, policy enforcement, and configuration management into automation workflows

Collaboration, Leadership & Mentoring

Mentor Systems Engineers and technical peers across the organization, fostering a culture of learning, collaboration, and high performance
Support Agile ceremonies and iterative delivery culture for cloud initiatives
Contribute to the Cloud Center of Excellence through knowledge sharing, documentation, tooling, and best practices

Security, Governance & Compliance

Implement Azure governance controls (Azure Policy, RBAC, resource organization)
Ensure secure-by-default configurations aligned with enterprise security standards
Support identity governance through Entra ID and least-privilege models

Resilience, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery

Lead planning and implementation of cloud-based Business Continuity and DR strategies
Implement resilient, highly available solutions leveraging availability zones, automated failover, and cloud-native backup strategies

Innovation & Continuous Improvement

Evaluate emerging Azure capabilities, including AI and automation technologies, and recommend platform enhancements that improve engineering productivity and platform maturity
Provide technical guidance and advocacy for cloud engineering best practices, automation-first patterns, and modern architectural approaches

What You Bring
Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree strongly preferred
10+ years of progressive IT infrastructure or platform engineering experience, including recent, sustained hands-on experience designing and operating enterprise-scale Azure environments
Deep expertise in Infrastructure as Code (Bicep preferred; strong scripting and automation experience required)
Advanced Windows/Linux, Entra ID/AD, and hybrid networking background
Experience building CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps and modern Git-based workflows
Proven experience with cloud cost management, observability, and performance optimization
Demonstrated technical leadership and mentoring skills

Experience supporting modernization, migration, and automation initiatives

Scope & Decision Authority

Make design and implementation decisions for cloud solutions within established enterprise standards and cloud guardrails
Operationalize architectural direction provided by the Cloud Architect through scalable, reusable engineering solutions
Influence platform evolution by providing engineering feedback, prototyping solutions, and identifying improvement opportunities
Promote and implement standardized engineering patterns, automation frameworks, and Infrastructure as Code practices
Identify and lead resolution of platform-level issues related to performance, cost, reliability, and security

title: Program Lead
description:
Who We Are

Founded in 1926, the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation is a private, not-for-profit educational, historic, and cultural institution that owns and operates one of the largest and best-known museum complexes in the world. Our mission is “that the future may learn from the past” through preserving and restoring 18th-century Williamsburg, Virginia’s colonial capital. We engage, inform, and inspire people to learn about this historic capital, the events that occurred here, and the diverse peoples who helped shape a new nation.

Today, Colonial Williamsburg is the largest living history museum in the U.S. The Historic Area is the 301-acre restored colonial capital with 89 original buildings and 525 buildings reconstructed to how they appeared in the 18th century through extensive archaeological, architectural, and documentary research. The Historic Area is staffed by highly trained, historically dressed interpreters and expert tradespeople who bring the 18th century to life. The Foundation also owns and operates two world-class museums, the DeWitt Wallace Decorative Arts Museum, and the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Folk Art Museum, The Bob and Marion Wilson Teacher Institute, and a renowned research library, the John D Rockefeller Jr Library.

Additionally, Colonial Williamsburg is home to five world class accommodations at the Williamsburg Inn, Williamsburg Lodge Autograph Collection, the Griffin Hotel, the Williamsburg Woodlands Hotels and Suites and the unique Colonial Houses in the Historical Area. Visitors may also indulge in food and drink at our many on-site restaurants and taverns that blend a historically inspired dining experience with today’s evolved tastes. Each year over five million people visit Williamsburg and another 20 million engage with us digitally.

Main Duties

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Rare Breeds Program:

  • Lead and coordinate the Rare Breeds equine program and expand outreach, education, and partnerships internally and externally in collaboration with the Equine Manager.
  • Lead the equine breeding program to promote healthy, manageable, and sustainable breed standards that support conservation.
  • Monitor breeding stock health daily; schedule and oversee veterinary visits, maintain accurate records, and report concerns to the Equine Manager.
  • Administer basic first aid, medications, bandaging, and other treatments as directed.

Engagement and Partnerships:

  • Build and maintain community, local, national, and international partnerships.
  • Grow and lead equine programming and community engagement initiatives.
  • Strengthen and expand educational resources and materials to support general knowledge and conservation efforts.
  • Coordinate volunteer & internship programs, including coaching, training, resources, and growth.

Operational Support:

  • Transport mares on- and off-site via trailer, including after-hours support during breeding season.
  • Provide quality training and cross-train staff; collaborate with internal departments to expand staff skills and knowledge.
  • Maintain organized, accurate, and transparent records for training, medical care, and programming.

Safety & Compliance:

  • Follow all safety protocols related to horse handling, carriage operations, and guest interactions.
  • Ensure compliance with museum policies and equine welfare standards.
  • Report safety hazards or equipment concerns promptly to leadership.

This is a non-exempt position, eligible to receive overtime in accordance with the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA). This position may be subject to overtime during high peak times, etc. as directed and approved by the supervisor.

This job description reflects the general responsibilities of the position and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. Duties and responsibilities may evolve over time based on operational needs.

Required Education and Experience

  • High School Diploma or GED (or equivalent experience in horse care)
  • Good driving record and experience driving horses
  • Interest in history and experience in public programming and engagement
  • Strong knowledge and professional working experience in equine breeding with a focus on AI use
  • Previous experience working with horses in a professional or structured setting.
  • Strong knowledge of horse care, feeding, grooming, and health monitoring.
  • Ability to handle and work around large horses confidently and safely.
  • Willingness to perform physical labor in various weather conditions.
  • Team-oriented with good communication skills and a positive attitude.
  • A valid Virginia Driver's License.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Distribution Center Operations Director
description:
The Director of Distribution Center Operations is the senior operational leader for our Tennessee Distribution Center and is accountable for the facility’s safety, service, quality, productivity, cost, and employee experience.
This leader will establish strong operating discipline, build an effective leadership team, and ensure consistent execution across receiving, inventory, fulfillment, shipping, transportation coordination, maintenance, and facility operations.
The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader who can improve performance, strengthen processes and systems, develop frontline leaders, and build a culture of accountability, communication, safety, and continuous improvement. The role requires both strong daily execution and the ability to lead the facility’s longer-term operational transformation.

Key Responsibilities

Operations Leadership

Provide day-to-day leadership and full operating accountability for the Tennessee Distribution Center.
Establish daily, weekly, and monthly operating plans aligned with volume forecasts, customer commitments, labor requirements, and facility capacity.
Deliver performance against safety, service, quality, productivity, cost, inventory accuracy, and equipment-reliability targets.
Lead operations across receiving, replenishment, picking, packing, value-added services, shipping, and dock activities.
Maintain clear visibility into order backlogs, aging, throughput constraints, staffing gaps, equipment issues, and customer-service risks.
Establish effective daily management routines, including shift handoffs, floor walks, performance reviews, escalation procedures, and corrective actions.
Improve workflows, labor deployment, material movement, and space utilization to increase throughput and reduce waste.
Ensure the facility, equipment, systems, and workforce are prepared for seasonal peaks and changing business demands.
Partner closely with IT, engineering, maintenance, transportation, customer service, finance, HR, and other distribution locations.
Maintain full compliance with OSHA requirements, company safety standards, employment practices, and other applicable regulations.
Collaborate with Finance on operating budgets, forecasts, capital plans, and resource allocation.

Build, coach, and retain a capable and accountable leadership team across all shifts and operating functions.
Set clear expectations for managers and supervisors and hold leaders accountable for performance, communication, employee development, and consistent policy application.
Maintain a strong and visible leadership presence throughout the facility.
Strengthen onboarding, job training, cross-training, coaching, and performance-management practices.
Develop succession plans and advancement opportunities for frontline employees, supervisors, and managers.
Build a culture in which employees are treated with respect, can raise concerns, receive timely information, and understand how their work affects customers, clients, authors, and the broader company.
Partner with HR and Talent Development on recruiting, retention, workforce planning, employee relations, and leadership development.
Champion employee safety, wellness, inclusion, and continuous learning.

Continuous Improvement and Transformation

Use operational data and direct floor observation to identify problems, prioritize improvements, and track results.

Promote collaboration and best-practice sharing across the company’s distribution network.

Bushnell, Florida (Sumter County)

Employees interested in this promotional opportunity must apply for this vacancy using the People First system. No paper applications will be accepted.

Applications will be accepted electronically until 11:59 pm ET on the closing date.

Applicants are responsible for providing the following information on their applicant profile: current employment, previous employment, training, and education.

Incomplete profiles will not be considered.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Must be at least 18 years of age,
  • Be a citizen of the United States,
  • Must have a High School Diploma or equivalent,
  • Must have completed the basic recruit training course for correctional officers and have one year of experience as a certified officer with the State of Florida,
  • Must not have received a suspension within the past 12 months,
  • Must not have received an involuntary demotion within the past 24 months,
  • Must not have received less than a 3.00 rating on a performance evaluation within the past 3 fiscal years.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

This Correctional Officer Sergeant position is located at Sumter Correctional Institution. The incumbent in this position is considered to have regulatory responsibilities and is subject to the provisions of Chapter 60L-36, Florida Administrative Code.

Duties include but are not limited to the following:

Supervises male or female inmates commensurate with the level of risk they present. Manages inmate housing areas, enforces rules and sanitation standards. Transports inmates using approved restraints and observing relevant laws, policies and procedures. Conducts accurate head counts, maintains custody and control over inmates at appointments outside the secured perimeter and escorts inmates within the secured perimeter. Inventories personal property of inmates and issues receipts.

Performs crisis intervention functions to include, but not limited to, subduing or restraining violent or uncooperative inmates, defending persons against attack, and preventing escapes, using approved deadly or non-deadly force, restraints or other approved methods. Required to wear body armor and use weapons.

Maintains facility security. This includes performing searches of inmates and other persons. This includes the visual inspection of body cavities and possible exposure to body fluids. Responsible for checking inmate mail and/or packages for contraband. Observes inmate behavior to identify inmates exhibiting mental or emotional disorders. Uses counseling techniques or referral action, as outlined in written policies or guidelines. Conducts inspections and visual and audio surveillance of persons, property, vehicles, building and outdoor areas. Physically checks doors, windows, gates, barred sections, fences and other areas to ensure proper security.

Provides emergency assistance during emergencies, disasters and accidents to include but not limited to, CPR, first aid, apprehension of escaping or escaped inmates, implementation of evacuation procedures, provides security of inmates and/or areas in accordance with the emergency situation.

Directs Correctional Officers in supervising inmates in housing units and those segregated for administrative or punitive measures. Directs Correctional Officers in checking inmate mail for possible contraband, and in supervising inmates working on work details both inside and outside the fenced perimeter. Directs Correctional Officers in maintaining master inmate location counts and directs the entire operation of the Control Room or the Main Gate. Ensures that all transportation permits are completed accurately and signed by the appropriate authority. Directs Officers in preparing reports such as special progress, minor work, disciplinary and/or incident reports.

Attends mandatory and other training as required.

Performs other related duties as required.

title: Service Centre Analyst
description:
Service Centre Analyst

So… you like solving problems under pressure?

Good. Because this role sits right at the beating heart of a large enterprise environment supporting a seriously important Queensland institution. No pressure at all. (Okay, a bit of pressure, but the good kind.)

What will help you succeed

You don’t need to tick every box, but most strong candidates bring a solid mix of the below:

  • Proven experience in a Helpdesk or Service Desk environment
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and attention to detail (the small stuff matters)
  • Experience with ticketing systems, SLAs, and time tracking
  • Working knowledge of ITIL concepts and best-practice service delivery
  • A genuine customer service mindset, calm, clear, and professional

Why this role is worth your time

If you’re looking to deepen your Service Centre skills, work with good humans, and be trusted to do your job properly, this could be your next smart move.

title: Inside Upholsterer
description:
Position Summary:
Perform a variety of operations to assemble and upholster portions of fully upholstered furniture. Move frame assembly from roller conveyor to upholstery lift and perform assigned duties using air stapling equipment, hand tools, templates, and measuring devices. Work on a variety of models to shape and form the upholstery for a specific appearance, fit and trim.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Use transfer cart to move assembled frame from conveyor to upholstery lift. The upholstery lift (scissor lift) is pneumatically powered and controlled by a foot pedal. Proper bending techniques should be used when moving the transfer cart to prevent strains.

Staple filler material (foam) to the frame. A Pneumatic staple gun is used to perform this task. Safety glasses are required to prevent any possible reflections from hitting the employee’s eye. Repetitive motion is a potential hazard from the triggering motion.

Use scissors to cut excessive filler material from the frame.
The pneumatic staple gun is used again to attach fabric/leather to the frame. The non-trigger hand is used to pull and stretch the fabric/leather to ensure the desired fit.

The seams in the upholstered product are smoothed out and tucked by the use of a regulator (ice pick) for a crisp finished appearance.

Excessive fabric is trimmed off around the finished wood portions of the frame with a box cutter (razor blade).

Occasional lifting is required to sit frames off of the assembly conveyor due to repairs.

Job Requirements:

High School diploma or equivalent
Minimum two to five years experience.
Ability to read and follow directions (verbal and written).
Basic math skills: counting adding, subtracting
Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds individually and up to 100 pounds with assistance
Must have hand to eye coordination
Must be organized and able to multi-task
Must be able to complete job duties in timely manner
Ability to pay close attention to details
Excellent attendance record
Flexible to changing work stations as business dictates
Work and make decisions with minimum supervision
Overtime as required, including Saturday

description:
Job Overview

We're seeking a skilled Architectural Technologist with a strong interest in architectural design excellence to support the high-quality technical execution of projects across a range of scales and program type.

Develop detailed BIM models and working drawings, including plans, sections, elevations, details, schedules, and drawing sets.

Preparing and issuing field review reports

Support internal quality control processes, maintaining well organized project files, drawing sets, and revision histories.

Collaborate with internal teams to meet project budget, schedule, and performance objectives.

Advanced proficiency in Revit for BIM and construction documentation. Working knowledge of AutoCAD.

Demonstrated interest in design excellence, high quality detailing, and contemporary architecture.

title: Outreach and Engagement Specialist

description:

        • Must be able to constantly remain in a stationary, sitting position, communicate and exchange information with others, inspect information, perform repetitive motions with arms and fingers, interpret data, problem solve, make decisions, organize and plan, and maintain a positive and professional attitude in all situations.

title: Travel Representative
description:

About the Role
The Travel Services Representative provides support to Members, Non-Members, Travel Consultants, and the Journeys Groups Division through travel sales, booking services, tour coordination, invoicing, and administrative support. This role assists customers with travel arrangements, including air, hotel, car rental, and group travel bookings, while promoting additional products and services that enhance the travel experience.

The position is responsible for the accurate administration of individual and group travel bookings, including documentation, invoicing, payment processing, supplier coordination, and tour operations support. The successful candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, customer-focused, and able to balance service with operational responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.

The expected hourly or salary range for this role is $18-$20. Placement within this range will be determined based on the successful candidate’s qualifications, skills, and experience.

Key Responsibilities

Provide exceptional service to Members and Non-Members in-person, by telephone and through scheduled appointments, assisting with general travel inquiries and booking needs.
Answer and support the Travel department phone queue, identifying customer needs and directing or completing requests as appropriate.
Facilitate bookings for air, hotel and car rental arrangements within North America.
Identify opportunities to cross-sell and promote additional products and services, including travel insurance
Process payments, deposits and refunds accurately and in accordance with TICO requirements and company policies.
Create accurate and timely travel invoices using booking information, supplier rates and payment details.
Review and verify travel bookings and invoices to ensure accuracy, consistency and completeness.
Cross-check online bookings to confirm payments have been processed correctly and invoices accurately reflect the original booking.
Complete invoicing for Travel Consultants and applicable suppliers/products, including Journeys Tours, Niagara Airbus, cruise excursions, car rentals, hotels and other eligible travel products.
Manage applicable booking changes, cancellations and rebooking requests.
Prepare and organize customer travel documentation, including itineraries, tickets, vouchers, insurance information and other required documents, ensuring materials are accurate and provided within required timelines.
Maintain current supplier, product, pricing and promotional information within applicable systems.
Provide administrative and operational support to Travel Consultants across CAA Niagara locations.
Maintain a high level of accuracy when completing reservations, invoicing, documentation and data entry.
Support department processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and the overall Member experience.
Work collaboratively with Travel Consultants, Journeys and other internal teams to ensure customer needs are handled efficiently and appropriately.
Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned on a permanent or temporary basis.

Please note that this list may not encompass all responsibilities, and other duties may be assigned on a permanent or temporary basis as needed.

Qualifications & Skills

Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport with customers.
Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Strong customer service and sales skills.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with frequent interruptions and changing priorities.
Strong administrative, computer and data-entry skills, proficient in MS Office.
Comfortable navigating multiple web-based systems, CRM platforms and travel booking systems.
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
Collaborative, adaptable and solutions-oriented approach.
Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a team environment.

Education & Experience

2+ years of customer service experience.
Post-secondary education in Travel & Tourism or a related field is considered an asset.
Previous travel agency or travel industry experience is considered an asset.
Demonstrated efficiency and accuracy in data entry and administrative work.

Must-Haves (BFOR)

Must be TICO Certified or able to obtain TICO Certification within the first three (3) months of employment.
Must maintain all required TICO and other applicable certifications throughout employment.

Working Conditions

Work within an office environment with frequent interruptions.
Frequent computer use, including typing and mouse use.
Ability to work at any CAA Niagara location as operationally required.
Flexibility to work varying hours, including days, evenings and weekends, as required.

What’s In It For You

100% employer-paid premiums for health, dental, vision, life, and travel insurance
Virtual healthcare and nurse navigation support
Defined Contribution Registered Pension Plan
Growth, training, and development opportunities
Give Where You Live program (community volunteer program)

Paid personal and vacation hours

Offer

title: Interior Design Sales Professional
description:
Named America's #1 Premium Furniture Retailer by Newsweek, Ethan Allen is a leading interior design destination combining state-of-the-art technology with personal service. After more than 90 profitable years in business, we still make about 75% of our custom-crafted products in our North American workshops and have an enduring reputation for quality and craftsmanship. In our global network of Design Centers, we offer complimentary interior design service and sell a full range of home furnishings, including custom furniture and artisan-crafted accents for every room in the home. General Objectives:
The Design Consultant works closely with the customer in the design center/studio, remotely, online or in the customer’s home to create individualized design solutions to sell Ethan Allen products and services. The designs include space planning, fabric coordination, product selection and overall project design. Successful execution is evidenced by developing individualized designs and achieving sales goals in a flexible relationship based selling environment. Some projects may require a team or partnership-based approach.
Design Consultants will be measured based on performance categories (teamwork, customer service, communication skills, decision making, project development, presentation, and technical skills) and benchmarks (Minimum Monthly Sales, Home Calls, Accent Sales, Softgood Sales, Be-Backs, PI, Close Ratio and Ethan Allen Trade Program) that contribute to the success of the Design Center as well as their own individual success. Must be skilled in the use of social media such as blogs, micro-blogs, on-line forum, content sharing web sites and other digital channels established for on-line interaction and connection to promote Ethan Allen’s brand as outlined in Ethan Allen’s Social Media Policy.
Design Consultants are compensated according to the Design Consultant Incentive Compensation Plan. Compensation is incentive based with total compensation determined by commissions earned. Design Consultants are expected to meet or exceed Minimum Monthly Sales and other benchmarks as determined by Ethan Allen.
This is a Full-Time position.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Create design solutions that are consistent with the customer’s preference and budget.
Sell Ethan Allen’s products and services.
Represent the Ethan Allen brand in all customer interactions. When in the design center professionally greet customers to establish rapport and obtain appointments and in-home consultations. Customarily and regularly make home calls to evaluate the customer’s needs and provide a total individualized design solution that closes the sale.
Utilize grassroots marketing and a variety of social media platforms to develop and grow the business.
Educate customers about the complimentary design service Ethan Allen provides, offering as little or as much design service as a customer desires.
Stay current on design and color trends to create fashionable design solutions.
Coordinate with the team to provide exceptional service to customers, before and after the sale, by promptly keeping customers informed of their order status including any delays.
Participate as required in all corporate sponsored marketing and training programs.
Educate customers on all the Ethan Allen sponsored finance options available to them.
Contribute towards the development and on-going upkeep of the design center’s portfolio.
Utilize corporate systems and technology to maximize efficiency in designing projects, creating presentations, and providing professional service for the design team’s customers.
Enter orders utilizing the retail point of sale system.
Work cooperatively in maintaining a neat and orderly design center projection.
Work with the Design Center Leader/Design Sales Leader and Design Consultants to develop business plans and grass roots marketing plans to further our market reach and exceed written goals; monitor effectiveness of the plans. Provide suggestions to modify plan based on reaching specific goals and objectives.
Utilize all technology, such as 3-D Room Planner, CRM, Live Chat, etc. to build volume of projects and productive relationships with prospective and current clients.
Utilize appropriate social media (i.e., Facebook, Instagram, etc.) to heighten own presence as well as Ethan Allen’s presence. Continually build relationships with outside talent via social media, such as LinkedIn, to build a network in the market.
Perform any other duties as required.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities:

Minimum High School Diploma or equivalent with relevant work experience.
Minimum of one (1) year of practical interior design experience.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a design-related field from an accredited institution, desirable.
Broad knowledge of interior design and effective sales techniques.
Working knowledge of online sales and design tools.
Good listening skills with excellent oral and written communication skills also required.
General understanding of how to utilize social media and grass-roots marketing to develop a book of business. Proven experience preferred.
Valid driver’s license, except in limited circumstances in which the associate can establish to the Company’s satisfaction that they have available, for use during all business hours, an alternate means of transportation not requiring the operation of a motor vehicle which will enable them to perform the duties of their position.
Intermediate skill competency using digital floor planning technology. 3D applications a plus.
Experience using interactive technology to view design concepts such as augmented reality, virtual reality and other visualization tools.
Willing and capable of learning new technologies.

Compensation
Our Design Consultants are paid a recoverable draw typically ranging from $59k to $70k annually based on written sales. The potential income for our experienced Design Consultants average $70,000-$115,000/year, with our top writers making $200,000 per year or more.
Benefits
Benefits are an important part of the total compensation that is offered, providing peace of mind and financial well-being. Ethan Allen is committed to offering a variety of benefits that allow associates to choose whether or not to participate based on personal and family needs. Some of the benefits offered are 401(k) plan (with Employer contributions), multiple Medical Plans with Prescription Drug Coverage, Health Savings Account (including Employer contributions), Dental Plan, Vision Plan, Basic Group Term Life & Accidental Death & Dismemberment, Supplemental Group Term Life & AD&D Insurance, Dependent Group Term Life Insurance, Short and Long-Term Disability, Business Travel Accident Life Insurance, Flexible Spending Accounts – Health Care & Dependent Care, Commuter Saving Plans – Public Transit & Parking, Voluntary Whole Life Insurance, Voluntary Critical Care Insurance, Voluntary Accident Insurance and Employee Assistance Program. Benefit availability varies based on employee classification.

title: Central Fill Inventory Technician
description:
About the company

Albertsons Companies is at the forefront of the revolution in retail. With a fixation on raising the bar with innovation and building belonging through our culture, our team is rallying our company around a unique purpose: to create joy around each table and inspire a healthier tomorrow for every community.

Albertsons Companies is one of the largest food and drug retailers in the United States, with over 2,200 stores in 34 states and the District of Columbia. Our well-known banners include Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Shaw's, Acme, Tom Thumb, Randalls, United Supermarkets, Pavilions, Star Market, Haggen, Carr’s, Kings Food Markets, and Balducci's Food Lovers Market. We support our stores with 22 distribution centers and 19 manufacturing plants.

Bring your flavor

Building the future of food and well-being starts with you. Join our team and bring your best self to the table.

What you will be doing

The Inventory Technician at the Central Fulfillment Center is responsible for working at the direction of the Group Supervisor and Central Fill Inventory Specialist with the appropriate procurement of pharmaceuticals, production supplies, and all other supply needs of the site. This includes receiving and reconciling orders, handling aging stock, minimizing out-of-stock, and helping to achieve the Inventory Team and the greater CF Team Goals.

The position will be based in Irving, TX. The shift arrangement is a morning to mid-day shift arrangement working Monday-Friday with occasional Sunday project work.

  • Monday through Thursday : 9:30AM to 6:00PM
    Friday : 7:00AM to 3:30PM

Main responsibilities

  • Place inventory orders with pharmaceutical wholesalers, 3rd Party suppliers, and follow up on shipments and deliveries, if requested.

  • Receive, reconcile, and document all such shipments, communicating with the vendor as needed, as well as inter-store transfers.

  • Maintains accurate inventory counts; maintains the accuracy of on-hand quantities including, but not limited to, pharmaceuticals, production line supplies, office supplies, etc.

  • Assist in developing and implementing new processes for improving efficiency and reducing costs within the supply chain function.

  • Participate in periodic Inventory Audit preparations.

  • Manages storage areas for cleanliness and order, ensuring that the stock is prepared for the next day, while considering ergonomics and efficiency.

  • Responsible for rotating stock and monitoring/managing aging products, including DSCSA. Manages out of stock issues to minimize production delays, while minimizing costs to carry.

  • Assists with appropriate reverse distribution, expired product handling, recalls and returns.

  • Assists in cross-training identified production personnel to help with inventory receiving and other inventory-specific projects.

  • Works as a within the licensure of a pharmacy technician if needed during production surges or inventory downtimes. See Pharmacy Technician job description for details.

  • Other duties as assigned concurrent with all applicable laws and regulations.

We believe the successful candidate has these qualifications and experience

  • Required:

  • Pharmacy Technician License in Texas.

  • Ability to preserve confidentiality of patient information.

  • Preferred:

  • A national Pharmacy Technician Certification.

  • Previous pharmacy inventory management experience in high-volume retail setting

  • Previous pharmacy technician experience within a retail setting.

  • Technical Experience:

  • Central Fulfillment Pharmacy Technician experience.

  • Prefers to work in a closed-door environment (no adjudication, customer interaction, phone work).

  • Previous supply chain or inventory control experience.

  • Good computer skills.

  • Good math skills.

Physical Requirements

  • Willing and able to stand/walk at least 8 hours with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Willing and able to perform tasks which include pushing, pulling, grasping, bending, stooping, rotating, reaching, and lifting/carrying up to 40 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Loading/unloading pallets with use of equipment including but not limited to, pallet jack, electric pallet jack.

  • Visual focus such as counting, observing, etc. is required consistently.

  • Performing repetitive tasks up to 100% of the time

Our 290,000 associates have a passion for great service and building lasting relationships with our customers. Through a companywide focus on innovation, we are continually enhancing our digital and product offerings, making it easy for customers to get what they need, wherever they are.

title: EWP Design Supervisor / Lead Designer - Indirect
description:
PURPOSE
Overseeing the work of the EWP design team, ensuring designs and layouts are accurate, cost effective, and completed on schedule. Coordinates work assignments, reviews and approves designs, supports customer and sales initiatives, manages optimization processes, and assists with inventory management activities related to Engineered Wood Products.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Oversees the work of employees utilizing EWP design software and related systems to perform engineering, layout, and design functions for floors.
Supervises daily workflow and design production to ensure timely completion of customer projects while maintaining quality and accuracy standards.
Reviews incoming orders and project specifications, estimates completion timelines, and assigns work to appropriate design personnel.
Reviews, approves, and verifies EWP layouts, calculations, design drawings, and material takeoffs prior to release for manufacturing or customer use.
Establishes pricing recommendations and supports sales teams in developing profitable and competitive engineered wood product solutions.
Assists designers and sales personnel in providing solutions that meet customer requirements for structural integrity, constructability, code compliance, and material efficiency.
Records, tracks, and analyzes design errors in accordance with company policy. Conducts training and review sessions with designers to identify root causes and implement corrective actions.
Performs EWP design and layout work as needed to support workload demands and customer requirements.
Reviews design office lead times and coordinates workload balancing with other designers and locations when necessary.
Communicates with contractors, architects, engineers, builders, and company sales representatives to obtain information required for accurate and timely project completion.
Administers new employee training and ongoing development programs to ensure proficiency with EWP products, software, company procedures, and industry standards.
Oversees and manages BC Connect Optimizer activities to maximize manufacturing efficiencies, improve material yield, reduce waste, and ensure optimized production output.
Coordinates inventory requirements with ICS, ensuring accurate inventory replenishment, stock availability, stocking lengths needed, and material planning to meet customer demand and production schedules.
Monitors inventory accuracy and assist with inventory control processes, including physical inventories, cycle count execution, discrepancy investigation, and corrective action implementation.
Partners with operations, purchasing, sales, and manufacturing teams to improve communication, workflow efficiency, inventory utilization, and customer service.
Provides technical support and expertise regarding EWP products, software applications, and design best practices.
Performs other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES
Supervises assigned employees including staff selection, onboarding, training, scheduling, performance management, coaching, and development. Plans, assigns, and directs work activities while fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, customer focus, and teamwork. Conducts performance reviews, addresses employee concerns, and supports career development initiatives.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Associate degree in Engineering Technology, Construction Management, Design Technology, or a related field; or equivalent experience.
Two (2) or more years of EWP design experience.
Previous supervisory or team leadership experience preferred.
Advanced proficiency in EWP design software.
Demonstrated knowledge of engineered wood products, floor systems, roof systems, and structural framing applications.
Equivalent combination of education, training, and experience will be considered.

COMPETENCIES

Extensive knowledge of EWP products, wood frame construction, and structural building systems.
Strong leadership, coaching, and team development skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Knowledge of optimization software and manufacturing efficiency principles.
Understanding of inventory management, cycle counting, and supply chain processes.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, truss layouts, and engineering documentation.
Strong customer service and relationship management skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, ERP systems, BC Connect, and design software platforms.
Ability to analyze data and make sound business decisions regarding pricing, inventory, efficiency, and resource allocation.

title: Specialty Care Coord Tech
description:
Why choose us?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.

Bring your flavor

Building the future of food and well-being starts with you. Join our team and bring your best self to the table.

What you will be doing

Our Riverview Office has an opening as Pharmacy Technician, Specialty Care. Our Specialty Care Technicians coordinate the care for patients that are starting and maintaining therapy on Specialty Pharmaceutical (SP) products. Agents perform benefits investigations with third party payers and coordinate authorization for payment with the prescribing physician. Agents direct the purchasing and filling of SP products with Albertsons Safeway pharmacies and coordinate the administration of the product, connecting the patient and the pharmacy staff. The position will be based out of our Boise Corporate office.

Main responsibilities:

  • Benefits investigation -- determining coverage, facilitating prior authorization and communicating coverage to the patient.
  • Care Coordination -- facilitating the buy, bill and administration of SP products within the company pharmacies and company mail order.
  • Therapy Support (Specialty)- Tracking patients on SP products conducting refill reminders, therapy questionnaires and coordinating just in time ordering and pick-up in the company pharmacies and the company mail order.
  • Therapy Support (Pharmacy Care) -- Contacting patients and organizations to assure patients are completely protected with up-to-date immunization and marketing immunization services to organizations.

We are looking for candidates who possess the following:

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Certified Pharmacy Technician.

We believe the successful candidate has these qualifications and experience:

  • Two years' experience as a Pharmacy Technician
  • Preferred experience with Albertsons or Safeway Pharmacies
  • Experience in acquiring prior authorization from third party payers.
  • Problem solving abilities and attention to details.
  • Administration skills, such as planning and organizing, resource management and the ability to set priorities and coordinate work activities.
  • Customer relations skills including meeting customer needs and establishing a service environment. This involves the ability to identify requirements of internal and external customers, focus on achieving optimal results, and develop solutions that positively affect customer satisfaction.
  • Good computer skills including Microsoft Office
  • Preferred experience with PDX, EPS and Enterprise

Physical Environment

  • Most work is performed in a temperature-controlled office environment
  • Incumbent may sit for long periods of time at desk or computer terminal
  • Incumbent may use calculators, keyboards, telephone and other office equipment in the course of a normal workday.
  • Stooping, bending, twisting, and reaching may be required in completion of job duties

We also provide a variety of benefits including:

  • Competitive wages paid weekly
· Access to up to 50% of your earned wages before payday, via our partnership with Stream
  • Associate discounts
  • Health and financial well-being benefits for eligible associates (Medical, Dental, 401k and more!)
  • Time off (vacation, holidays, sick pay). For eligibility requirements please visit myACI Benefits
  • Leaders invested in your training, career growth and development
  • An inclusive work environment with talented colleagues who reflect the communities we serve

Our Values – Click below to view video: ACI Values

A copy of the full job description can be made available to you.

title: Porter - Residential
description:

title: Team Leader
description:
GENERAL JOB DESCRIPTION:
The Dispensing Team Leader is a proactive and results-driven leader responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the dispensing department. Working closely with the Color Manufacturing Supervisor, this role ensures production priorities are achieved, operational challenges are resolved promptly, and communication flows seamlessly between staff and management. The Team Leader provides hands-on direction, promotes a safe and productive work environment, and drives continuous improvement while maintaining quality standards.
DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES:

Ensure team compliance with company policies, procedures, and safety standards.
Identify production issues, correct where possible, and communicate promptly to Supervisors and the Color Manufacturing Manager.
Provide hands-on direction for all production activities and support staff in achieving daily goals.
Maintain production priorities as directed by Supervisors and administrative staff, following both verbal and written instructions.
Collaborate with staff to identify inefficiencies, training needs, and areas for procedural improvement.
Monitor daily production outputs, assess team capabilities, and make informed operational decisions.
Communicate production updates and challenges with Supervisors/Managers on a regular basis.
Work with higher management to resolve employee conflicts quickly and effectively.
Ensure all employees receive appropriate training, development, and guidance.
Attend and actively participate in daily huddles to align team goals and priorities.
Perform other departmental duties and support various positions as needed to maintain workflow.
Promote and implement continuous improvement initiatives through approved procedures and standards.

SKILLS REQUIRED:

Strong understanding of dispensing operations, production processes, and departmental workflows.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Ability to multitask and manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
General mechanical aptitude (asset).
Strong leadership skills with the ability to guide, train, and motivate employees.
Effective conflict resolution and team management capabilities.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Time management skills with a strong focus on efficiency and output.
Reliability, consistent attendance, and commitment to team success.

EDUCATION, TRAINING, and EXPERIENCE:

Minimum Grade 12 education or equivalent.
Previous experience in a dispensing, manufacturing, or production environment is preferred.
Experience or knowledge of continuous improvement methodologies and safety practices is an advantage.

Shift:

Monday to Friday - 6:30 am to 3:00 pm
Monday to Friday - 3:00 pm to 11:30 pm
Sunday to Thursday - 11:00 pm to 7:30 am

title: Junior Water and Wastewater Engineer
description:
R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited and Neegan Burnside Ltd. are seeking a highly motivated and collaborative Junior Water & Wastewater Engineer to join our Winnipeg office. This junior-level position, ideal for a recent graduate or early-career engineer with 1–3 years of experience, who enjoys solving practical infrastructure challenges and contributing to municipal projects from planning and design through construction. You will work with senior staff and project managers to deliver a variety of water and wastewater assignments across Manitoba and Northwestern Ontario, with opportunities to take on increasing responsibility in project coordination and client support.

What You’ll Do:

  • Support the planning, design, and delivery of municipal water and wastewater infrastructure projects (linear and vertical) under the guidance of intermediate and senior engineers.
  • Assist in the preparation of design calculations, drawings inputs, technical reports, specifications, and tender/construction contract documents.
  • Coordinate with engineering staff, technologists, and drafting teams to advance project deliverables.
  • Contribute to technical reports, proposals, schedules, and cost estimates.
  • Participate in field investigations, condition assessments, and data collection; compile and summarize findings for review by the project team.
  • Support construction-phase activities (shop drawing review, RFIs, site visits) under the supervision of the project team.
  • Communicate effectively within the project team and, with guidance, support client-facing interactions.
  • Build technical skills and professional competency through mentorship, training, and progressively increasing responsibility on project assignments.

What You Bring:

  • Engineer-in-Training (EIT) registered with Engineers Geoscientists Manitoba (EGM), or eligible for EIT registration; recent P.Eng. applicants also welcome.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of progressive experience (including co-op/internship) in consulting and/or other municipal water/wastewater design.
  • Foundational knowledge of or strong academic interest in municipal water and wastewater infrastructure, applicable standards, and design principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to assist in producing engineering deliverables including calculations, drawings inputs, and technical reports.
  • Strong organization and communication skills, with the ability to manage tasks and priorities under supervision.
  • Collaborative, team-oriented approach; eager to learn within a fast-paced, multi-project consulting environment.

    Preferred Skills and Assets:

    • Academic or practical exposure to water/wastewater infrastructure design (water treatment plants, lagoons, pumping stations, watermains, sewers, forcemains) or civil site servicing.
    • Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D, or related design software.
    • Experience with civil site servicing, grading, and site design.
    • Familiarity working with Indigenous clients and communities.
    • Enrolment in or completion of the EGM Engineer-in-Training (EIT) professional development program.

      Why Choose Burnside Group of Companies?

      As a R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited / Neegan Burnside Ltd. employee, you will become part of a supportive group of colleagues across the organization, that work together to provide value and service to our clients, while extending care to each other. We know that our employees are our greatest asset, and thus we strive to provide a positive work/life balance.

      Burnside has an over 50-year track record of building a great reputation both internally with their staff and externally with their clients, as an established leader in quality engineering, environmental, project management and consulting services.

      Becoming part of the Burnside team opens the door to a wide range of career development, advancement, mentorship and collaboration opportunities across our 12 office locations.

      We offer a wide variety of opportunities for our staff, geared to your comfort level in independence and interests. As an agile firm willing to consider a multitude of opportunities as presented by our long-term client base, and in a number of emerging disciplines, we are willing to work with you to set a meaningful career path for you.

      We offer:

      • A collaborative culture where friendship, honesty and respect are part of our core values and practices
      • Flexible working hours and office locations, including hybrid working opportunities
      • A competitive compensation and benefits package
      • RRSP company matching plan
      • Career growth and professional development opportunities
      • Potential for performance-driven bonusing
      • Active social committees
      • A welcoming, positive, and inclusive work environment

      We are an equal opportunity employer committed to valuing diversity in the workplace and we welcome resumes from all qualified candidates. Burnside will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the entire recruitment, assessment, and selection process, as required. If you are a person with a disability and require an accommodation during these processes, please contact our Human Resources department.

      RJ Burnside and Associates Limited and Neegan Burnside Ltd. Company Profiles

      Founded in 1970, R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited is a growing values-driven employee-owned multidiscipline Canadian engineering and environmental consulting firm with over 450 staff. Our consistent commitment to investing in technological advancements and training, in addition to encouraging and promoting professional development, has enabled our firm to meet our ongoing and stated goal of continual improvement.

      Founded in 1999, Neegan Burnside Ltd. is a majority-Indigenous owned firm committed to working with Indigenous (First Nation, Metis and Inuit) communities, agencies and industries to meet their infrastructure, development and economic goals while remaining sensitive to culture, values and beliefs. We have completed over 1,500 projects for more than 300 Indigenous communities and agencies throughout North America, many of them repeat clients with whom we work to develop long term and meaningful relationships. We endeavor to provide opportunities with our organization for Indigenous staff, as well as for community members in the projects we deliver.

      Our Companies are uniquely integrated, allowing us to coordinate and access resources across both firms. As a result, we offer our clients expertise in many technical disciplines including but not limited to water and wastewater, transportation planning and design, land development, stormwater management, bridges and culverts, building engineering and sciences, municipal drainage, municipal advisory services, environmental planning and ecology, hydrogeology, air and noise, asset management, solid waste, landscape architecture and well drilling & diagnostics.

      Together, we actively seek to develop relationships with a broad and diversified client base in the Public, Private and Indigenous sectors. We work on a variety of projects throughout Canada, with 11 office locations in Ontario and one in Manitoba.

      We look forward to considering you as a part of our team!

      #LI-HYBRID

title: Building Services Supervisor
description:
Building Services Supervisor
Full-Time | Non-Exempt | Eligible for Overtime | Pay: $33.00–$35.50/hour
Touchmark on West Prospect, Appleton’s leading full-service senior living community, is seeking an experienced Building Services Supervisor to join our team.
This is a hands-on working supervisor position for someone who brings strong maintenance experience along with the ability to lead, train, coach, and provide daily direction to others. You will work alongside the Building Services team while helping ensure our buildings, grounds, equipment, vehicles, and building systems remain safe, attractive, reliable, and well maintained.
The Building Services Supervisor reports to the Building Services Manager/Director and plays an important role in keeping daily operations organized, responsive, and focused on exceptional service to our residents.
What You’ll Do

Provide day-to-day leadership, work direction, training, and coaching to Building Services team members.
Help establish daily priorities, assign work, coordinate coverage, and follow up to ensure work is completed safely and to established standards.
Work alongside the team performing general maintenance and repairs involving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, flooring, equipment, and building systems.
Monitor and prioritize resident and community work orders and service requests.
Inspect completed work and community areas for quality, safety, cleanliness, and needed corrective action.
Coordinate and participate in preventative maintenance activities and inspections.
Assist with scheduling, onboarding, attendance follow-up, performance feedback, and other supervisory responsibilities.
Respond to urgent maintenance needs and participate in the department’s on-call rotation as assigned.
Assist with unit refurbishments, repairs, remodels, moves, seasonal projects, and other community projects.
Coordinate appropriately with contractors, vendors, other departments, residents, and families.
Help maintain accurate maintenance, inspection, preventative maintenance, and work-order records.
Reinforce safe work practices, department expectations, Touchmark Gold Standards, and our commitment to exceptional resident service.

What We’re Looking For

High school diploma or equivalent.
Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in general building, facilities, or maintenance work.
General industrial or commercial maintenance experience.
Previous experience providing work direction, training, coaching, or supervision to maintenance or facilities employees.
Strong working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, carpentry, painting, floor coverings, life safety systems, grounds maintenance, and general equipment repair.
Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
Ability to organize work, manage competing priorities, and provide effective direction during urgent situations.
Strong communication skills and a professional, service-oriented approach when working with residents, families, team members, vendors, and contractors.
Basic computer skills and experience with work-order or maintenance tracking systems.
Working knowledge of Outlook, Word, and Excel.
Valid driver’s license and ability to meet company driving requirements.
Ability to lift and carry up to 60 pounds and perform the physical requirements associated with building and grounds maintenance.

Preferred: Experience in senior living, health care, hospitality, or a similar community environment.
Why Touchmark?
At Touchmark, our Building Services team does much more than maintain buildings. Their work directly affects the comfort, safety, and quality of life of the residents who call our community home.
We are looking for a supervisor who takes pride in their work, enjoys solving problems, understands the importance of follow-through, and knows how to bring out the best in a team.
If you are an experienced maintenance professional ready to combine your technical skills with hands-on leadership, we invite you to apply and learn more about joining the team at Touchmark on West Prospect.

title: Assistant Product Manager
description:
About us:

Napa Home & Garden is a wholesale home décor brand headquartered in Norcross, GA, and one in a family of highly regarded brands under C&F Enterprises. We design and source seasonal collections — furniture, décor, botanicals, and lifestyle accessories — for style-conscious independent retailers, designers, and specialty stores across North America.

Job Purpose:

Napa Home & Garden is looking for an Assistant Product Manager who wants more than a foot in the door; someone who wants a real seat at the table while learning the full arc of merchandising, from trend to assortment to P&L. This is the first step on Napa's merchandising career path, built for someone who's analytical, design-curious, and ready to grow into a future Product Manager.

What You'll Own

  • Assortment & product execution. Maintain assortment line lists, product setup, and SKU data across 2–3 seasons at once; support development from concept through launch, tracking milestones, samples, and vendor communication.
  • Brand & Market audits. Support competitive audits, contribute to collection naming and feature storytelling for new product launches.
  • Analytics that drive decisions. Build weekly and monthly reporting on sales, margin, and inventory health, and flag trends before they become problems — using Excel, Power BI, and ERP tools.
  • Vendor & cross-functional coordination. Communicate daily with domestic and international vendors on POs, samples, and timelines; partner with Design, Supply, Sales, and Marketing to keep launches on track.
  • Growing into the role. Participate in line reviews, trade shows (Atlanta Market, High Point), and category business reviews. Napa wants Assistant Product Managers who ask good questions and push category performance forward.

Qualifications

  • 1-3 years in Buying, Merchandising, Retail or related analytical or commercial role
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Merchandising, Marketing, or a related field
  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort working with data
  • Sharp organizational skills. Ability to coordinate multiple seasons and deadlines.
  • Curiosity about home décor, design trends, and consumer behavior
  • Clear, confident written and verbal communication
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Merchandising, or related field, or equivalent career/internship experience.

Bonus points: ERP/PLM exposure, Power BI experience, or prior internship/early-career work supporting product or buyers/merchants.

Career Path: Assistant Product Manager → Product Manager → Senior Product Manager → Director of Product & Merchandising → VP, Product Merchandising & Management. This role is designed to build the foundation for that path.

Physical requirements

  • Sitting, Standing, Walking
  • Prolonged use of computer involved; use of hands and finger coordination; specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision. Color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus as needed.
  • Twice a year during Market periods, standing and walking for 8-12 hours each day

Benefits:

  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Employee assistance program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Health savings account
  • 401(k) and 401(k) matching
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Voluntary Life Insurance
  • Voluntary Short-Term Disability
  • Paid time off

This is a hybrid role based at our Norcross, GA headquarters. Candidates should expect to be in the office up to 3 days a week. Extended hours and select weekends during peak season, showroom prep and market (twice annually).

The successful candidate must be able to pass a pre-employment background check and drug screening.

All applicants are required to successfully complete a background check and drug screening as part of the pre-employment process. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and must not require sponsorship now or in the future.

title: 6A11 - Extrusion-roll - EXTC - EXTRUSION TECHNICIAN C
description:
TITLE: Extrusion Technician C

POSITION OBJECTIVE: Operate in a safe and efficient manner so as to be productive, while maintaining high quality product with strict deadlines

QUALIFICATIONS:

Good oral and written communication skills

Mechanical Aptitude

Ensure consistent, dependable attendance and demonstrate a willingness to accommodate non-standard work hours as necessary

Capable of effectively managing job-related stress and fostering productive workplace interactions

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Perform routine operations required to set up, operate and adjust multiple polyethylene blown film extrusion lines with conveying and winding equipment to produce integral zipper plastic tubing.
Work from prescribed production goals and standards, schedules, manuals, detailed specifications, consultations with bag department, shift leadership, maintenance, purchasing and others.
Ensure the availability of raw materials and other requirements and requisition needed items.
Work with shift supervisor and team members to establish team production, scrap and quality goals and ensure completion.
Perform simple calculations for daily production totals and quality results.
Maintain necessary production, quality and equipment records.

WORK ENVIRONMENT CONDITIONS SUBJECTED TO IN THIS POSITION:

Subject to extreme heat, temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour
Subject to loud noises
Hazards, such as moving machinery, electrical currents, debris, chemicals, gases

TRAINING:

Safety in the Workplace Rules and Regulations.
cGMP's and SOP's.

PHYSICAL ACTIVITY REQUIRED FOR THIS POSITION:

Stooping/Bending
Kneeling
Reaching
Standing for long periods of time
Grasping
Getting on/off forklift

title: Manufacturing Assistant Lead Hand – Shipping, Receiving & Inventory Control
description:
Manufacturing Assistant Lead Hand – Shipping, Receiving
The Assistant Lead Hand – Shipping, Receiving & Inventory Control supports daily material movement within a manufacturing environment. This role coordinates shipping, receiving, and inventory control activities that directly support production flow, on-time order fulfillment, and accuracy of raw materials, WIP, and finished goods. The Assistant Lead Hand provides floor-level leadership, trains employees, and ensures compliance with safety, quality, and manufacturing standards.
Shift: Monday to Thursday (7:00 Am to 4:00 Pm, Friday 7:00 Am to 1:00 Pm)
Pay Rate: Between $25.31 to $27.31
The successful candidate's responsibilities will include:
Shipping

Plan and stage outbound orders based on production schedules ; verify pick accuracy and packaging standards.
Create shipping documents (BOL, packing lists, courier labels) and coordinate carrier pickups.
Ensure shipments meet customer requirements and on-time dispatch targets.
Conduct final quality checks; address discrepancies before release.

Receiving

Receive and inspect incoming sheet metal, steel coils, fabricated parts, and raw materials.
Identify damages or shortages; work with Purchasing/Production to resolve.
Direct put-away to proper locations; maintain 5S in receiving areas.
Update system transactions promptly to maintain inventory accuracy.

Inventory Control

Lead daily cycle counts and investigate variances; implement corrective actions.
Maintain bin/location integrity; support stock rotation (FIFO) and lot/serial tracking.
Monitor min/max levels; flag replenishment needs and slow-moving/obsolete items.
Prepare routine inventory reports for operations leadership.

Leadership & Coordination

Assign and follow up on tasks; balance workloads across the team.
Train employees on SOPs, safety, and equipment; reinforce standard work.
Promote a safe workplace; conduct hazard observations and support incident reporting.
Act as point of contact for cross-functional stakeholders (Production, Purchasing, Quality).
Escalate equipment, quality, and schedule risks to the Supervisor/Manager.

The ideal candidate for this position will have:

High school or college diploma
2–4 years of experience in a manufacturing environment supporting shipping, receiving, or inventory control is a must.
Experience handling sheet metal, steel coils, or heavy industrial materials is required.
Prior lead hand or team coordination experience in a manufacturing/warehouse environment.
Comfort with ERP/WMS transactions (e.g., receipts, picks, transfers, cycle counts).
Comfortable with Microsoft Excel and basic data entry/reporting.
Strong attention to detail; able to investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies.
Solid communication skills and ability to coach.
Valid forklift license/certification; experience with counterbalance and/or reach truck would be an asset.
Frequent standing, walking, and lifting up to 50 lbs; use of forklifts/pallet jacks.

Artificial Intelligence may be used to assist with screening applications for this position.

title: Hagerstown Walmart - MH II
description:
Lifetime Brands is looking for machine operators to work in our brand new Distribution Center located in Hagerstown, MD. Be part of this exciting new operation by working with the Maintenance Manager in labeling the new racking system in our state of the art facility.
For the first few months, the primary focus will be on making certain that the distribution center is ready to receive our products. This will entail using a scissor lift to label racks in the newly built space while being up to a maximum of 35 feet off the ground. Once the distribution center is operational, your job responsibilities will be as follows:
Overview:
A Material Handler II operates various light industrial vehicles and/or RF devices to perform material handling assignments such as picking bulk orders, loading/unloading, and shipping/receiving of merchandise.
Essential Job Functions

Operate powered light industrial trucks to move product to and from designated areas in the warehouse

Follow daily procedures & protocols as set forth in job orientations and training.

Review orders and place them within the appropriate areas as directed by the vehicle mounted computer manifest.

Must be able to operate a scissor lift at a height of 35 feet above the group to label racks.

Conduct preventative maintenance checks before each use and complete the inspection card.

Perform general housekeeping duties i.e. removal of empty skids and stacking thereof in designated areas.

At the end of each shift return the equipment to the correct charging station and prepare for daily overnight charge.

Follow all safety regulations required by OSHA and Company.

Other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Education: High School or equivalent

Experience: 1 -4 years experience operating Light Industrial equipment.

Specialized Knowledge, Licenses, etc.: Certification on: Electric Jack, sit-down forklift, and/or Order Picker and/or Reach. Experience with WMS a plus.

Working Conditions: Distribution Center. Ability to stand, walk, stoop, bend, reach, pull and push for extended periods. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs.

Other Skills/Abilities: Ability to satisfactorily complete Equipment driving training program. Must be able to listen and communicate effectively and have the ability to follow specific instructions. Ability to work independently and to carry out assignments to completion within parameters of instructions given.

title: Investigator 1/2/3 (PCN 073064)
description:
Job Description

ATTENTION ALASKA RESIDENTS!

The Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Division of Workers Compensation, is recruiting for an
Investigator 1/2/3 located in Anchorage!
No Cover Letter Required!



This position is in the General Government Unit (GGU) at a Range 14/16/18.


What You Will Be Doing:
This position is flexibly staffed and may be filled at the Investigator 1, Investigator 2, or Investigator 3 level, depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience. Work progresses from routine investigations performed with close supervision at the Investigator 1 level, to independent journey-level work at Investigator 2, and to unusual, difficult, or exceptionally complex investigations at Investigator 3.
  • Investigate reports of employers operating without required workers’ compensation insurance and allegations of workers’ compensation fraud using interviews, records research, databases, and field work.
  • Analyze payroll, insurance, employment, business, financial, medical, and other records to determine compliance, identify violations, and develop evidence.
  • Prepare investigative reports, petitions, discovery requests, subpoenas, hearing materials, exhibits, and other documentation, and provide factual testimony regarding investigations personally conducted.
  • Work with employers, employees, witnesses, insurers, attorneys, and Local, State, and Federal partners to obtain information, coordinate investigative activity, and support appropriate enforcement action.

Our Mission, Values, and Culture:
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) enforces compliance with the Alaska Workers’ Compensation Act through thorough and fair fraud investigations, accountability for violations, and proactive public education intended to prevent uninsured injuries. SIU values integrity, respect, dedication and commitment, accountability, and a collaborative team environment. This position directly supports the Division’s responsibility to promote compliance and protect Alaska workers and employers.

Benefits of Joining Our Team:
This position offers meaningful public-service work with varied investigative assignments and direct opportunities to improve compliance with Alaska’s workers’ compensation laws. The flex structure provides a defined career path from the entry-level Investigator 1 through the journey-level Investigator 2 and advanced Investigator 3. New investigators receive structured on-the-job training, coaching from experienced investigators, and progressive assignments designed to build investigative, analytical, legal, interviewing, and case-presentation skills. SIU works collaboratively and shares information and expertise across the team to support consistent, fair, and effective investigations.

The Working Environment You Can Expect:
This position is based in the Division of Workers’ Compensation office in midtown Anchorage and combines office-based research and case preparation with field work such as interviews, site visits, service of documents, and other investigative activity. The position requires local driving and occasional statewide travel, which may include remote locations, inclement weather, and travel by small aircraft or boat when necessary.

Who We Are Looking For:
We are interested in candidates who possess some or all of the following position specific competencies:
  • Manages and Organizes Information: Identifies a need; gathers, organizes, and maintains information; determines its importance and accuracy, and communicates it by a variety of methods.
  • Self-Management: Sets well-defined and realistic personal goals; displays a high level of initiative, effort, and commitment towards completing assignments in a timely manner; works with minimal supervision; is motivated to achieve; demonstrates responsible behavior.
