title: Assistant Site Superintendent
description:
The Assistant Site Superintendent supports the Site Superintendent in managing daily construction activities and ensuring projects run smoothly. They help coordinate subcontractors, monitor progress, and address any site challenges to keep work on schedule. This role also involves maintaining quality standards, ensuring compliance with regulations, and assisting with inspections. By managing resources and communicating with project teams, they contribute to the overall efficiency of the construction process. With strong organizational and problem-solving skills, the Assistant Site Superintendent plays a key role in delivering successful homebuilding projects. We are looking for journeyman tradespeople to fill our assistant site sup role.

Key Responsibilities:

Site Coordination & Trade Management

  • Provide support to the Site Superintendent for day-to-day operations of the site and projects.
  • Identify and resolve trade performance issues and other challenges affecting project timelines, escalating concerns as necessary.
  • Synchronize activities between trades and subcontractors, preventing scheduling conflicts and workflow disruptions.
  • Ensure that debris, tools, and materials are properly stored at the end of each workday to maintain a safe and organized job site.

Quality Control & Inspections

  • Verify that materials, tools, and plans are ready before starting tasks to ensure compliance and efficiency and that teams have access to shared tools and materials.
  • Conduct routine inspections during construction to identify and correct issues early, preventing delays.
  • Review completed work to confirm quality standards are met, ensuring zero missing items at the Pre-Possession Inspection (PPI) stage with a maximum of 6 deficiencies per unit for FSO, and per building for TH.
  • Record and document inspection results, noting any deficiencies and implementing corrective actions as needed.
  • Walk all units 3 times per week to ensure compliance with local building codes, safety regulations, and environmental guidelines.

Compliance & Safety Assurance

  • Compare on-site work to project drawings and specifications, identifying and addressing discrepancies.
  • Confirm compliance with local building codes, safety regulations, and industry standards to avoid violations.
  • Assign and oversee corrective actions to resolve deficiencies, ensuring all subcontractors complete necessary repairs.
  • Coordinate with inspectors to secure occupancy permits and certifications, verifying the proper installation of HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems.

Resource & Budget Management

  • Track daily expenses, including labor, materials, and equipment usage, ensuring adherence to budget expectations.
  • Optimize on-site labor and material usage to minimize waste, prevent over-ordering, and control costs.
  • Coordinate with procurement teams to schedule timely material deliveries without overstocking or delaying tasks.

Project Communication & Reporting

  • Provide regular updates to construction and project managers regarding budget status, quality concerns, and potential risks.
  • Attend weekly construction meetings to discuss progress, resolve issues, and ensure alignment across teams.
  • Ensure teams have access to necessary tools and materials at the start of each workday to prevent delays.
  • Document and share weekly project updates with relevant stakeholders to maintain transparency and accountability.

Annual Expectations & Performance Goals:

  • Project Timeliness & Coordination: Ensure that all scheduled tasks are completed on time, maintaining adherence to project timelines and preventing delays. Achieve a 95% on-time completion rate for trades and subcontractors.
  • Quality Assurance & Compliance: Ensure that 100% of work meets quality standards, with zero missing items identified during Pre-Possession Inspections. Maintain 100% compliance with safety and building codes, with no major violations reported.
  • Site Organization & Safety: Maintain a 100% organized and safe job site, with no safety incidents or accidents reported. Ensure that debris, tools, and materials are cleared at the end of each workday, contributing to an organized work environment.

Accountabilities:

  • Site Coordination & Trade Management: Effectively manage trade activities, identify and resolve performance issues.
  • Quality Control & Inspections: Ensure high-quality work standards are met and defects are addressed promptly.
  • Compliance & Safety Assurance: Ensure the site adheres to regulations, and safety protocols are enforced.
  • Resource & Budget Management: Maintain project costs and resource use within expectations.
  • Project Communication & Reporting: Provide timely and accurate project updates and communication.

title: Installer I
description:
Now Hiring: Installer
Location: Idaho Falls, ID Millwork
Build Your Career with Builder's FirstSource
At Builder's FirstSource, our Installers play a vital role in bringing projects to life. From installing doors and windows to cabinetry, millwork, stairs, and insulation, you'll help ensure every project is completed safely, accurately, and to the highest quality standards. If you enjoy hands-on work, take pride in craftsmanship, and want to be part of a team that builds the places people live and work, we'd love to hear from you.
Position Summary
The Installer is responsible for the professional installation of building materials and products in residential and commercial construction projects. This role requires attention to detail, a commitment to safety, and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced construction environment. Installers work both independently and as part of a team to ensure projects are completed on time and according to company standards, building codes, and customer expectations.
Key Responsibilities

Load, unload, and transport materials, tools, and equipment to and from job sites.
Install products such as insulation, doors, windows, stairs, cabinets, sinks, millwork, and other building materials.
Measure, cut, and prepare materials to required specifications.
Verify the accuracy, alignment, and trueness of structures and installations.
Follow all applicable building codes, industry standards, and company policies.
Maintain a strong commitment to job site safety by adhering to OSHA regulations and company safety procedures.
Properly use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, steel-toe boots, fall protection equipment, and other safety gear.
Operate company vehicles as assigned to transport materials and equipment.
Communicate effectively with team members, supervisors, and customers to ensure successful project completion.
Perform additional duties and support project needs as assigned.

What We're Looking For

Previous construction, installation, carpentry, or related experience is preferred but not required.
Ability to safely operate tools and equipment used in the installation process.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
Ability to follow instructions and work effectively as part of a team.
Dependable work ethic and commitment to maintaining a safe work environment.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record in accordance with company policy.

Minimum Qualifications

Less than high school education, or
Up to one month of related experience or training, or
An equivalent combination of education and experience.
Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license and acceptable motor vehicle record (MVR).

Physical Requirements

Frequent standing, walking, reaching, lifting, and use of hands and arms.
Regular climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and crawling.
Routinely lift and carry up to 50 pounds; occasionally lift up to 100 pounds.
Ability to work in various weather conditions and outdoor environments.
Ability to work at heights when necessary.
Visual abilities include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.

Work Environment

Primarily works on residential and commercial construction job sites.
Regular exposure to outdoor weather conditions.
Occasional exposure to heights, fumes, airborne particles, and other construction-related conditions.
Moderate noise levels are typical.

Why Join Builder's FirstSource?
At Builder's FirstSource, you'll have the opportunity to build a rewarding career with an industry leader. We invest in our people by providing a safety-first culture, opportunities for growth and development, competitive benefits, and the chance to work alongside experienced professionals who take pride in quality craftsmanship.
Build what matters. Build your future with Builder's FirstSource.

title: Director of Finance
description:
Happy Corner Hospitality is a collective consisting of Motek, a Mediterranean concept restaurant, Sesame Bakery, and Yalla Motek. We pride ourselves on delivering exceptional service and culinary experiences to our valued guests. Our commitment to excellence extends to every aspect of our operations, and we're currently seeking passionate, highly motivated, experienced professionals to join our corporate team.


Position Overview


The Director of Finance will serve as a key strategic leader, responsible for overseeing the financial health and performance of a rapidly growing multi-unit hospitality group. This role will lead financial planning and analysis, accounting oversight, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, and financial reporting across multiple venues. title: Intake Worker
description:
Program: Homebase Service Area 7 | 1860 East Tremont Avenue, Bronx, NY 10460
What You’ll Do
As part of New York City’s plan to end homelessness, the Department of Homeless Services established Homebase Homeless Prevention Community Resource Centers throughout New York City. Homebase programs are designed to assist families and individuals who are homeless or at imminent risk for becoming homeless to develop a plan for long-term housing stability. Homebase helps clients navigate the complicated eviction process, offers financial and money management counseling, helps clients obtain public benefits, provides short-term financial assistance, and helps with relocation if necessary.
As Intake Worker, you’ll assess all new clients for program eligibility, answer and respond to inquiry calls, and provide program information to new and prospective clients. You’ll also collect, review, and process eligibility documentation for new clients. The Homebase program is a fast-paced environment and requires a close attention to details.
Your responsibilities will include:

Providing a clear and concise explanation of Homebase services to clients and collecting and reviewing initial documentation to determine clients’ program eligibility.

Verifying the presented housing crisis via housing court stipulations, rent demands, subsidy information, etc.

Assisting clients with completion of all intake forms, completing the initial intake service plan, and entering intake information into the database.

Referring clients to external agencies and organizations for financial assistance, legal services, and public assistance benefits as appropriate.

Referring clients to financial, housing, and housing court workshops.

Participating in program outreach by conducting presentations on the Homebase program at various community-based organizations.

Establishing and maintaining relationships with internal and external agencies to assist clients with their housing crises.

Preparing regular reports as required by regulatory agencies and ensuring that all client records comply with regulatory policies and procedures.

You’re a great fit for this role if you have:

High School Diploma or equivalent OR equivalent experience and skills.

Prior experience in case management, assessment counseling, and crisis intervention with excellent interviewing skills.

Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Ability to work in a fast-paced, demanding environment.

Resourceful and detail oriented, with strong decision making and organizational skills

Computer literacy, particularly with Microsoft Office applications.

Valid US driver’s license a plus.

title: MES Engineer
description:
_Are you passionate about Information (IT) and Automation Technology (OT) and aspiring to make a meaningful impact? Are you curious to shape a digital manufacturing architecture, ready to advance competitiveness on the market?_ This role could be for you!

We Make Medicines!

Behind every product sold by Roche is Pharma Global Technical Operations (PT). Starting with Phase I of the development process and continuing through to product maturity, PT makes lifesaving medicines at 11 locations, with the support of partners from around the world. Information (IT) and Automation Technology (OT) teams are key in producing and delivering medicine to patients. The organization is currently undergoing a transformation towards digitalization, advancing fundamental elements to meet future needs, such as using new technologies.

**The Opportunity**

This position, based in Genentech's Hillsboro, Oregon facility, provides the opportunity to have a key role in a highly automated pharmaceutical drug substance facility. The site employs highly integrated computer control systems to manage plant operations and manufacturing data.

The IT OT Team in Hillsboro is supporting Hillsboro Technical Operations (HTO) which is the commercial Make Assess and Release (MAR) and launch site for North America, and Hillsboro Innovative Therapies (HIT) which is transitioning into a multi-product facility for development, clinical and commercial supply capabilities for individualized and cell therapies.

As part of the Hillsboro IT OT team, you will report to the Manufacturing Systems Development Lead to support the Manufacturing Execution System  (MES) as a Recipe Author, designing, building, validating, and troubleshooting MES recipes in support  Make/Assess/Release in a 24x7 Goods Manufacturing Practice (GMP) environment. As part of the Site Team and larger Global IT OT organization, you will also be expected to contribute to Manufacturing Operations Management initiatives and optimization/standardization of the global IT OT landscape.

Responsibilities:

- Manufacturing Execution System (MES) Rockwell (PharmaSuite) recipe authoring and software development

- Troubleshooting plant floor MES execution and business system integration issues

- Compliance with corporate and site business processes, valid design principles, and quality procedures

- Qualification test plan development/review/approval and execution

- Implementing production tech transfer requirements into automation IT systems

- Contribute to the development of solutions for reporting, production and operational analysis tools, recipe procedural enhancements, batch review/release, equipment automation integration, and business system integration

- Present system and electronic batch record process to health authorities

- Contributing to development of supply chain network MES standards and best practices

- Provide Consulting with Business Process owners in the Value Streams

- Contribute with MES Recipe Authoring knowledge to Projects/Squads for MES Projects, process improvement initiatives or support

- Participate in an after hours on-call support rotation

- Document system changes and incidents in ServiceNow

- Own and manage Change records and Deviation in Veeva Quality System


**Who You Are**

- A BS/MS in Chemical, Electrical, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent

- A minimum of 2-4 years of relevant experience

- MES Recipe Authoring experience preferred

- Project management skills

- Ability to multi-task while handling routine and impromptu assignments with minimal supervision

- Must be able to plan and perform testing, including documenting test conditions, expected results, and test validation

- Must be comfortable working under pressure, delivering quality results with schedule deadlines and have a proven track record in meeting schedule for tasks while still meeting or exceeding business requirements and goals

- Work autonomously  direct with Engineering and Value Streams

- Work with Global Recipe Authors Team on common templates for Rockwell PharmaSuite MES

- Job duties include after hours on call support at least one week a month


The expected salary range for this position based on the primary location of Oregon is $78,900 - $176,800.  Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law.  A discretionary annual bonus may be available based on individual and Company performance.  This position also qualifies for the benefits detailed at the link provided below.

[_**Benefits**_](https://roche.ehr.com/default.ashx?CLASSNAME=splash)

It is our policy and practice to employ, promote, and otherwise treat any and all employees and applicants on the basis of merit, qualifications, and competence. title: Filler Operator - 3rd Shift
company: Maryland & Virginia Milk Producers Cooperative Association
description:
SHIFT: 3rd

HOURS: 8:00pm-4:30am.. Must be able to work overtime, weekends and holidays.

HOURLY PAY= $21.00 PER HOUR

Why you will love working at Maola®:

  • Built on over a century of dedication, Maola is always looking ahead—investing in our people, strengthening our communities, and securing fresh, local dairy for the future.
  • Join a farmer-owned cooperative rooted in integrity, sustainability, and a passion for providing fresh, high-quality Maola dairy products.
  • We prioritize your well-being with competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package, including Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with employer match, Life Insurance, paid time off, and more—available within your first month.
  • Our employees are an integral part of who we are — what you do and what you think matters.

SUMMARY

Tends machines that perform one or more packaging functions, such as filling, marking, labeling. Starts machine and observes operation to detect malfunctions. Stops machine and reports malfunction to supervisor. Various machines involved in this operation such as the 30 Valve filler; Quart filler; Nep filler; Bulk filler; 18 Valve plastic filler; and the 1/2 Gallon paper filler.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Tends machine that fill pasteurized products into containers.
  • Examines containers from all lines for seals, labels, weights, dates, and valves.
  • Seals are to be checked top and bottom for stains and valves are to be checked for excess leakage.
  • Review with the lab for approvals of each product change on each machine.
  • Observes flow of milk into machine and remove defective containers.
  • Notifies foreman of machine malfunction.
  • Place containers on machine and adjust machines of various sizes.
  • Records information in 15 minutes intervals for weight, date, and label.
  • Follow all safety and food quality standards.
  • Perform organoleptic testing (e.g. sensory testing with taste, smell, touch, and sight) on finished product.
  • Other duties may be assigned. .

BASIC REQUIREMENTS

  • High school diploma, General Education Degree (GED), or International Education Equivalent.
  • Related experience preferred.
  • Manufacturing experience preferred.

COMPETENCIES

  • Communication
    • Communicate clearly and effectively through multiple channels – oral, written, visual, and non-verbal – ensuring our messages are understood and delivered appropriately, whether in-person or digitally.
  • Accountability
    • Take responsibility for actions and anticipate challenges before they arise.
    • Solve problems both within and outside of departments, proactively addressing issues as they occur.
  • Customer Focused
    • Prioritize understanding and meeting both internal and external customer needs.
    • Ensure high levels of satisfaction and loyalty by anticipating customer requirements and striving for exceptional service.
  • Initiative
    • Proactive in identifying opportunities and addressing potential threats.
    • Act independently and decisively, rather than waiting for situations to demand action.
  • Problem-Solving
    • Possess the ability to identify and address complex issues with minimal guidance.
    • Skilled at analyzing challenges and finding practical, effective solutions.
  • Collaboration
    • Take responsibility for deliverables while also supporting others to ensure that collective goals are met.
    • Able to work harmoniously with others toward a common goal, recognizing and valuing each person’s contributions, is fundamental to successful collaboration.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand and walk. The employee must be able to reach, bend, extend, and lift 50-60 pounds. It also requires reaching and handling dairy products and pushing and pulling stacks of products weighing up to 200lbs.

The employee is frequently required to perform organoleptic assessments. This requires the acute physical ability to taste, smell, see, and feel product samples to detect deviations in flavor, aroma, color, and texture.

The employee must be physically able to consume and evaluate a wide variety of food ingredients, including potential allergens (e.g., diary, wheat, soy, nuts) processed in the facility.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • The work environment may require working in the cooler room with varying degrees of temperature and may include contact with water or dairy liquids.
  • Exposed to a noise level of 90 decibels. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate/high. Wet/slippery work conditions.

Maola Local Dairies® is a farmer-owned cooperative committed to its local farm families and to producing high-quality, nutritious dairy products. Founded in 1920, Maola processes and delivers your favorite milk, cream, and dairy products to families, schools, and communities while investing in quality, innovation, and sustainability across its farms and supply chain. Learn more at www.maolamilk.com.

title: Track & Field Sprint Coach
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Harlem Children’s Zone (HCZ)—a world-renowned education and poverty-fighting organization based in New York—seeks an enthusiastic, dedicated, and mission-aligned Track & Field Sprint Coach.

The Track & Field Sprint Coach will bring a strong commitment to Harlem Children’s Zone’s mission of breaking the cycle of intergenerational poverty through comprehensive, on-the-ground programming that creates opportunities for children and families to thrive in school, work, and life.

We are seeking an experienced Track & Field Sprint Coach to lead and develop scholar-athletes competing in sprint and related events across our elementary, middle, and high school programs. The Sprint Coach will be responsible for providing high-quality instruction, developing scholar-athletes’ technical, physical, tactical, and mental skills, preparing athletes for competition, and strengthening the overall Track & Field program.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a passion for HCZ’s mission, an understanding of and respect for the Harlem community, and experience working with youth in a school-based or community-based setting. The successful candidate will use athletics as a platform to promote academic achievement, leadership, accountability, teamwork, discipline, resilience, and personal growth.

For more information, check out Want to Work at Harlem Children's Zone? Here's 7 Things You Need to Know.

Requirements

• High school diploma or GED required, bachelor’s degree preferred.

• At least three years of experience coaching track and field, sprinting, hurdles, or a related speed-based discipline, preferably at the middle school, high school, collegiate, club, or elite competitive level.

• Demonstrated experience developing and coaching competitive sprint and/or hurdle athletes.

• Strong knowledge of track and field rules, regulations, sprint mechanics, starting techniques, acceleration, maximum velocity, speed development, conditioning, race strategy, relay development, and athlete performance.

• Demonstrated ability to design and implement progressive training programs appropriate for youth and adolescent athletes.

• Experience coaching and supporting youth and adolescent populations.

• Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, mentor, and retain scholar-athletes.

• Commitment to the mission, values, and programs of Harlem Children’s Zone.

• Strong leadership, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, and meet established deadlines.

• A positive, enthusiastic, collaborative, flexible, and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Ability to work effectively with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, HCZ colleagues, community organizations, and external partners.

• CPR and First Aid certification, or the ability to obtain certification within the required timeframe.

• Ability to travel to away meets, invitationals, tournaments, championships, and other athletic events.

• Ability to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours as required by the athletic schedule.

Who You Are

The Track & Field Sprint Coach is responsible for the development and performance of scholar-athletes competing in sprint and related events while contributing to the overall success and culture of the HCZ Track & Field program.

The Sprint Coach will design and implement age-appropriate training plans, lead practices, prepare athletes for competition, evaluate performance, and provide individualized coaching and feedback. The coach will work closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leadership, and other coaching staff to ensure consistency in training, expectations, athlete development, and program operations.

The successful candidate understands that coaching extends beyond athletic performance. They will serve as a mentor and role model who promotes academic accountability, positive behavior, leadership, teamwork, discipline, resilience, and long-term scholar development.

The Sprint Coach must understand the importance of developing speed and power progressively and safely. They should be able to balance competitive expectations with appropriate training loads, recovery, strength development, injury prevention, and the individual needs of developing athletes.

What You’ll Do

Sprint Program Leadership and Training

• In collaboration with the Head Track & Field Coach and Athletic Leadership, develop and implement a comprehensive sprint-development program for elementary, middle, and high school scholar-athletes.

• Design and implement age-appropriate, progressive training plans that develop acceleration, maximum velocity, speed endurance, strength, power, mobility, running mechanics, and overall athletic performance.

• Lead daily practices and sprint-specific training sessions in accordance with the overall Track & Field program schedule.

• Develop individualized training plans based on athlete ability, experience, event specialization, competition schedule, and developmental needs.

• Prepare scholar-athletes for sprint and related events, including the 60m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 4x100m, 4x400m, hurdles, and other applicable events.

• Teach proper sprint mechanics, posture, arm action, stride mechanics, block starts, acceleration technique, transition to maximum velocity, pacing, and race execution.

• Develop and implement appropriate drills and progressions to improve starts, acceleration, top-end speed, speed endurance, and sprint performance.

• Develop scholar-athletes’ ability to execute effective race strategies based on event, athlete strengths, competition level, and meet conditions.

• Incorporate appropriate strength, power, mobility, flexibility, conditioning, and injury-prevention strategies into sprint training.

• Collaborate with Strength & Conditioning staff, Athletic Trainers, medical personnel, and other coaches when appropriate to support athlete health and performance.

• Evaluate athlete performance through practices, competitions, time trials, testing, video analysis, and other appropriate measures.

• Use performance data to establish goals and adjust training plans.

• Identify and develop scholar-athletes with potential to compete at higher levels of competition.

Competition and Meet Preparation

• Prepare scholar-athletes for league meets, invitationals, championships, tournaments, and other sanctioned athletic events.

• Develop individualized race strategies and competition plans based on event, athlete strengths, competition level, and meet conditions.

• Prepare athletes for efficient execution of starts, acceleration, race positioning, pacing, finishes, and event-specific strategies.

• Attend and actively coach assigned competitions and provide real-time instruction, support, and feedback.

• Maintain accurate records of athlete times, personal records, placements, qualifying standards, and other relevant performance data.

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with meet entries, athlete selection, event assignments, relay considerations, and competition logistics.

• Develop and evaluate relay teams and ensure athletes understand relay exchanges, positioning, communication, and race strategy.

• Promote sportsmanship, professionalism, accountability, and appropriate conduct before, during, and after competitions.

Scholar-Athlete Development and Accountability

• Recruit, evaluate, develop, and retain scholar-athletes interested in sprinting, hurdles, and related speed events.

• Provide individualized instruction and feedback to support each scholar-athlete’s athletic development.

• Create a positive, inclusive, disciplined, and high-performing training environment.

• Promote sportsmanship, teamwork, leadership, resilience, accountability, discipline, and respect.

• Establish and communicate clear expectations regarding attendance, participation, behavior, academic performance, training standards, and team responsibilities.

• Hold scholar-athletes accountable for meeting HCZ academic, school attendance, and after-school programming standards.

• Collaborate with school staff, CCLR, Zone site staff, families, and other HCZ colleagues to identify and support scholars experiencing academic, attendance, behavioral, or engagement challenges.

• Reinforce the expectation that academic responsibilities and required school or after-school programming take priority over athletic participation.

• Teach scholar-athletes the importance of goal setting, time management, discipline, consistency, recovery, responsible decision-making, and preparation.

• Recognize and celebrate academic achievement, leadership, positive behavior, personal growth, and athletic accomplishments.

Athlete Health, Safety, and Wellness

• Prioritize the health and safety of all scholar-athletes during practices and competitions.

• Implement appropriate warm-up, cool-down, mobility, recovery, hydration, and environmental safety practices.

• Monitor athletes for signs of excessive fatigue, overtraining, injury, dehydration, heat-related illness, or other health concerns.

• Follow all HCZ, school, league, and athletic safety policies and procedures.

• Immediately report injuries, incidents, behavioral concerns, and other relevant matters through established protocols.

• Collaborate with Athletic Trainers, school nurses, Strength & Conditioning staff, and other appropriate professionals regarding scholar-athlete health and readiness.

• Promote healthy training habits and educate scholar-athletes on the importance of recovery, nutrition, hydration, sleep, and injury prevention.

Program Operations

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with the day-to-day operation of the Track & Field program.

• Maintain accurate records related to athlete participation, attendance, performance, eligibility, competition results, and program outcomes.

• Support the management and maintenance of Track & Field equipment, uniforms, supplies, timing equipment, starting blocks, hurdles, and other program resources.

• Ensure equipment is properly maintained, stored, and returned following practices and competitions.

• Assist with scheduling practices, competitions, transportation, facilities, and other program logistics.

• Support the planning and execution of Track & Field events, clinics, showcases, camps, community events, and other program activities.

• Maintain a clean, organized, safe, and professional training environment.

• Provide timely updates regarding program needs, athlete concerns, equipment, facilities, competitions, and other operational matters.

Collaboration and Organizational Alignment

• Collaborate closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leaders, and other coaches to ensure program alignment.

• Support the implementation of HCZ policies, procedures, organizational initiatives, and strategic priorities.

• Participate in required meetings, professional development sessions, trainings, family engagement activities, and organizational events.

• Maintain consistent and professional communication with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, and external partners.

• Collaborate with CCLR to integrate college, career, leadership, and readiness opportunities into the scholar-athlete experience.

• Collaborate with Wealth Builds to support financial literacy, long-term planning, and economic empowerment opportunities for scholar-athletes and families.

• Build relationships with local track and field organizations, clubs, colleges, athletic programs, leagues, governing bodies, and community partners to expand opportunities for scholar-athletes.

• Support a strong, inclusive, collaborative, and mission-aligned Track & Field culture across HCZ.

Compliance and Data-Informed Decision-Making

• Ensure all coaching activities comply with HCZ policies, school requirements, league regulations, and applicable athletic governing-body standards.

• Maintain accurate records of scholar participation, attendance, academic eligibility, performance, competition results, and development.

• Use performance data to inform training plans, event assignments, athlete development, competition preparation, and program improvements.

• Monitor scholar-athletes’ academic eligibility and readiness for collegiate athletic opportunities.

• Research and identify appropriate sprint competitions, invitationals, showcases, camps, clinics, and collegiate exposure opportunities.

• Support scholar-athletes who demonstrate the potential and interest to pursue collegiate athletics.

• Ensure scholar participation in external competitions and opportunities aligns with applicable school, league, organizational, and NCAA requirements.

Schedule

The Track & Field Distance Coach must be available to work:

Fall/Spring

  • Monday–Friday, 1:00 p.m.–8:00 p.m.
  • Saturday, 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. is required depending on the sport & game schedule.

Summer

  • 1:00 PM - 7:00 PM

The position may also require attendance at administrative meetings, professional development sessions, athletic events, competitions, invitationals, championships, family engagement activities, and other organizational responsibilities outside of the standard work schedule.

title: Shenandoah Valley Migrant Education Program Director
description:
The Shenandoah Valley Migrant Education Program (SVMEP) is hiring for a full-time Program Director. SVMEP provides quality academic support services and advocacy to newly arrived migrant families in the community. SVMEP staff visit the families in their homes and migrant camps to assess their needs and aid the students and young adults in achieving their educational goals. SVMEP is one of many programs and clinics within the Institute for Innovation in Health and Human Services (IIHHS). IIHHS is a forward-thinking and dynamic organization that strives to cultivate a shared sense of purpose in building healthier and safer communities where all individuals can thrive and flourish. IIHHS is housed within JMU’s College of Health and Behavioral Studies (CHBS).

CHBS is committed to shaping a forward-thinking and dynamic environment by refining policies, practices, and processes that strengthen our community, drive real-world advancement, and maintain spaces conducive to individual and collective growth. Through education, scholarship, and service, individuals are inspired to make responsible and meaningful contributions to the college, campus, local community, and broader world. Join us in fostering collaboration and innovation as we grow a dynamic college that embodies an atmosphere of belonging, champions excellence, and shares a sense of purpose. James Madison University is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a thriving environment where a wide range of perspectives are embraced, and fairness is upheld.

title: Residential Coordinator PT (Sat-Sun, 12am-8am)
description:
Title: Residential Coordinator PT (Weekend Overnight 12am-8am)

Department: Katherine Hanley Family Shelter

Reports to: Assistant Director of Operations

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

About Us:

Shelter House was established in 1981 as a grassroots responder to the homelessness crisis in Fairfax County. Since the organization’s inception, we have adapted and grown to meet community needs, all while working in partnership with government and private partners and community members. Today, Shelter House is a successful and reputable organization of over 100 employees committed to preventing and ending homelessness and domestic violence. In the last year, our compassionate team of individuals changed the lives of nearly 2,000 individuals, half of which were children.

Our Culture is built from our Core Values of Inclusivity, Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, and Empowerment (iC.A.R.E.). In addition to our incredible mission and culture, we offer our employees a work-life balance, 401K (with employer matching), and core benefits (medical/dental/vision) for full-time employees with a generous employer contribution towards premiums.

About the Role:

The Residential Coordinator provides essential 24-hour awake coverage and supervision of the shelter. The Residential Coordinator is the lead person on shift acting as the first point of contact for client needs and support. This position is responsible for crisis intervention, facilities management, ensuring the safe and efficient operation of the front desk and maintaining a positive living environment within the shelter. The residential coordinator will ensure the safety of shelter residents and the property of Shelter House.

How you will contribute:

  • Ensure the safe functioning of the shelter and maintain a safe environment for clients. Monitor visitor check-in and front desk calls and inquiries
  • Update the daily log by documenting all interactions with clients and any other significant events in the shelter
  • Work closely with case managers to support and reinforce the client’s service plan and maintain ongoing communication regarding client progress
  • Complete efficient shift exchange with incoming/ outgoing staff and report on the day’s activities in order to maintain consistency throughout the day
  • Ensure all documentation pertaining to the Shelter House log is completed and in compliance with agency best practice
  • Evaluate and provide for basic needs of shelter clients while on shift. Distribute household items, toiletries and other items to clients as needed.
  • Maintain the dignity and confidentiality of all clients during service delivery
  • Maintain current knowledge and ability to administer emergency procedures to include building evacuation, health emergencies, and safety management
  • Conduct assessments and intakes for One-Night-Only families seeking shelter after hours.
  • Assist with administration of medication delivery and security
  • Accept donations and support volunteer programs and events in the shelter
  • Participate in staff meetings and staff training as directed
  • Ensure compliance with all agency policies and best practices
  • Proficiently utilize Microsoft applications (email, calendar, drive, docs, etc.) as a part of day-to-day work requirements
  • Serve as emergency personnel and must report to work as scheduled regardless of circumstances (inclement weather, highway congestion, etc.)
  • Safely utilize Shelter House owned vehicles to drive clients to various locations.
  • Exemplify the Shelter House core values; Collaboration, Accountability, Respect and Empowerment
  • Other Duties as assigned

Requirements

Required

  • A high school diploma or GED
  • 2+ years of experience in human services field i.e., mental health, substance abuse, homeless and domestic violence
  • Ability to build strong working relationships with clients and team members
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Valid Driver’s License
  • Willingness work evenings and weekends when needed

Preferred

  • A bachelor’s in human services/ related field
  • 1 year of experience in customer service
  • Experience working in programs serving homeless families
  • Experience working in a residential environment
  • Current CPR/ First aid certification

Physical Requirements

  • Annual TB Test is required
  • Ability to sit or stand for long periods
  • Ability to lift items weighing 10-20 pounds

Benefits

Benefits:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
  • 401K contributions with a 4% employer match
  • 13 Paid Holidays, 2 Floating Holidays and the opportunity to take your Birthday Off
  • Two Semi-Annual Team Building Events

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy: Shelter House is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all employees and applicants. All employment-related decisions will be made and carried out without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age (over 40), sex, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability unrelated to the individual's ability to perform his or her job or any other legally protected status. Shelter House will also provide reasonable accommodations to pregnant and qualified employees with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of their job, and to employees with respect to their observance of their religious beliefs, in accordance with applicable law. Any job applicant or employee who would like or needs an accommodation may request an accommodation by contacting the Human Resources department.

Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace Policy:

Drug-Free Workplace: Shelter House is committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace. Employment is contingent upon compliance with our Drug-Free Workplace Policy, which prohibits the unlawful manufacture, sale, distribution, dispensation, possession, or use of controlled substances or marijuana in the workplace. Additionally, all subcontracts and purchase orders over $10,000 must include provisions ensuring a drug-free workplace.

title: Fuel Station Supervisor
description:
Why choose us?

Are you ready to take the next step in your career? Join us for an exciting opportunity at Albertsons Companies, where innovation and customer service go hand-in-hand!

At Albertsons Companies, we are looking for someone who’s not just seeking a job, but someone who wants to make an impact. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to lead, innovate, and contribute to the growth of a company that values great service and lasting customer relationships. This position offers the chance to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that’s constantly evolving.


Position Purpose

The Fuel Station Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the fuel center, ensuring a safe, clean, and customer-focused environment while meeting sales, profitability, and compliance goals. This position provides leadership for fuel station associates, maintains regulatory compliance, manages inventory and cash handling procedures, and delivers exceptional customer service.

Key Responsibilities Department Operations
  • Supervise daily fuel station operations to ensure efficient and effective performance.
  • Ensure fuel pumps, payment systems, and fuel dispensing equipment are functioning properly.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and professional fuel station environment.
  • Monitor fuel levels and coordinate deliveries as directed.
  • Execute merchandising, promotional, and marketing programs.
Leadership & Team Development
  • Lead, coach, and develop fuel station associates.
  • Train associates on company policies, customer service standards, cash handling procedures, and safety requirements.
  • Assign daily responsibilities and ensure work is completed according to company standards.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, and customer service excellence.
  • Provide performance feedback and operational guidance to associates.
Customer Service
  • Deliver outstanding customer service and foster positive customer relationships.
  • Assist customers with questions, concerns, and fuel station transactions.
  • Resolve customer complaints promptly and professionally.
  • Promote loyalty programs and company promotions.
Inventory & Merchandising
  • Monitor inventory levels of convenience merchandise, beverages, and other fuel station products.
  • Ensure shelves, displays, coolers, and promotional areas remain stocked and properly merchandised.
  • Verify pricing accuracy and promotional signage.
  • Assist with receiving and inventory control processes.
Cash Handling & Financial Accountability
  • Ensure proper cash handling, reconciliation, and deposit procedures are followed.
  • Monitor and investigate cash shortages, overages, and transaction discrepancies.
  • Support achievement of sales, labor, and profitability goals.
  • Assist with reporting and operational recordkeeping.
Safety & Regulatory Compliance
  • Ensure compliance with all federal, state, local, and company regulations related to fuel operations.
  • Conduct routine safety inspections and verify emergency equipment is operational.
  • Ensure compliance with fuel handling, environmental, and hazardous materials standards.
  • Enforce age-restricted sales requirements and company policies where applicable.
  • Promote workplace safety and accident prevention practices.

We also provide a variety of benefits including:

  • Competitive wages paid weekly
· Access to up to 50% of your earned wages before payday, via our partnership with Stream
  • Associate discounts
  • Health and financial well-being benefits for eligible associates (Medical, Dental, 401k and more!)
  • Time off (vacation, holidays, sick pay). For eligibility requirements please visit myACI Benefits
  • Leaders invested in your training, career growth and development
  • An inclusive work environment with talented colleagues who reflect the communities we serve

title: Real Estate Quality Assurance Specialist
description:
Live your best (work) life at TruWest Credit Union!

Are you eager to be part of a company that stands out? Want to make a difference in your clients' lives? We do too!

At TruWest, we focus on our employees so you can focus on your business. We offer first day medical, dental, vision, life insurance, pet benefits, 401(k), and so much more. We even help you save for retirement by matching $0.50 per $1 contributed, up to 6% of your pay to your 401(k) contributions.


Check out our video that highlights all the amazing things we do here: https://vimeo.com/721196286/593a894041

If you’re looking for a place to call home, you’ve found it. What are you waiting for? Apply Now!

Want to learn more? Scroll down and check out the job details.

Pay Range: $27.78 - $33.95.
Final salary is dependent on a candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Summary of Responsibilities

The Real Estate Quality Assurance Specialist independently performs quality assurance reviews of real estate loan files to ensure documentation and lending activities are accurate and consistent with established credit union policies, procedures, underwriting guidelines, regulatory requirements, and investor guidelines. The position identifies and analyzes exceptions, determines appropriate corrective action within established guidelines, and monitors findings through resolution.

The Specialist researches and analyzes complex quality assurance issues, identifies trends and recurring exceptions, and provides recommendations for process, workflow, procedural, or training improvements. This position works closely with Mortgage employees and leaders to communicate findings, provide guidance, coaching, and training, and influence practices that improve loan quality and reduce recurring errors. Complex regulatory interpretations and significant risk matters are escalated to the appropriate leader.

Education

A high school education or GED

Experience

Three years to five years of similar or related experience.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Knowledge of real estate lending, loan origination, servicing, underwriting, or quality assurance processes.
  • Working knowledge of applicable mortgage lending regulations, investor requirements, underwriting guidelines, policies, and procedures.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to research and evaluate complex quality assurance issues and develop recommendations for resolution.
  • Ability to independently interpret and apply established policies, procedures, underwriting guidelines, investor requirements, and quality assurance standards.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify documentation errors, inconsistencies, exceptions, and potential areas of risk.
  • Strong interpersonal communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate sensitive or complex quality assurance findings.
  • Ability to influence, coach, and provide guidance to employees and leaders regarding quality assurance requirements, findings, and corrective actions.
  • Ability to build collaborative working relationships and obtain cooperation when addressing exceptions, recurring errors, or required corrective actions.
  • Ability to provide training and education related to established quality assurance standards, lending requirements, and identified areas for improvement.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to independently manage multiple reviews, findings, and follow-up activities.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn and effectively utilize lending and quality assurance systems.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive member, employee, and business information.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  1. Independently perform quality assurance reviews of real estate loan files to determine adherence to established credit union policies, procedures, underwriting guidelines, regulatory requirements, and investor requirements.
  2. Review loan documentation for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and compliance with established requirements; identify, analyze, and document exceptions or discrepancies.
  3. Evaluate identified quality assurance exceptions and determine appropriate corrective action within established guidelines. Escalate complex regulatory interpretations, significant risk matters, or issues outside established authority as appropriate.
  4. Research and analyze complex quality assurance exceptions, including situations where established procedures or prior precedent may not fully address the issue; evaluate available information and potential solutions and provide recommendations for resolution.
  5. Monitor quality assurance findings through resolution, follow up on required corrective actions, and validate that identified exceptions have been appropriately addressed.
  6. Communicate quality assurance findings and required corrective actions to Mortgage employees and leaders, including sensitive or complex findings, and work collaboratively to obtain appropriate resolution.
  7. Provide feedback to Mortgage employees regarding established quality assurance requirements, recurring exceptions, corrective actions, and practices that improve loan quality and reduce errors.
  8. Partner with Quality Assurance Analyst to address recurring quality issues and influence changes in practices, workflows, or behaviors based on quality assurance findings and trends.
  9. Assist Quality Assurance Analyst in preparing and maintaining quality assurance reporting, including review results, findings, trends, exception rates, corrective actions, and other information used by management to evaluate loan quality and operational risk.
  10. Assist with the development and maintenance of quality assurance review standards, checklists, procedures, job aids, and other departmental documentation based on established lending and investor requirements.
  11. Support internal and external audit, examination, and quality control activities by gathering, reviewing, and organizing requested documentation and information.
  12. Effectively collaborate and communicate with team members, leaders, members, business partners, and other stakeholders to support business operations and achieve departmental objectives. This includes participating in designated onsite workdays and other required in-person activities, such as meetings, training, coaching, mentoring, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration, as determined by business needs. Regular and reliable attendance is required to perform these essential functions effectively. Reasonable accommodation will be considered in accordance with applicable law.

Secondary Duties and Responsibilities

  1. Assist with special projects and research related to mortgage quality assurance and departmental initiatives.
  2. Support investor certifications, vendor due diligence, audits, and other mortgage quality assurance activities as assigned.
  3. Participate in cross-training and professional development to maintain and expand knowledge of mortgage lending, servicing, investor requirements, regulations, and quality assurance practices.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be required to sit, stand, walk, bend, and lift or move objects of up to 15 pounds; use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms above shoulder height and below the waist; and communicate effectively. Specific vision abilities required for this role may include close vision, distance vision, color vision, the ability to adjust focus, and the ability to work at a computer and view a monitor for extended periods of time.

Disclosure

This job description describes the current assignment of essential functions and responsibilities and is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all duties, qualifications, or tasks. It does not constitute an employment agreement and does not restrict TruWest Credit Union’s right to assign, reassign, modify, or eliminate duties and responsibilities at any time, with or without notice, based on business needs or organizational changes.

title: Brand Graphic Designer (Contractor)
description:
Position Overview

Aimtal is seeking a skilled Brand Graphic Designer Contractor to support our team across specific client accounts. In this role, you will support our clients with elevating their visual communications through polished editorial design, brand systems, and high-impact marketing collateral.


The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in B2B marketing contexts, translating complex technical concepts into clean, visually engaging formats. You excel at working with long-form content—such as eBooks, white-papers, and one-pagers—and can step into established brand design systems or build new ones from scratch. This is a fully remote, independent contractor position collaborating closely with Aimtal’s strategy, creative, and project management teams.


Responsibilities

  • Editorial & Collateral Layout: Design high-converting B2B marketing collateral with a heavy focus on multi-page editorial design, including eBooks, whitepapers, one-pagers, case studies, and presentation decks.
  • InDesign & Template Systems: Build and maintain scalable document templates, master pages, character/paragraph styles, and visual systems in Adobe InDesign to streamline ongoing client publishing needs.
  • Digital Campaign Design: Create supporting digital and print creative for integrated marketing campaigns, including social media assets, advertising graphics for multiple channels, and visual elements for client websites.
  • Data Visualization & Tech Graphics: Translate complex technical concepts, product workflows, and data insights into clear, engaging custom illustrations, infographics, and visual assets.
  • Strategic Client Consultation: Advise internal teams and clients during meetings and feedback sessions, advocating for design best practices that align with overall campaign strategy and business goals.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Aimtal account managers and designers to interpret creative briefs, iterate on feedback, and deliver production-ready assets on tight deadlines.
  • Brand Governance & Quality Assurance: Maintain absolute visual integrity and production quality across all deliverables, rapidly adapting to distinct client brand guidelines and technical specifications.


Qualifications

  • Experience: 5+ years of graphic design experience in a B2B, agency, or technology-focused environment (freelance or contract experience preferred).
  • Editorial Mastery: Proven track record in layout and editorial design for digital publications (eBooks, whitepapers, reports, and one-pagers).
  • Technical Tooling: High proficiency in Adobe InDesign (master pages, style sheets, grid systems), Adobe Creative Cloud, and Figma.
  • Portfolio Requirement: A strong portfolio demonstrating experience with B2B tech-focused brand campaigns , and data visualization.
  • Communication & Independence: Strong client-facing presence with the ability to confidently present concepts, articulate design choices, and manage feedback, paired with self-directed time management in a remote workplace.
  • Availability: Ability to align working hours with North American Eastern Time (ET) for project check-ins and client feedback review.
  • Software & Equipment Setup: Able to provide and maintain your own professional workstation and hardware. You must hold and manage your own active licenses for all necessary design platforms required to execute project deliverables, specifically Adobe Creative Cloud and Figma.
  • Self-Management & Prioritization: Operate with a high degree of autonomy and manage your workload across overlapping projects and deadlines.

title: Newborn Photographer - OhioHealth Grant
description:

We are looking to fill Thursday and Sunday shifts, starting at 9am, with weekends required. There is the possibility of additional hours at other Columbus hospitals if desired.

  • Adaptability
  • Resourcefulness
  • Motivated
  • Demonstrates a commitment to service through a positive work ethic that benefits both the individual and the performance of a thriving and successful workplace environment.

  • Communicates effectively to ensure success, Helps when needed, helps team overcome hurdles, enables the team to be the best they can be.

Overall, a WelcomeNewborn photographer is not just a photographer but a storyteller who helps families preserve their most precious memories.


Why Join Us?

title: Underground Storage Tank Inspector - NV/UT

As an Underground Storage Tank (UST) Inspector Trainee, you will receive on-the-job training to gain a comprehensive understanding of fuel management for facilities with above and below-ground storage systems. This role involves learning about the equipment, documentation, and procedures necessary for conducting inspection

Drive a company service vehicle to customer locations, often on a designated route
Perform inspections of fueling facilities, including visual observations and site surveys
Provide on-site training to customers or company staff
Conduct limited maintenance tasks based on site conditions
Capture inspection results using customized data collection software on handheld devices or laptops

Ability to lift up to 70 lbs and perform physical tasks (stooping, bending, kneeling)
Comfortable climbing 20 ft extension ladders multiple times daily
Basic computer skills for data entry
Effective communication skills

What Tanknology Can Offer You:

title: Mammography Trainee
description:
Envision Radiology is looking for a Mammography Trainee to join our Team!
Monday - Friday 8:30 AM - 4:00 PM | Position Pay Range: $35.48 - $38.48

Summary/Objective

The Mammography Trainee performs routine and diagnostic exams relating to breast anatomy to obtain images at a satisfactory level under the guidance of a certified Mammography Technologist. Maintains and monitors patient environment, adheres to safety procedures and contributes to the security and maintenance of the unit.

Essential Functions

· Interfaces with patients to ascertain medical history and provides instructions/explanation of the procedure and/or exam to obtain the best possible image.

· Provides patient education on breast self-examination as needed.

· Reviews patient charts for missed clinical information and/or consent.

· Screens patients for surgical and other implants, contrast allergies, etc.

· Obtains prior imaging as needed and performs high quality scans to submit to the Radiologist for interpretation.

· Performs exams while attending to patient’s care before, during and following exam and notifies the appropriate party if patient’s condition changes at any time.

· Transfers images to other locations as needed.

· Coordinates procedure protocols with Radiologist.

· Maintains and regularly inspects equipment and immediately reports any quality concerns as well as equipment failures or deficiencies.

· Interfaces with Lead Technologist & Center/Area Manager regarding any and all departmental concerns.

· Other duties as assigned.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Competencies

1. Technical Capacity.

2. Ethical Conduct.

3. Thoroughness.

4. Time Management.

5. Personal Effectiveness/Credibility.

This position has no supervision responsibilities.

Work Environment

This job operates in an environmentally controlled outpatient clinical environment. Potential exposure to radiation, which is minimized by the use of Personal Protective Equipment. Possible exposure to bodily fluids, communicable diseases, toxic substances, ionizing radiation and other conditions common to a medical office environment. Often requires work in cool, dimly lighted rooms.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by and employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee may exert up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

The employee is regularly required to use hands and fingers to handle, feel or operate objects, tools or controls and reach with hands and arms. The employee is frequently required to talk and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Travel

No travel is expected for this position.

Job Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications/Experience:

· Ability to educate patients on procedures being performed

· Detail oriented, self-motivated, a problem solver and a team player

· Ability to navigate multiple computer screens and browsers quickly and accurately

· Ability to excel in a very fast-pace team environment

· Ability to continuously “exceed” company and customer expectation

· Strong communication skills & professional demeanor

Education / Certifications;

· Graduate of an accredited Registered Technologist program

· Current American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) certification

· Current license from state medical board (if applicable)

· Current CPR/BLS certification

None required for this position.

title: MiINIGRIP - SR. PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER
description:
TITLE: Sr. Product Development Engineer
POSITION OBJECTIVE: The core focus of the Sr. Product Development Engineer role is to drive and implement pioneering research and development initiatives, placing a significant emphasis on innovation across various domains, including emerging technologies, data utilization, product enhancement, engineering materials, and advanced manufacturing processes, particularly in the plastics sector. By staying abreast of the latest trends in technology and materials science, the Sr. Product Development Engineer will propel the organization forward, establishing new industry benchmarks and fostering a culture centered around continuous improvement and cutting-edge product development. Responsibilities involve leading the development of new products for our consumer business sector, from concept to commercialization. In this capacity, this position is tasked with driving innovation and facilitating growth by coordinating brainstorming sessions, developing prototypes, and conducting comprehensive analyses to evaluate feasibility and scalability.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Proven experience (2+ years) in mechanical engineering, preferably in plastic manufacturing or a related industry.
Proven experience in new product development within the consumer goods industry, with a focus on plastic bags or related products preferred.
Strong proficiency in Six Sigma methodologies and statistical analysis tools.
Excellent project management skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks, manage timelines, and deliver results on schedule.
Proficient in CAD and Solid modeling software
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Intellectual property management experience, including filing for patents and conducting patent searches.
Strong organizational skills, able to handle multiple tasks.
Willingness to travel to manufacturing sites as needed (10% - 40% travel, international travel possible)

Ensure consistent, dependable attendance and demonstrate a willingness to accommodate non-standard work hours as necessary.
Capable of effectively managing job-related stress and fostering productive workplace interactions.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead the development of new products for consumer product businesses, from concept generation to commercialization.
Coordinate brainstorming sessions to generate creative and unique product ideas that address consumer needs and market trends.
Analyze consumer, market, and industry trends to identify opportunities for innovation and growth.\
Attend trade shows and industry events to stay informed about emerging trends and technologies in the consumer goods industry.
Investigate and evaluate new mechanical technologies, machines, and equipment that could improve manufacturing processes, and help integrate them into existing production lines.
Evaluate existing mechanical designs for plastic manufacturing systems and recommend improvements to increase efficiency, reduce downtime, and enhance product quality.
Lead or collaborate on the development of prototypes for new mechanical designs or systems, ensuring they meet performance and safety standards and conduct manufacturing and ROI analysis to evaluate feasibility and scalability of production concepts.
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities for process automation, energy efficiency, cost reduction, and waste minimization in the plastic manufacturing process.
Actively file for IP protection of innovative ideas for new products
Regularly perform patent searches to identify potential filing opportunities and monitor competitive landscape.
Utilize six sigma methodologies and statistical problem-solving tools to drive process improvements and optimize product quality.
Apply data-driven approaches to identify and address root causes of product and process issues.
Work closely with cross-functional teams, including design engineers, production managers, and quality control, to ensure that mechanical systems and designs are aligned with production goals and business objectives.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously, from idea generation to product launch, ensuring timely execution and delivery of results.
Communicate project status, risk, and milestones to stakeholders and proactively address any issues that may arise.
