title: Gas Distribution and Facilities Designer
description:
Primary Engineering and Construction Corporation is building a team to deliver natural gas engineering services for projects across Alberta. The Gas Distribution and Facilities Designer will develop and coordinate distribution pipeline and facility designs under individual project assignments.
The role is responsible for safe, reliable, and cost-effective natural gas distribution infrastructure. Work involves engineering design, pipeline routing, station sizing, hydraulic modeling, material selection, and coordination with municipal and utility stakeholders for customer additions, franchise relocations, and system renewal projects.
Responsibilities

Review work requests, existing records, survey information, utility data, site constraints, and applicable client requirements to establish the design basis and identify missing inputs.
Prepare designs for natural gas distribution mains, service extensions, subdivisions, replacements, relocations, and feeder projects as assigned.
Support station and facility work such as piping layouts, valves, meter and regulator arrangements, site plans, equipment replacement, and interfaces with cathodic protection, electrical, and automation specialists.
Develop calculations, drawings, material lists, specifications, cost estimates, construction packages, and design records appropriate to each assignment; coordinate drafting and check outputs before issue.
Apply utility standards and project specifications for materials, pipe and fittings, pressure testing, coatings, station design, and facility integrity where relevant.
Coordinate surveys, geotechnical input, crossings, land and permitting requirements, constructability reviews, and field verification with the responsible specialists.
Identify safety, environmental, operational, and construction risks; document assumptions and changes, resolve review comments, and support field questions and record updates.
Plan assigned work against agreed scope, schedule, and budget; maintain clear communication with the client and internal team.

Qualifications

Diploma in engineering technology or degree in mechanical, civil, petroleum, or a related engineering discipline; equivalent directly relevant gas utility design experience will be considered.
Experience designing natural gas distribution pipelines or related gas facilities in Alberta, including preparation of construction drawings and design documentation.
Working knowledge of CSA Z662, applicable Alberta regulatory requirements, utility design standards, and engineering quality control practices.
Ability to interpret pressure class, pipe material selection, fittings, valves, crossings, clearances, testing, and installation requirements within the assigned scope.
Proficiency with MicroStation, AutoCAD or comparable drafting tools and Microsoft Office; ability to learn client systems and maintain accurate design records.
Clear written and verbal communication, sound coordination skills, and a commitment to field and office safety.
Valid driver’s licence and ability to attend Alberta project sites when required.

Qualifications That Would Help You Succeed

Experience with ATCO Gas and Pipelines design guides, work processes, and construction packages.
Experience with polyethylene and steel distribution systems, station piping and metering, cathodic protection interfaces, or facility upgrades.
Exposure to transmission pipeline projects, facility integrity assessments, risk studies, geotechnical coordination, or trenchless installation.
APEGA professional registration or eligibility, or registration as a certified engineering technologist, appropriate to the responsibilities of the role.
Experience mentoring designers, reviewing drawings, and coordinating multiple concurrent work releases.

If you want to help build a capable gas engineering team and deliver practical designs for Alberta projects, we welcome your application.

title: Intermediate CAD/Revit and Civil 3D Designer
description:
R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited and Neegan Burnside Ltd. are expanding their regional business strategy across Manitoba and Northwest Ontario, with offices in Winnipeg and Thunder Bay. We serve a diverse range of municipal, Indigenous, and private sector clients—and we’re looking for an Intermediate CAD / Revit and Civil 3D Designer to help us deliver exceptional infrastructure solutions.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll be a key technical contributor to our engineering design team, developing detailed drawings and design deliverables for land development, water/wastewater, and municipal infrastructure projects. You’ll work closely with engineers and project managers to interpret designs, coordinate technical information, and take ownership of assigned drawing packages from preliminary design through construction.

Key Responsibilities

  • Independently develop detailed engineering drawings including plan/profile views, site plans, grading layouts, details, and sections.
  • Produce water and wastewater infrastructure drawings, including watermains and sewers, pump stations, site layouts, process/mechanical layouts, equipment arrangements, and process and instrumentation diagrams.
  • Interpret engineering designs and technical information and translate them into accurate, complete, and constructible drawing packages.
  • Apply applicable municipal, provincial, and industry standards and specifications.
  • Coordinate drawing requirements with engineers, project managers, surveyors, contractors, and other disciplines.
  • Review drawings for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with project requirements; identify potential design conflicts and constructability concerns.
  • Prepare quantity take-offs and support design calculations as required.
  • Provide technical support during construction, including responding to contractor inquiries and preparing drawing revisions.
  • Manage multiple projects and competing priorities while meeting established timelines and quality standards.
  • Provide technical guidance and knowledge-sharing to junior designers and technicians.

What You Bring

  • Diploma in Civil/Environmental/Construction Management, Computer Drafting (AutoCAD/Civil 3D), or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
  • Minimum 4 years of relevant engineering design and drafting experience, preferably with municipal infrastructure, land development, or water/wastewater projects.
  • Strong proficiency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D with the ability to independently develop detailed engineering drawing packages.
  • Experience with Revit and/or other BIM platforms is an asset.
  • Experience producing water and wastewater infrastructure drawings.
  • Strong understanding of engineering drawing standards, municipal infrastructure design principles, and applicable technical standards and specifications.
  • Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft 365 and PDF editing tools.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented approach and willingness to support the development of junior team members.
  • CADD work samples may be requested for consideration of work quality.

Bonus Skills (Assets)

  • Experience with municipal infrastructure design, including horizontal and vertical infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with BIM, MicroStation, OpenRoads, or other design and modelling platforms.
  • Experience with municipal design standards and specifications in Manitoba and/or Ontario.
  • Exposure to project management and contract administration.

What Success Looks Like

  • You independently manage assigned drawing packages and deliver accurate, high-quality work on schedule.
  • You apply sound technical judgment and identify design, coordination, and constructability issues.
  • You collaborate effectively with engineers, project managers, contractors, and other disciplines.
  • You respond professionally to field inquiries and changing project requirements.
  • You contribute technical expertise and support the development of junior team members.
  • You demonstrate initiative, accountability, and a commitment to quality project delivery.

Why Choose Burnside Group of Companies?

As a R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited / Neegan Burnside Ltd. employee, you will become part of a supportive group of colleagues across the organization, that work together to provide value and service to our clients, while extending care to each other. We know that our employees are our greatest asset, and thus we strive to provide a positive work/life balance.

Burnside has an over 50-year track record of building a great reputation both internally with their staff and externally with their clients, as an established leader in quality engineering, environmental, project management and consulting services.

Becoming part of the Burnside team opens the door to a wide range of career development, advancement, mentorship and collaboration opportunities across our 12 office locations.

We offer a wide variety of opportunities for our staff, geared to your comfort level in independence and interests. As an agile firm willing to consider a multitude of opportunities as presented by our long-term client base, and in a number of emerging disciplines, we are willing to work with you to set a meaningful career path for you.

We offer:

  • A collaborative culture where friendship, honesty and respect are part of our core values and practices
  • Flexible working hours and office locations, including hybrid working opportunities
  • A competitive compensation and benefits package
  • RRSP company matching plan
  • Career growth and professional development opportunities
  • Potential for performance-driven bonusing
  • Active social committees
  • A welcoming, positive, and inclusive work environment

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to valuing diversity in the workplace and we welcome resumes from all qualified candidates. Burnside will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the entire recruitment, assessment, and selection process, as required. If you are a person with a disability and require an accommodation during these processes, please contact our Human Resources department.

RJ Burnside and Associates Limited and Neegan Burnside Ltd. Company Profiles

Founded in 1970, R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited is a growing values-driven employee-owned multidiscipline Canadian engineering and environmental consulting firm with over 450 staff. Our consistent commitment to investing in technological advancements and training, in addition to encouraging and promoting professional development, has enabled our firm to meet our ongoing and stated goal of continual improvement.

Founded in 1999, Neegan Burnside Ltd. is a majority-Indigenous owned firm committed to working with Indigenous (First Nation, Metis and Inuit) communities, agencies and industries to meet their infrastructure, development and economic goals while remaining sensitive to culture, values and beliefs. As a result, we offer our clients expertise in many technical disciplines including but not limited to water and wastewater, transportation planning and design, land development, stormwater management, bridges and culverts, building engineering and sciences, municipal drainage, municipal advisory services, environmental planning and ecology, hydrogeology, air and noise, asset management, solid waste, landscape architecture and well drilling & diagnostics.

Together, we actively seek to develop relationships with a broad and diversified client base in the Public, Private and Indigenous sectors. We work on a variety of projects throughout Canada, with 11 office locations in Ontario and one in Manitoba.

title: NEON Theatrical Distribution Intern - Spring 2027

  • Research marketing and distribution plans to develop knowledge of the competitive landscape; build decks for case studies on past successful releases.

Program Timeline: Monday, January 4, 2027–Friday, May 21, 2027

We offer a competitive hourly rate of $18.50 per hour. School credit is optional, and documentation can be provided if needed. No relocation assistance is available. Our interns are onsite and in person based in either the New York or the Los Angeles office.

Schedules vary based on department needs and your availability. We do our best to work around your class schedule.

To qualify, you must be a current undergraduate student enrolled at an accredited college or university and taking at least one class during the internship term.

This internship is based in Los Angeles, so candidates must reside in the LA area, hold a valid driver’s license, and have access to a car. Reliable transportation is key — many assignments involve theater visits, screening checks, and event support (including Q&As and other in-person activations).

Ideal Candidates will Have:

  • Genuine interest in theatrical distribution and the release, marketing, and exhibition of independent films
  • Familiarity with NEON’s slate and how films build momentum through press, audience response, and box office performance
  • Excellent organization and attention to detail; comfortable managing release calendars, box office data, and regional research
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret trends and performance metrics across markets and titles
  • Clear and effective written communication for internal updates, exhibitor outreach, and screening reports
  • Proficiency in Excel and Google Sheets (formulas, trackers, and datasets a plus)
  • Comfortable using Google Workspace tools (Docs, Gmail, Zoom) and research platforms such as IMDbPro or exhibitor databases
  • Working knowledge of the theatrical landscape — indie cinemas, major chains, festivals, and current industry trends
  • A self-starter mindset — proactive, resourceful, and eager to take initiative beyond assigned tasks
  • Interest in the intersection of marketing and exhibition, including trailer placements, regional strategies, and audience targeting
  • Experience with Premiere or Photoshop is a plus (e.g., basic trailer edits or deliverables)
  • Prior experience in distribution, exhibition, programming, or marketing is a bonus, but not required

About NEON

NEON internships focus on real-world experience and supporting boundary-pushing projects that define our brand. For college students interested in creative careers, securing an internship with a leading independent film studio like NEON can be a major career booster, providing hands-on industry exposure, valuable connections, and mentorship from professionals passionate about visionary cinema.

Here's what makes the NEON Internship Program unique:

  • Dive Deep: Get hands-on experience in various aspects of film distribution: from marketing and publicity, to acquisitions and theatrical sales and distribution
  • Find Your Fit: We tailor your internship to your interests and skills, placing you on projects that excite you
  • Become Part of the Team: Our internship program is a collaborative experience. You get to work alongside industry veterans who are passionate about nurturing the next generation of filmmakers and industry leaders

At NEON, we are looking for diverse perspectives. We believe a thriving film industry requires a variety of voices and perspectives. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourage applications from all candidates without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, family or parental status, veteran, or disability status. title: Services Principal
description:
Position Title: Services Principal - Professional Services

Job Summary:
Pellera Technologies is hiring a Services Principal to own the growth and health of the services relationship with our most strategic clients. This is a senior, client-facing role that sits between Sales and Delivery and is accountable for one thing above all: turning what our clients are trying to accomplish into services engagements that deliver real outcomes and expand the relationship over time.
You will be assigned a small portfolio of our largest services clients and most significant services pursuits. Within those accounts you are the senior services voice, the person the client calls about services, and the person internally accountable for whether that services relationship is growing and whether it is healthy.

Essential Functions:

Own the services relationship within strategic accounts. Become a trusted services advisor to key client stakeholders and understand their priorities, challenges, initiatives, and technology roadmap.
Build the Services Account Plan alongside the AE. Understand what services the client buys today, where whitespace exists, and develop a strategy to expand the relationship.
Identify and develop new services opportunities. Across Professional Services, Managed Services, consulting and advisory, cloud, security, infrastructure, AI and data, and adoption.
Engage early in strategic pursuits. Help shape the opportunity before an SOW or solution is defined, rather than responding to a services request after the fact.
Connect technology sales to services opportunities. Look at major product and platform initiatives and determine what assessment, design, implementation, migration, optimization, adoption, or managed services should surround them.
Conduct executive and client services reviews. Review current engagements, outcomes, satisfaction, upcoming initiatives, risks, and expansion opportunities.
Act as an escalation point and client advocate. When delivery issues arise, work with delivery leadership to protect the relationship and restore client confidence.
Orchestrate internal services resources. Bring in the right architects, consultants, practice leaders, delivery executives, and specialists based on the client's needs.
Help develop and position solutions and proposals. Ensure the proposed services solution addresses the client's business problem and tells a compelling value story.
Drive cross-sell and lifecycle expansion. Move clients from isolated projects toward broader, recurring relationships, particularly Managed Services and ongoing advisory and optimization services.
Maintain a services pipeline and growth plan. For assigned strategic accounts and pursuits, partnering closely with the AE and sales leadership.
Capture and route client feedback. Bring it back into the services organization to improve offerings, delivery quality, and overall client experience.

Required Skills/Abilities/Competencies

Ten or more years in professional services, consulting, or technology services, including at least five in a client-facing role carrying growth accountability for a portfolio of accounts.
A demonstrated record of growing services revenue inside large enterprise accounts, including Managed Services and recurring advisory engagements.
Credibility at the executive level. Able to hold a business conversation with a CIO, CTO, or VP of Infrastructure without a technical escort.
Working fluency across the modern enterprise stack: hybrid infrastructure, cloud, data and AI, cybersecurity, and managed operations. Depth in one, literacy in all.
Experience shaping opportunities before an SOW exists, through assessments, workshops, roadmaps, and business cases.
Comfortable operating between Sales and Delivery without owning either. This role runs on influence rather than authority.
VAR, systems integrator, MSP, or consultancy background strongly preferred.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, and willingness to travel to assigned accounts (approximately 30 to 50 percent).

How is Performance Measured:

Services gross profit growth within assigned accounts.
Services penetration, measured as services GP as a share of total account GP.
Managed Services and recurring revenue mix within the portfolio.
Qualified services pipeline created and shaped, particularly pre-SOW.
Client satisfaction and retention within assigned accounts.

Physical Requirements:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

title: Track and Field Distance Coach
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Harlem Children’s Zone (HCZ)—a world-renowned education and poverty-fighting organization based in New York—seeks an enthusiastic, dedicated, and mission-aligned Track & Field Distance Coach.

The Track & Field Distance Coach will bring a strong commitment to Harlem Children’s Zone’s mission of breaking the cycle of intergenerational poverty through comprehensive, on-the-ground programming that creates opportunities for children and families to thrive in school, work, and life.

We are seeking an experienced Track & Field Distance Coach to lead the development of scholar-athletes competing in distance events across our elementary, middle, and high school programs. The Distance Coach will be responsible for providing high-quality instruction, developing scholar-athletes’ technical, physical, tactical, and mental skills, preparing athletes for competition, and contributing to the overall growth and success of the HCZ Track & Field program.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a passion for HCZ’s mission, an understanding of and respect for the Harlem community, and experience working with youth in a school-based or community-based setting. The successful candidate will use athletics as a platform to promote academic achievement, leadership, accountability, discipline, teamwork, resilience, and personal growth.

For more information, check out Want to Work at Harlem Children's Zone? Here's 7 Things You Need to Know.

Requirements

• High school diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree preferred.

• At least three years of experience coaching track and field, cross country, distance running, or a related endurance sport, preferably at the middle school, high school, collegiate, club, or elite competitive level.

• Demonstrated experience coaching distance events, including but not limited to the 800m, 1500m/1600m, 3000m, 3200m, 5K, and cross country.

• Strong knowledge of distance running principles, race strategy, conditioning, training methodology, recovery, injury prevention, and athlete development.

• Demonstrated ability to design and implement progressive training programs appropriate for youth and adolescent athletes.

• Experience coaching and supporting youth and adolescent populations.

• Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, mentor, and retain scholar-athletes.

• Commitment to the mission, values, and programs of Harlem Children’s Zone.

• Strong leadership, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, and meet established deadlines.

• A positive, enthusiastic, collaborative, flexible, and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Ability to work effectively with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, HCZ colleagues, community organizations, and external partners.

• CPR and First Aid certification, or the ability to obtain certification within the required timeframe.

• Ability to travel to away meets, cross country competitions, tournaments, invitationals, championships, and other athletic events.

• Ability to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours as required by the athletic schedule.

Who You Are

The Track & Field Distance Coach is responsible for the development and performance of scholar-athletes competing in distance events while contributing to the overall success and culture of the HCZ Track & Field program.

The Distance Coach will design and implement age-appropriate training plans, lead practices, prepare athletes for competition, evaluate performance, and provide individualized coaching and feedback. The coach will work closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leadership, and other coaching staff to ensure consistency in training, expectations, athlete development, and program operations.

The successful candidate understands that coaching extends beyond athletic performance. They will serve as a mentor and role model who promotes academic accountability, positive behavior, discipline, leadership, teamwork, resilience, healthy habits, and long-term scholar development.

The Distance Coach must understand the importance of developing athletes progressively and safely. They should be able to balance competitive expectations with appropriate training loads, recovery, conditioning, injury prevention, and the individual needs of developing athletes.

What You’ll Do

Distance Program Leadership and Training

• In collaboration with the Head Track & Field Coach and Athletic Leadership, develop and implement a comprehensive distance-training program for elementary, middle, and high school scholar-athletes.

• Design age-appropriate, progressive training plans that develop endurance, speed endurance, strength, mobility, running mechanics, race strategy, and overall athletic performance.

• Lead daily practices and distance-specific training sessions in accordance with the overall Track & Field program schedule.

• Develop individualized training plans based on athlete ability, experience, event specialization, competition schedule, and developmental needs.

• Prepare scholar-athletes for distance events, including the 800m, 1500m/1600m, 3000m, 3200m, 5K, cross country, and other applicable endurance events.

• Teach proper running mechanics, pacing, race strategy, warm-up and cool-down procedures, recovery techniques, and training principles.

• Monitor training volume, intensity, recovery, and athlete readiness to support healthy and sustainable development.

• Incorporate strength, mobility, flexibility, conditioning, and injury-prevention strategies appropriate for distance athletes.

• Collaborate with Strength & Conditioning staff, Athletic Trainers, medical personnel, and other coaches when appropriate to support athlete health and performance.

• Evaluate athlete performance through practices, competitions, time trials, fitness assessments, and other appropriate measures.

• Use performance data to establish goals and adjust training plans.

• Identify and develop scholar-athletes with potential to compete at higher levels of competition.

Competition and Meet Preparation

• Prepare scholar-athletes for league meets, invitationals, championships, cross country competitions, tournaments, and other sanctioned athletic events.

• Develop race strategies and individualized competition plans based on event, athlete strengths, competition level, and meet conditions.

• Attend and actively coach assigned competitions and provide real-time instruction, support, and feedback.

• Maintain accurate records of athlete times, personal records, placements, qualifying standards, and other relevant performance data.

• Help identify opportunities for scholar-athletes to compete in appropriate competitive environments that support their development.

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with meet entries, athlete selection, relay considerations, event assignments, and competition logistics.

• Promote sportsmanship, professionalism, accountability, and appropriate conduct before, during, and after competitions.

Scholar-Athlete Development and Accountability

• Recruit, evaluate, develop, and retain scholar-athletes interested in distance running and endurance events.

• Provide individualized instruction and feedback to support each scholar-athlete’s athletic development.

• Establish a positive, disciplined, inclusive, and competitive training environment.

• Promote sportsmanship, teamwork, leadership, resilience, accountability, discipline, and respect.

• Establish and communicate clear expectations regarding attendance, participation, behavior, academic performance, training standards, and team responsibilities.

• Hold scholar-athletes accountable for meeting HCZ academic, school attendance, and after-school programming standards.

• Collaborate with school staff, CCLR, Zone site staff, families, and other HCZ colleagues to identify and support scholars experiencing academic, attendance, behavioral, or engagement challenges.

• Reinforce the expectation that academic responsibilities and required school or after-school programming take priority over athletic participation.

• Teach scholar-athletes the importance of goal setting, consistency, time management, nutrition, hydration, recovery, discipline, and responsible decision-making.

• Recognize and celebrate academic achievement, leadership, positive behavior, personal growth, and athletic accomplishments.

Athlete Health, Safety, and Wellness

• Prioritize the health and safety of all scholar-athletes during practices and competitions.

• Implement appropriate warm-up, cool-down, recovery, hydration, and environmental safety practices.

• Monitor athletes for signs of excessive fatigue, overtraining, injury, dehydration, heat-related illness, or other health concerns.

• Follow all HCZ, school, league, and athletic safety policies and procedures.

• Immediately report injuries, incidents, behavioral concerns, and other relevant matters through established protocols.

• Collaborate with Athletic Trainers, school nurses, Strength & Conditioning staff, and other appropriate professionals regarding scholar-athlete health and readiness.

• Promote healthy training habits and educate scholar-athletes on the importance of recovery, nutrition, hydration, sleep, and injury prevention.

Program Operations

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with the day-to-day operation of the Track & Field program.

• Maintain accurate records related to athlete participation, attendance, performance, eligibility, competition results, and program outcomes.

• Support the management and maintenance of Track & Field equipment, uniforms, supplies, and program resources.

• Ensure equipment is properly maintained and returned following practices and competitions.

• Assist with scheduling practices, competitions, transportation, facilities, and other program logistics.

• Support the planning and execution of Track & Field events, clinics, showcases, camps, community events, and other program activities.

• Maintain a clean, organized, safe, and professional training environment.

• Provide timely updates regarding program needs, athlete concerns, equipment, facilities, competitions, and other operational matters.

Collaboration and Organizational Alignment

• Collaborate closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leaders, and other coaches to ensure program alignment.

• Support the implementation of HCZ policies, procedures, organizational initiatives, and strategic priorities.

• Participate in required meetings, professional development sessions, trainings, family engagement activities, and organizational events.

• Maintain consistent and professional communication with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, and external partners.

• Collaborate with CCLR to integrate college, career, leadership, and readiness opportunities into the scholar-athlete experience.

• Collaborate with Wealth Builds to support financial literacy, long-term planning, and economic empowerment opportunities for scholar-athletes and families.

• Build relationships with local running organizations, clubs, colleges, athletic programs, leagues, and other community partners to expand opportunities for scholar-athletes.

• Support a strong, inclusive, collaborative, and mission-aligned Track & Field culture across HCZ.

Compliance and Data-Informed Decision-Making

• Ensure all coaching activities comply with HCZ policies, school requirements, league regulations, and applicable athletic governing-body standards.

• Maintain accurate records of scholar participation, attendance, academic eligibility, performance, competition results, and development.

• Use performance data to inform training plans, event assignments, athlete development, competition preparation, and program improvements.

• Monitor scholar-athletes’ academic eligibility and readiness for collegiate athletic opportunities.

• Research and identify appropriate distance-running competitions, invitationals, showcases, camps, clinics, and collegiate exposure opportunities.

• Support scholar-athletes who demonstrate the potential and interest to pursue collegiate athletics.

• Ensure scholar participation in external competitions and opportunities aligns with applicable school, league, organizational, and NCAA requirements.

Schedule

The Track & Field Distance Coach must be available to work:

Fall/Spring

  • Monday–Friday, 1:00 p.m.–8:00 p.m.
  • Saturday, 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. is required depending on the sport & game schedule.

Summer

  • 1:00 PM - 7:00 PM

The position may also require attendance at administrative meetings, professional development sessions, athletic events, competitions, invitationals, championships, cross country meets, family engagement activities, and other organizational responsibilities outside of the standard work schedule.

Benefits

As a member of the Harlem Children's Zone team, you will join a supportive and inclusive community dedicated to helping children, families — and our staff — thrive.

Please take a look at our Part-Time benefits below.

Our exceptional Part-Time benefits include:

  • Career Advancement
  • Paid sick leave
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Physical wellness discounts
  • Commuter benefits
  • Additional Benefits (Discounts on flights, hotels, theme parks, concert tickets, and more.)

The salary range for this position is $25-$30 per hour. To be considered, interested applicants should apply directly through the posting. No telephone inquiries or recruiters, please. Replies will only be sent to qualified applicants. Harlem Children's Zone and Promise Academy Charter Schools does not provide work visas for candidates who require employer sponsorship to ensure work authorization in the United States. Harlem Children’s Zone is an EOE.

title: IT Support Specialist
description:
Position Summary

IronOrbit is seeking an experienced, customer-focused IT Support Specialist to join our remote Managed Services team. This role takes ownership of technical issues that require deeper investigation than front-line support, while partnering with engineers when advanced infrastructure expertise is needed.

The ideal candidate has strong troubleshooting fundamentals, excellent communication skills, and a genuine curiosity about how technology works. You enjoy digging into the “why” behind an issue, not just restoring service, and are motivated to learn new tools, platforms, and technical concepts. You will support customers across a variety of environments, including end-user hardware and software, virtual desktops, Microsoft technologies, networking, access management, monitoring, and hosted applications.

Schedule and Growth

The schedule for this position will be core 1st shift business hours, Monday – Friday, covering the Pacific Time Zone, starting between 0700 and 0900 am PST.

IronOrbit offers the opportunity to deepen technical expertise across cloud infrastructure, virtualization, networking, Microsoft technologies, monitoring, backup and recovery, automation, and security. This role is well suited for a support professional who enjoys solving complex problems, sharing knowledge with teammates, and growing toward senior support or engineering responsibilities.
  • Investigate and resolve escalated end-user technical issues across applications, operating systems, virtual desktops, authentication, networking, endpoints, and supporting infrastructure.
  • Use a methodical, curious approach to troubleshooting: review symptoms, logs, alerts, recent changes, and business impact to identify root causes where practical, not just immediate workarounds.
  • Provide professional customer support through phone, email, chat, remote sessions, and the IT service management platform, keeping customers informed throughout the resolution process.
  • Review ticket details, previous troubleshooting, and environmental context to determine appropriate next steps, identify patterns, and escalate thoughtfully when needed.
  • Manage and troubleshoot user accounts, access requests, MFA, Active Directory, Microsoft 365, onboarding, and offboarding activities.
  • Configure and support virtual desktops, desktops, laptops, mobile devices, printers, peripherals, and client applications in cloud or hosted environments.
  • Diagnose connectivity, DNS, DHCP, VLAN, and other network-related issues; escalate appropriately to Tier Three Engineering while maintaining ownership of the issue through resolution.
  • Review, triage, and respond to monitoring alerts and events, including identifying issues that require tickets, investigation, escalation, or proactive follow-up.
  • Build familiarity with customer environments and look for opportunities to prevent recurring issues, improve documentation, and make support more efficient.
  • Document customer communications, troubleshooting steps, findings, and resolutions thoroughly in the IT service management platform.
  • Create and improve knowledge base documentation, share lessons learned, and support cross-training with front-line Analysts and fellow Specialists.
  • Perform approved application upgrades, maintenance, and after-hours support activities as needed.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; an Associate degree in Information Technology or a related field is preferred.
  • Three or more years of professional IT support experience, preferably within a Managed Services Provider or multi-customer support environment.
  • Demonstrated experience troubleshooting beyond scripted solutions and standard knowledge base procedures.
  • Strong working knowledge of Windows, Active Directory, Microsoft 365, TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, remote support tools, and IT service management platforms.
  • Experience supporting virtual desktop, remote desktop, or hosted application environments such as VMware Horizon, Citrix, RDS, or similar technologies.
  • Familiarity with VMware, Hyper-V, Windows Server, Group Policy, RMM tools such as NinjaOne, Veeam or comparable backup tools, VoIP, MDM, and network security appliances is preferred.
  • A strong technical curiosity and desire to continue developing expertise across cloud infrastructure, virtualization, networking, automation, backup and recovery, security, and Microsoft technologies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and organized while managing multiple issues.
  • Technical certifications such as VCTA, VCP, CCNA, or Microsoft certifications are a plus, but not required.

AREAS OF EXCELLENCE

Happy Guests
Spotless Cleanliness
Product Consistency & Quality
Teamwork

3. Product Consistency & Quality

Checklists to 100% Accuracy: All operational checklists are completed accurately and at the designated times, every shift.
Shift Handover Reports: Handover reports must be accurate and on time, for effective shift-to-shift communication.
Flawless Uniform: All Team Members must wear a clean, approved uniform and be well-groomed per the Team Member Handbook, while wearing a nametag and smiling at all times.

4. Teamwork

Communication: Communication between Team Members should be clear, honest, and professional.
Can Do Attitude: Willing to stretch beyond traditional role to meet the needs of the business and MCR’s guests.
Collaboration: All Team Members at all levels must be committed to working together to create a welcoming environment for guests and an effective, positive workplace.

SECTION TWO: Houseperson, Role Specific Duties and Expectations

Other Duties and Expectations

Luggage Handling: Store and retrieve luggage or packages for guests in storage areas, as needed.
Cleaning and Trash Management: Clean and maintain the guest hallways, stairwells, service areas and ice rooms. Collect trash from all exterior garbage receptacles, as well as picking up trash and debris from the parking lot, swimming pool area and common grounds. All front and back of house areas should be well-organized and clean. Collect trash and soiled linen from the housekeepers and deliver to laundry room.
Furniture Upkeep: Monitor placement and condition of public space furniture, report issues to management.
Restocking: Maintain stock levels in guest floor linen closets and guest amenities. Replenish amenities and supplies in assigned guestrooms. Stock and maintain housekeeping cart.

Happy Guests

Management Performance Ratings
Guest Satisfaction Scores/Intent to Return

Spotless Cleanliness

GM/AGM Spot Checks
Leadership Walk-throughs (RVP, etc.)
Guest Ratings/Reviews

Product Consistency & Quality

Checklist Tracking
Management Performance Ratings
Guest Ratings

Teamwork

Management Performance Ratings

Qualifications & Requirements:

Experience in a hospitality, service, consumer-facing franchise or related field preferred.
Can-Do Attitude: Must have a positive attitude and willingness to learn.
Ability to Follow Guidelines: Must be able to understand and follow established guidelines and procedures.
Handle Pace and Pressure: Must work well in stressful, high-pressure situations.
Listening, Conflict Resolution: Must be effective at listening to, understanding, clarifying, and resolving the concerns and issues raised by co-workers and guests.
Communication Skills: Must be able to convey information and ideas clearly.
Hospitality and Guest Service: Must have a desire to serve all guests.
Age Requirement: Must be 18 years of age or older to perform this job.
Schedule and Travel: Must be willing to work a varied schedule that may include evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays based upon the demands of the hotel.
Clock-in/Out: Arrive and clock in on time for every shift worked and clock out at the scheduled shift ending time, unless otherwise directed by your immediate supervisor. Never work while off the clock.
Breaks: Clock in/out for breaks at the designated time on your schedule.
Call Outs: Provide sufficient notice as directed by your supervisor when calling out for a scheduled shift.

Physical Working Demands & Working Environment:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to carry out physical working demands such as:

Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at waist. Requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.
Climbing: Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms.
Balancing: Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing or crouching on narrow, slippery or erratically moving surfaces.
Kneeling: Bending legs at knee to come to rest on one or both knees.
Crawling: Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
Standing: Remaining upright on the feet, particularly for sustained periods of time.
Walking: Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.
Repetitive Motions: Making substantial movements (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.
Lifting: Carrying certain housekeeping items such as linens, trash, or vacuums.

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) of this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

This Correctional Officer Lieutenant position is located at Avon Park Correctional Institution. The incumbent in this position is considered to have regulatory responsibilities and is subject to the provisions of Chapter 60L-36, Florida Administrative Code. The Officer assigned to this position has responsibility for supervising Correctional Officers and Correctional Officer Sergeants assigned to any security post on any of the established shifts. This position serves as the initial commander during emergency situations. Functions as facility manager during non-administrative hours.

Duties include but are not limited to the following:

Plans, organizes and coordinates the activities of all Correctional Officers and Correctional Officer Sergeants assigned to a shift. Delegates post assignments, specific duty assignments, coordinates leave use and ensures accurate completion of attendance and leave reports. Works with employees to ensure proper security coverage. Conducts periodic individual counseling with staff to outline problem areas and to give additional duties or instructions. May take or recommend non-appealable disciplinary action or recommend appealable disciplinary action to higher level management.

Supervises searches for contraband and makes daily inspections of buildings and grounds. Inspects physical plant for security concerns and to maintain proper sanitation standards. Circulates throughout institution observing officers’ performance. Conducts performance evaluations. Schedules and/or coordinates training programs for subordinates. Conducts continuous training of subordinate staff in security procedures.

Supervises and coordinates body cavity searches as authorized by the Warden, Assistant Warden or Chief Correctional Officer. Authorizes non-emergency applications of use of force per DC Rule 33-3.0065(3).

Supervises inmates at the level of risk they present. Manages inmate housing areas, enforces rules and sanitation standards. Transports inmates using approved restraints and observing relevant laws, policies and procedures. Conducts accurate head counts, maintains custody and control over inmates at appointments outside the secured perimeter and escorts inmates within the secured perimeter.

Performs crisis intervention functions to include, but not limited to restraining violent or uncooperative inmates, defending persons against attack, and preventing escapes, using approved deadly or non-deadly force, restraints or other approved methods. Provides emergency assistance during emergencies, disasters and accidents to include, but not limited to, CPR, first aid, implementation of evacuation procedures, security of inmates and/or areas in accordance with the emergency situation.

Conducts inspections and visual and audio surveillance of persons, property, vehicles, building and outdoor areas. Physically checks doors, windows, gates, barred sections, fences and other areas to ensure proper security.

Attends mandatory and other training.

Performs other related duties as required.

This position is an integral member of the Development team, reporting directly to the Director of Development and Communications (DDC) and works closely with the Deputy Director of Development and Communications (DDDC) to drive successful event execution and cross-functional alignment. The role owns a $1.5M event portfolio, supporting the organization’s $6M annual fundraising goal (FY27). In collaboration with Development leadership and event Chairs, the Event Producer is responsible for leading the planning and execution of the organization’s events portfolio, including signature fundraising events (Slay Bells, Jammies at Sammie’s, Dinner with Friends and The Big Pickle) as well as smaller donor engagement events and the organization’s 10th Birthday celebration coming up in Fall 2027.

This role ensures a high-quality guest experience while driving revenue, strengthening relationships, and supporting donor growth. This role is primarily based onsite at our East Austin office, with occasional flexibility for remote work, and requires availability to work occasional evenings and weekends as they relate to events.

The following statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work to be performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended as a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Serve as the internal production lead and primary project manager for all events, including signature fundraising events (Slay Bells, Jammies at Sammie’s, Dinner with Friends and The Big Pickle) and other cultivation and donor engagement events.
  • Manage the entire event lifecycle from the initial brainstorm to planning and execution, post event reporting, and budget oversight.
  • Partner with Development leadership and Host Committees to turn fundraising goals and an established event vision into an engaging guest experience. Shape event design, aesthetic, and program details within an approved budget and direction, bringing forward new ideas for consideration.
  • Build and manage project timelines, workflows, and cross-functional coordination to ensure strong accountability and seamless execution across Development, Communications, and Program teams.
  • Oversee all core event logistics while vetting and managing specialized contractors.
  • Support the solicitation of event support through table sales, sponsorships, and donations.
  • Manage sponsor benefit fulfillment.
  • Manage event budgets and relationships with vendors, contractors, and production partners to deliver high-quality events within financial targets.
  • Own the event platform, project tracking tools, invitations, and guest communications, including registration setup, RSVP monitoring, seating plans, and pre- and post-event communications. Coordinate with the Development Manager to ensure guest, donor, and gift information is accurately recorded in the CRM.
  • Collaborate with the team to manage guest communications from pre-event outreach through post-event follow-up
  • Lead event-day execution, including the run of show, staff and volunteer assignments, vendor coordination, and real-time troubleshooting. Bring significant program, budget, and other consequential decisions to the Director of Development and Communications.
  • Produce post-event attendance and revenue summaries, sponsor recap materials, donor follow-up lists, and a debrief with recommendations for future events.
ESSENTIAL SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
  • Ability to lead event planning, including producing thoughtfully curated events and ensuring high-quality operations and execution.
  • Preferable to have exposure to planning and executing fundraising events and donor engagement activities.
  • Experience managing complex, cross-functional projects and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to engage donors, sponsors, vendors, volunteers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage the contribution of ideas and feedback from a variety of stakeholders, including staff leadership, board members, event co-chairs and host committee.
  • Capacity to effectively project manage and plan for the long term and anticipate future needs, as well as make quick decisions and operate flexibly.
  • Experience managing event budgets, vendors, contractors, and production partners.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple events and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and project management platforms (e.g., Monday.com).
  • Experience with event management platforms, with exposure to fundraising event platforms preferred
  • Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment.
  • Keen eye for detail, design, and delivering high-quality event experiences.
  • Associate or bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent experience (4-8 years' work experience).
  • Minimum of three years of event-planning experience, including serving as the primary lead for an event.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:
  • Associate or bachelor's degree preferred or equivalent experience (4-8 years' work experience).
  • Minimum of three years of event-planning experience, including serving as the primary lead for an event.

title: Automated Fabric Cutter
description:
Postion Summary
Produces machined fabric cover parts by programming, setting up and operating an automated fabric cutting machine; maintaining quality and safety standards; keeping records; and maintaining equipment and supplies.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Roll pre-nested fabric roll onto machine and lift into cradle (2 persons perform the lift).
Pull up cut pattern on computer system using Plataine software. Use joystick control to line up pattern and then initiate machine to cut.
Use a screw driver and allen wrench to change the circular cutting blade (8-10 times per day).
As machine cuts and rolls off cut parts, sort the parts and tie them into a bundle to send to sewing. Sometimes use scissors to cut loose parts that are still attached to scrap.
Gather scrap and place in scrap tray for recycling.
Unload fabric roll from cradle and place onto return conveyor.
May perform other duties/ special or non-routine assignments as instructed.

title: Fire Fighter- Trainee
description:
JOB TITLE: Firefighter
DEPARTMENT/DIVISION: Fire
REPORTS TO: Captain
SUMMARY: Performs a variety of technical tasks in fire suppression, rescue, emergency medical services, prevention, investigation, administrative and other special assignments

POSSIBLE ASSIGNMENTS WITHIN THIS RANK INCLUDE:

Paramedic, Field Training Officer, Fire Inspector, Fire Investigator, Support Services Specialists, or Public Education Coordinator.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Responds to fire alarms, emergency medical service calls and other emergency calls
Performs firefighting operations including deploying and operating hoses, pumping apparatus, directing water streams or other chemicals and raising and climbing unsupported ladders including ground and aerial of up to 105 feet
Performs search and rescue for trapped or injured persons to include swift water rescue work with and without use of boat
Administers first aid and emergency medical services to injured persons to level authorized by Emergency Medical Technician or Paramedic certification
Communicates with dispatch and command staff through the use of specialized communications equipment such as two-way radio system, data link in stations to administration and dispatch
Works shift schedules including weekends, holidays and extended hours in emergency, disaster or other situations influenced by workload or staffing difficulties
Runs, walks, stoops, bends, crawls, rolls, climbs, jumps, lifts, carries, drags, and operates assigned equipment, vehicles while performing fire prevention and suppression duties
With assistance, advances charged and flowing fire hoses discharging up to 250 gpm at 100 psi spray or fog or 50 psi straight bore tip pressure
With assistance, places patients on an ambulance stretcher, lifts stretcher, may carry stretcher some distance, including up/down stairs, and over rough terrain; places in ambulance with assistance of other personnel
Cleans and maintains station facilities, grounds, equipment, and apparatus
Establishes and maintains cooperative working relationships
Tactfully responds to requests and inquiries from the general public, other department personnel, and other City departments
Communicates clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing
Resolves a variety of situations characterized by conflict or danger
May perform duties of higher classification in an acting capacity as needed
Participates on department committees and attends staff meetings as required
Assists in providing public fire education
Provides fire station tours; presents information to students at local schools
Assists in developing and presenting a variety of training programs relative to fire suppression, prevention, operations and hazardous materials handling
Must learn streets and routes within the city of Carrollton and surrounding areas to include the location of medical facilities to ensure expeditious response times
Operates departmental computer equipment to review records, inquire about activities and programs and input various data
Assists with fire investigations as assigned
Attends scheduled training to maintain minimum required certification through continuing education as required by the Texas Commission on Fire Protection
Performs related duties as assigned

EQUIPMENT:

Operates numerous types of rescue, salvage, emergency and fire suppression equipment, including vehicles, hydraulic powered spreaders, cutters, rams, come-a-long, air chisel, air bags, ropes and pulleys
Operates firefighter hand tools including nozzle, ax, pry bar, fire hose, and ground ladders; common hand tools include wrenches, screwdrivers, and hammers
Operates power tools including exhaust fans, portable pump, chain saws, generators and air compressors
Operates departmental computer equipment to input and extract
May be exposed to harsh weather, poor or no lighting, exposure to hazardous chemicals, fire and smoke, extremes in temperature, electrical hazards, confined or high work places, dangerous animals, extreme noise, traffic, and natural and man made disasters
Works in areas where movement is restricted such as rescue from wrecked automobiles, underground excavations, structure collapse, etc.
Listens for victims at fire and accident scenes, communications from other firefighters, superiors, etc.
Wears full protective clothing and self-contained breathing apparatus, and must function fully in this limiting and heavy attire
May be exposed to human body fluids, infectious disease, victims of fire and accident scenes, bodies recovered from fire and accident scenes, etc.
Interprets and explains city and department policies and procedures for public
Works under stress and uses good judgment in emergency situations

TRAINING, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND CERTIFICATION:

Knowledge of fire suppression and prevention principles and practices, and emergency medical services
Knowledge of specialized communication equipment
Knowledge of safe work practices and procedures
Knowledge of operational characteristics , services and activities of a comprehensive fire suppression program
Knowledge of technical aspects of fire prevention and suppression including operation of fire hydrants, use of ladders, use of water and various chemicals to suppress fire, salvage and rescue operations
Knowledge of fire apparatus operations practices and principles
Knowledge of procedures and techniques involved in responding to and handling incidents involving hazardous materials
Knowledge of pertinent Federal, State and local codes and regulations
Exercises sound judgment and rational thinning under dangerous circumstances
Evaluates various options and alternatives and chooses an appropriate and reasonable course of action
Working knowledge of chemistry and hazardous materials
Skill in calculating engine pressures and friction losses of fire hose using mathematics and physics
Skill in operating two-way radio equipment
Must obtain Paramedic certification upon request and subsequently perform all essential functions of that assignment
Must obtain any and all certifications for all possible assignments and subsequently perform all essential functions of an assignment when assigned

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Must be on a certified and current eligibility list in accordance with Local Government Code Chapter 143 State Civil Service and City of Carrollton Local Rules
Must possess and maintain a valid Texas class “B” drivers license and meet all City policies regarding insurability; must pass annual MVR check
Must maintain necessary physical condition to carry out all essential functions of rank/assignment

title: College Preparatory Counselor
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Harlem Children’s Zone (HCZ) — a world-renowned education and poverty-fighting organization based in New York — seeks an enthusiastic, dedicated, and mission-aligned College Preparatory Program Counselor at our College Success Office.

The College Success Office provides year-round academic, administrative, and emotional support as well as financial and career preparation to participants of HCZ’s Promise Academy high schools and afterschool programs. Our mission is to ensure that our participants are provided with the resources and guidance needed to be successful in college and beyond. The main components of the College Success Office include student outreach, academic support and guidance, financial aid advisement, college transfer assistance, summer and winter internship opportunities, and community-building efforts within our program.

The College Preparatory Program Counselor will bring a passion for the mission of Harlem Children’s Zone: break the cycle of intergenerational poverty with comprehensive, on-the-ground programming that builds up opportunities for children and families to thrive in school, work, and life.

For more information, check out Want to Work at Harlem Children’s Zone? Here’s 7 Things You Need to Know

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in counseling, education, or a related field preferred.
  • 2+ years of experience in college counseling, advising, or a related field, preferably in a high school setting, is required.

Who you are

  • Passionate about college access and student success, with a strong commitment to helping high school scholars identify and pursue postsecondary opportunities that align with their goals.
  • A skilled counselor and trusted advisor who can build meaningful relationships with scholars and families while providing individualized guidance throughout the college preparation and application process.
  • A clear and engaging communicator who is comfortable facilitating workshops, presentations, and one-on-one conversations on college admissions, financial aid, scholarships, and academic planning.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple scholars, deadlines, applications, events, and priorities while maintaining accurate records.
  • You are a collaborative relationship-builder who can partner effectively with school teams, internal departments, college admissions representatives, scholarship organizations, and other external partners to expand opportunities for scholars.
  • Someone who is proactive and data-informed, using student progress and outcomes to identify needs, strengthen support, and continuously improve the college readiness experience.
  • You are deeply committed to HCZ’s values and mission and passionate about expanding educational opportunities for students from historically underserved urban communities, particularly first-generation college students and families navigating the college process.

What you'll do

  • Provide individualized college counseling to scholars in grades 9-12, helping them develop college readiness plans and navigate postsecondary opportunities.
  • Plan and facilitate college readiness workshops, presentations, and curriculum for scholars and families on topics including admissions, academic planning, standardized testing, financial aid, and scholarships.
  • Guide scholars through all aspects of the college application process, including college matching, application completion, essay review, interview preparation, and postsecondary decision-making.
  • Educate and support scholars and families throughout the financial aid process, including FAFSA and CSS Profile completion, scholarship applications, financial aid package review, and college affordability planning.
  • Coordinate college exposure opportunities, including college fairs, campus visits, pre-college programs, post-acceptance visits, and other activities that promote informed college selection.
  • Partner with school leadership and other HCZ departments (such as Wealth Builds) to support college readiness programming, standardized testing efforts, and successful college transitions.
  • Build and maintain relationships with college admissions representatives, scholarship providers, and other postsecondary partners to expand opportunities for scholars.
  • Maintain accurate student records and utilize data to monitor scholar progress, track admissions and enrollment outcomes, and inform program improvements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Schedule

  • Monday - Friday, schedule may vary (e.g., 10:00 am to 6:00 pm, or 11:00 am to 7:00 pm) based on scholar, site location, and program needs.
  • Some weekends and evenings, depending on site needs and events; occasional travels

Benefits

As a member of the Harlem Children's Zone team, you will join a supportive and inclusive community dedicated to helping children, families — and our staff — thrive. We offer highly competitive salaries, a comprehensive benefits package, and opportunities for growth.

Our exceptional full-time benefits include:

  • Highly competitive base salaries
  • Paid time off
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Career advancement
  • No-cost health insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Additional voluntary benefits
  • Wellness discounts
  • Commuter benefits
  • Financial wellness perks
  • Additional Benefits (Discounts on flights, hotels, theme parks, concert tickets, and more.)

We offer competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. The salary range is $60,000 to $70,000. To be considered, interested applicants should submit their applications directly through the posting. No telephone inquiries or recruiters, please. Replies will only be sent to qualified applicants. HCZ is an EOE.

  • Provide proof of all required vaccines. The Employer strongly recommends to “stay up to date” with the recommended vaccines. Vaccination requirements are subject to changes as determined by the Employer.

What do we offer you?

title: Maintenance & Facilities Supervisor
description:
SUMMARY
The Maintenance & Facilities Supervisor is responsible for overseeing maintenance activities for manufacturing equipment, facilities, utilities, tooling support systems, and preventative maintenance programs at Amphenol CDI's Cerritos manufacturing facility. The position leads maintenance personnel and coordinates repairs, equipment uptime initiatives, contractor activities, facility improvements, and asset reliability programs.

The Maintenance & Facilities Supervisor supports Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) compliance through execution of facility inspections, corrective actions, preventative maintenance programs, regulatory remediation activities, and equipment safety programs. This role partners with Human Resources, Operations, Quality, and company EHS resources to maintain a safe and compliant manufacturing environment.

The position supports a manufacturing operation that includes Swiss screw machines, CNC milling equipment, air compressor systems, soldering equipment, curing and bake ovens, facility utilities, and related production support equipment.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

Maintenance Leadership & Equipment Reliability

Supervise and lead maintenance technicians and facility support personnel.
Develop and execute preventative and predictive maintenance programs for production equipment and facility infrastructure.
Maintain high levels of equipment uptime and responsiveness to production needs.
Troubleshoot and coordinate repairs for manufacturing equipment, including:

Deco 10 Swiss machines
CNC milling machines
Air compressor systems
Soldering equipment
Small industrial ovens
Material handling equipment
Facility electrical and mechanical systems

Coordinate equipment installations, relocations, upgrades, and decommissioning activities.
Manage outside service providers and maintenance contractors.
Maintain maintenance records, work orders, spare parts inventory, and equipment documentation.

title: Building Inspection - Building Inspector
description:
GENERAL DEFINITION OF WORK
Performs technical and regulatory inspections of residential and commercial structures during construction, alteration, repair, and occupancy to ensure compliance with applicable building, fire safety, housing, zoning, and related codes. Reviews construction plans and specifications for conformance with adopted regulations; conducts field inspections to identify deficiencies; issues permit, notices of violation, and stop-work orders as necessary; and provides guidance to contractors, property owners, and the public regarding code requirements. Work is performed under general supervision with considerable independent judgment in the interpretation and application of codes and standards.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
include the following. Other duties may be assigned:

Determines whether plans for the structure comply with regulations.
The Building Inspector inspects new and existing structures to determine safety standards are met and notifies property owners if deficiencies are found. Issues Building permits.
Maintains a daily log of work inspected, permits issued, and violations issued. Maintains files including reports and photographs of projects.
Notifies contractor or building owner of violations giving guidelines for correcting the deficiency within a reasonably specified time.
Issues stop-work order if deficiencies are not corrected.
Support Building Inspections Department as assigned by the Chief Building and/or Planning Director.
Reliable attendance and punctuality are essential functions of this role

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the plans and documents.
Ability to respond effectively to the most sensitive inquiries or complaints.
Ability to express oneself clearly and concisely, orally and in writing.
General Knowledge of methods of building and construction.
Knowledge of drafting and math.
General knowledge of International Code, City Housing Codes and related inspections.
Ability to operate a computer system using various MS Office system programs.
Ability to operate computer based permitting programs.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to perform basic and intermediate mathematical calculations related to building construction and code compliance.
Ability to calculate dimensions, areas, volumes, loads, and ratios as required to verify compliance with building and safety codes.
Ability to calculate and verify permit fees, inspection fees, and valuation estimates in accordance with adopted fee schedules.
Ability to interpret scaled drawings and blueprints, including converting measurements and applying formulas accurately.

SOFTWARE SKILLS

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, for report writing, correspondence, scheduling, and recordkeeping.
Ability to use computer-based permitting, inspection, and code enforcement software systems for permit issuance, inspection tracking, and documentation of violations.
Ability to review and annotate digital plans, photographs, and inspection reports using electronic file management systems.
Basic proficiency with mobile devices or tablets for conducting field inspections, entering inspection data, and accessing code references remotely.
Ability to learn and adapt to new software systems and technologies used by the Building Inspections Department.

EDUCATION
High School Diploma or GED is required.
Associate’s degree from accredited college or technical school is strongly desired.
EXPERIENCE
Minimum 2 years of prior experience in building inspection, construction or closely related field is strongly desired.
OR
Equivalent combination of education and work experience in a related field.
CERTIFICATIONS
Must obtain certification in various approved Building International Code council classes: Individuals must obtain certification as a Residential Building Inspector, Residential Plumbing Inspector, Residential Mechanical Inspector, through the International Code Council within six (6) months of hire date: per TCA 68-120-113.
Must obtain certification in various approved Building International Code council classes: Individuals must obtain certification as a Commercial Building Inspector, Commercial Plumbing Inspector, Commercial Mechanical Inspector, through the International Code Council within twelve (12) months of hire date: per TCA 68-120-113.
DRIVER LICENSE
Must possess a valid Tennessee Driver's License with a clear driving record. Or ability to obtain TN driver's license within 30 days of hire.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS, WORK ENVIROMENT, REASONABLE ACCOMMADOTIONS
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to talk or hear. The employee is also required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to finger, and to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls. Visual acuity is required for preparing and analyzing written or computer data, visual inspection involving small defects and/or small parts, use of measuring devices, operation of motor vehicles, determining the accuracy and thoroughness of work and observing general surroundings and activities. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
The employee often uses hands and fingers to manipulate measuring devices or read and peruse job data sheets. Specific vision abilities required by this job include the ability to adjust focus and ability to read small blueprint materials. Physical demands consist of frequent standing, climbing, walking, lifting, bending, or stooping. May be required to lift and carry items weighing up to 50 pounds
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Most work is performed outdoors and requires ability to climb and move about construction sites. Some work is performed generally in an office environment using general office equipment. Frequent travel between City offices and job sites is required to conduct meetings and inspections. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate to loud. Attendance at council meetings, work sessions and other meetings may be required, as directed by the Chief Building Official, Planning Director or Executive Director of Engineering & Planning.
Reasonable accommodations shall be the responsibility of the City of Lebanon, Executive Director of Engineering & Planning to assess the type(s) of reasonable accommodations which may be necessary to allow the individual "to perform the essential functions of this role and to provide such necessary reasonable accommodations to a qualified individual with a disability, provided that nothing herein shall be construed to require the provision of reasonable accommodations if doing so will impose an undue hardship on the employing agency or a direct threat to the safety of himself/herself or others.

title: VDC Engineer
description:
Summary
Balfour Beatty is seeking a VDC Engineer to join our Carolinas team, based out of Raleigh . This role is ideal for a technically skilled, detail-oriented professional with hands-on experience in VDC/BIM modeling and coordination who is looking to grow their career within a collaborative, project-driven environment. This is a hands-on technical role, emphasizing modeling, coordination, and digital workflows. The role offers exposure to complex projects, evolving technologies, and opportunities for professional growth within Balfour Beatty’s digital delivery practice.
Essential Functions

Model Coordination: Support and facilitate multi-trade coordination and clash detection using Navisworks and Revit; assist with coordination meetings and model issue tracking.
VDC & BIM Support: Contribute to BIM execution planning, model logistics, and data management in alignment with company VDC standards and workflows (including R5 process).
Model Development: Create, update, and maintain architectural, structural, and MEP models at appropriate Levels of Development (LOD) through design and construction phases.
MEP & Trade Integration: Coordinate building systems with trade partners to identify and resolve conflicts and support constructability reviews.
Technology & Platform Support: Provide model-based support for documentation, coordination, and field use; assist teams with Procore and Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) workflows.
Quality & Accuracy: Perform model checks to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with construction documents and project standards.
Collaboration & Communication: Work collaboratively with project teams, designers, and subcontractors to support alignment, efficiency, and best practices in digital delivery.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
3+ of experience in VDC/BIM modeling and coordination within the construction industry.
Proficiency with Revit and Navisworks.
Working knowledge of Procore, AutoCAD, Bluebeam, and BIM 360 / ACC.
Experience supporting MEP coordination and understanding LOD requirements.
Ability to read and interpret construction documents, specifications, and shop drawings.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.

Preferred Experience

Experience coordinating large, complex, or multi-phase projects with multiple trades and stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to lead or independently manage multi-trade coordination efforts, including facilitating coordination or clash resolution discussions.
Experience contributing to or helping develop BIM execution plans, VDC standards, or project-specific workflows.
Exposure to preconstruction or design-assist modeling, including early coordination, constructability reviews, or model-based problem-solving.
Experience mentoring or supporting junior VDC/BIM staff, interns, or project team members.
Advanced Revit capabilities, such as family creation, content management, or model optimization.
Familiarity with lean construction principles, model-based coordination strategies, or digital delivery best practices.
Interest in expanding technical leadership, coordination ownership, or process improvement responsibilities over time.

Candidates who demonstrate strong technical ownership, coordination leadership, and process improvement capabilities may be considered for a senior-level engineer opportunity.
