description:
Keep Our Fleet Moving. Maintain Safety. Make an Impact.

At zTrip, the nation's largest taxi transportation company, our fleet is the foundation of our success. We're looking for a skilled and dependable Fleet Tech to help maintain, repair, and inspect vehicles so they remain safe, reliable, and ready for service.

If you're hands-on, mechanically inclined, and take pride in diagnosing and repairing vehicles, this is a great opportunity to build a long-term career with a growing transportation leader.

Benefits

  • Competitive Pay Based on Experience
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Paid Holidays
  • 401(k) with Company Match
  • Annual Tool Allowance
  • Paid Training and Development Opportunities
  • Career Advancement Opportunities
  • Stable, Year-Round Employment

What You'll Do as a Fleet Tech:

Maintenance & Repairs

  • Perform preventative maintenance and scheduled services on fleet vehicles.
  • Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and drivability issues.
  • Complete oil changes, brake repairs, tire services, and other routine maintenance.
  • Troubleshoot vehicle problems and perform effective repairs.
  • Identify potential issues before they lead to costly breakdowns.

Inspections & Safety

  • Conduct vehicle inspections to ensure safety and operational readiness.
  • Verify vehicles meet company and safety standards.
  • Document findings and recommend necessary repairs.
  • Ensure vehicles are road-ready before returning to service.

Fleet Support

  • Work closely with operations and maintenance teams to keep vehicles available and on the road.
  • Prioritize repairs to minimize downtime.
  • Assist with urgent vehicle repairs when needed.
  • Support overall fleet reliability and performance goals.

Shop Operations

  • Maintain accurate maintenance and repair records.
  • Keep the shop clean, organized, and safe.
  • Properly use and maintain tools and equipment.
  • Assist with parts inventory and shop organization.
  • Follow all company safety procedures and maintenance standards.

Qualifications of a Fleet Tech:

Preferred Experience

  • Experience as an Automotive Technician, Fleet Technician, Mechanic, Diesel Technician, or similar role.
  • Strong knowledge of vehicle maintenance and repair procedures.
  • Ability to diagnose and troubleshoot mechanical and electrical issues.
  • Experience working on fleet vehicles, commercial vehicles, vans, or light-duty trucks preferred.
  • Familiarity with diagnostic equipment and repair software.
  • ASE certifications are a plus but not required.
  • Valid driver's license required.

What Makes You Successful:

  • Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to quality work.
  • Dependable and safety-focused mindset.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong work ethic and positive attitude.
  • Commitment to keeping vehicles operating at peak performance.

Why Join zTrip?

  • Join the nation's largest taxi transportation company.
  • Work on a diverse and active fleet.
  • Receive ongoing training and support.
  • Enjoy long-term career stability and growth opportunities.
  • Be part of a team that values safety, reliability, and excellence.
  • Make a direct impact on the vehicles that keep our communities moving every day.

Apply Today

If you're a motivated technician who enjoys vehicle repair and maintenance, apply today to become a Fleet Tech with zTrip. Help keep our fleet safe, dependable, and ready to serve.

title: Finance Associate
description:
About Tetra Foundation

Tetra Foundation is a UK-based charity with a mission to transform Nigeria through maritime training. We provide scholarships that equip Nigerian youth with world-class vocational skills, enabling them to build international careers in the maritime industry. This initiative aims to transform not only individual lives but also the prospects of communities and the nation as a whole.

The Foundation was established by Union Maritime, one of the UK’s largest shipowners. Since its inception in 2006, Union Maritime has grown into a leading global operator with significant operations in Nigeria. It also manages Goodwork Crewing—the largest private Nigerian crewing agent—employing over 1,000 Nigerian seafarers. This experience gives us unique insight into both the challenges and opportunities facing Nigeria’s youth, forming the foundation for our transformational mission.

Role Definition: Finance Associate

We are seeking an experienced Finance Associate who will oversee the Foundation's day-to-day financial operations while helping design and implement a best-practice finance function. You will work closely with Foundation leadership, donors, trustees, programme teams, and external service providers to ensure transparency, financial control, and effective stewardship of charitable funds.

A key aspect of the role will be reviewing and mapping existing financial processes across the Foundation, its donors, and service providers, and creating a new unified operating model that improves efficiency, accountability, and reporting.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Map existing finance processes across the Foundation, donors, and service providers.
  • Develop and implement a unified finance operating model, including policies and controls.
  • Manage and reconcile all incoming donations, grants, and funding received by the Foundation.
  • Prepare monthly financial reports, budget tracking, and variance analysis.
  • Develop and maintain cashflow forecasts and financial projections.
  • Oversee invoicing, payments, and accounts receivable/payable activities.
  • Design and implement a new restricted funding process for future donations.
  • Monitor and report on restricted and unrestricted funding.
  • Support budgeting, annual planning, audit preparation, and financial compliance requirements.
  • Provide financial insights and recommendations to support strategic decision-making.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field.
  • Part-qualified or qualified accountant (ACCA, ACA, CIMA, or equivalent) preferred.
  • 3+ years of experience in finance, accounting, FP&A, or charity finance.
  • Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, cashflow management, and financial reporting.
  • Experience managing donor funding, grants, or restricted funds is desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve and streamline financial processes.
  • Strong analytical and financial modelling skills.
  • Advanced Excel skills and familiarity with accounting systems.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management abilities.
  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced, growing organisation.

Desirable

  • Experience within a charity, foundation, not-for-profit, or donor-funded environment.
  • Knowledge of UK charity finance and restricted fund accounting.
  • Experience supporting audits, governance, and finance transformation projects.

title: School Psychologist
description:
School Psychologist – School-Based

Caldwell, Idaho | Full-Time | 2026–2027 School Year | On-Site

TheraPeds Partners is seeking a dedicated School Psychologist to join our team for a full-time, school-based opportunity in Caldwell, Idaho for the 2026–2027 school year.

About Us

TheraPeds Partners is a therapist-owned and operated team of special education providers who partner with schools to provide special education and related services to students nationwide. We understand the education process, IDEA requirements, and the importance of collaboration within multidisciplinary teams. Our mission is to deliver high-quality services while building meaningful connections in a collaborative learning environment.

This position serves students and includes evaluations, consultation, eligibility and diagnostic services, and student support. You'll work collaboratively with educators, families, administrators, and multidisciplinary team members, with support from both the school district and TheraPeds Partners.

Position Details

  • Full-time: 37.5 hours per week
  • School year: 2026–2027, August through May/June
  • Grades: High School
  • Location: Caldwell, Idaho
  • Setting: On-site, in-person
  • Pay: $55–$65+/hour, based on experience and employment arrangement
  • Guaranteed hours, including designated documentation, administrative, and planning time
  • Manageable caseload
  • Dual support from the school district and TheraPeds Partners

What You'll Do

As a school-based School Psychologist, you'll support students' academic, behavioral, social, and emotional needs while helping multidisciplinary teams make informed educational decisions.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Conducting comprehensive psychoeducational evaluations and assessments
  • Participating in referral, evaluation, eligibility, reevaluation, and diagnostic processes
  • Interpreting assessment results and preparing comprehensive written reports
  • Participating in the development and implementation of IEPs
  • Providing consultation to teachers, administrators, families, and other school professionals
  • Supporting students in accordance with their IEPs and identified educational needs
  • Participating in eligibility, IEP, multidisciplinary, and problem-solving team meetings
  • Providing student services and interventions within the scope of the position
  • Collaborating with special education teams, general education staff, related-service providers, and families
  • Maintaining accurate and timely documentation
  • Supporting compliance with IDEA, district procedures, and applicable state and federal special education requirements

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Master's degree or higher in School Psychology
  • Active or eligible for the appropriate Idaho School Psychologist credential/certification
  • NASP/NCSP credential preferred, but not required
  • Two or more years of school psychology experience preferred, but not required
  • Knowledge of psychoeducational assessment, counseling, consultation, and special education eligibility processes
  • Experience working with children and adolescents
  • Understanding of IDEA, IEPs, and multidisciplinary special education practices
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills
  • Proficiency with technology used for assessment, documentation, and communication
  • Ability to successfully complete required fingerprinting and background clearances
  • Ability to collaborate professionally with students, families, educators, administrators, and related-service professionals
  • Professionalism, discretion, and respect for student and family confidentiality

Physical Requirements

School-based services require participation in a variety of educational environments. The School Psychologist must be able to perform the physical functions necessary to fulfill assigned responsibilities, which may include sitting, standing, walking, bending, reaching, transitioning between school environments, and engaging with students in various educational settings.

All responsibilities will be performed in accordance with assigned duties, district safety requirements, and applicable accommodations.

Benefits

Compensation & Benefits

Benefits and compensation are based on employment classification and eligibility.

W-2 employees may be eligible for:

  • Competitive hourly compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • 401(k)
  • Guaranteed hours
  • Professional development and continuing education opportunities
  • Ongoing clinical and administrative support
  • Access to the TheraPeds professional community

1099 independent contractor opportunities may include:

  • Competitive contract rates
  • Benefit Resources
  • Flexibility associated with independent contractor status
  • Access to professional and administrative resources through TheraPeds Partners
  • Guaranteed hours
  • Professional development and continuing education opportunities
  • Ongoing clinical and administrative support
  • Access to the TheraPeds professional community

Specific compensation, benefits, and terms will be outlined in the applicable employment or independent contractor agreement.

Why TheraPeds Partners?

At TheraPeds Partners, we believe school-based professionals do their best work when they feel supported, valued, and connected to the teams they serve.

As a therapist-owned organization, we understand the realities of working in school-based practice. Our goal is to create strong partnerships between professionals and schools while providing the clinical and administrative support needed for both students and providers to succeed.

If you're a Certified School Psychologist looking for a full-time school-based position, we'd love to connect wtih you

title: Quality Auditor (Nights)
description:
Summary
Delta Star Inc. is seeking a detail-oriented and professional Quality Auditor to ensure product quality, compliance, and customer satisfaction throughout the manufacturing of power and mobile transformers. This role combines hands-on inspection, process auditing, and customer-facing responsibilities. As a key representative of the company, you’ll frequently host customers during plant visits, product inspections, and progress reviews, making professionalism and customer service essential to success.
What You’ll Do
As a Quality Auditor, you’ll verify product quality through in-process and final inspections of electrical and mechanical components, ensuring conformance to engineering specifications. You’ll promote and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS) in compliance with ISO 9001:2015, document inspection results, and oversee corrective actions for non-conformances. You’ll also serve as a point of contact for customers during inspections, providing clear communication and a positive experience.
A Day in the Life
Your day may begin on the shop floor, conducting inspections and using precision measurement tools to confirm components meet specifications. You’ll record results, flag non-conforming materials, and collaborate with production, engineering, and management teams to resolve issues and prevent recurrence.
Throughout the day, you’ll host customer visits, guide product reviews, and present inspection results in a professional and confident manner. You’ll also participate in internal audits, assist with root cause analysis, and contribute to corrective action planning. Maintaining calibrated measuring equipment, supporting employee training on quality requirements, and occasionally traveling to customer or supplier sites will round out your responsibilities.
What We’re Looking For
The ideal candidate will have experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment with strong skills in inspection, blueprint reading, and customer communication. You should be detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working independently, while also collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams. Professionalism and customer service are key, as you’ll often represent the company directly to clients.

The Principal, IT & Cyber GRC is the seasoned generalist and trusted advisor across Questrade Financial Group’s (QFG) IT & Cyber GRC function. The role bridges governance, risk, and control intent with operational execution by partnering with IT, Cybersecurity, and business teams to ensure that "built-in" security and compliance is practical, proportionate, and audit-defensible. The Principal brings deep subject matter expertise to this work and partners with the Manager on framework accountability, novel control architecture, and regulatory interpretation.
The Principal, IT & Cyber GRC is a champion for putting the customer first and has a deep passion in understanding customer behaviour. Governance, Policy, and Regulatory Strategy

Governance Documentation Lead: Lead the periodic review and update cycle for Technology and Cyber Governance documents (policies, standards, procedures, frameworks, and handbooks), ensuring they remain accurate, aligned with legislative changes, regulatory requirements, consistent with the relevant frameworks, and reflective of the constantly evolving technology landscape.
Audit & Regulatory Management: Support all audit engagements (OSFI, CIRO, SOC 1, SOC 2, etc.) and perform quality-control vetting of materials to ensure a successful "audit-ready" posture.
Compliance Initiatives: Drive initiatives including gap assessments for new and existing policies against evolving industry requirements.

Control Advisory & Risk Partnership

Horizon Scanning: Maintain a forward-looking understanding of GRC practices and emerging threats to proactively manage risk. Perform analysis and support the issuance of communications to inform of organizational impact.
Innovative Monitoring: Identify opportunities to streamline processes through innovative solutions and automation logic.
Tabletop Facilitation: Coordinate and facilitate the execution of cybersecurity tabletop and simulation exercises designed by partner teams — managing scheduling, participant readiness, exercise delivery, and post-exercise documentation and remediation tracking.

Risk Assessment

Entity-Level Risk Assessments: Perform and support entity-level risk assessments across QFG’s regulated entities — identifying systemic risk exposures specific to each entity, assessing control sufficiency against entity-specific regulatory requirements, and partnering with the Manager and entity leadership on remediation roadmaps.
Agile Problem Solving: Take ownership of ad-hoc, high-priority activities emerging from a dynamic threat landscape.

Mentorship, Metrics & Technical Guidance

Strategic Mentorship & Coaching: Provide technical and craft-level coaching to the Business Analyst and Risk & Control Analyst — reviewing work product, modelling professional skepticism, and raising the quality bar of the team through peer review. This is a technical mentorship relationship, not a people-leadership role; formal performance management remains with the Manager.
Metrics Stewardship: Curate and quality-review IT & Cyber Risk metrics (KRIs/KPIs), ensuring the numbers, narratives, and visualizations that reach executive audiences are accurate, well-contextualized, and actionable.
Automation & AI Vision: Champion and curate the team’s use of AI and automation — setting practical standards for prompt engineering, output validation, and human review — to keep tooling and AI integrations aligned with GRC objectives.

title: Product Engineer / Special Projects
description:
JOB TITLE Product Engineer / Special Projects

The Product Engineer / Special Projects Engineer serves a dual-role function combining customer-focused product engineering responsibilities with strategic coordination of critical special projects. This position is responsible for collaborating directly with aerospace customers on bearing design, application support, qualification activities, and technical issue resolution while also leading cross-functional initiatives within the factory to address material obsolescence, process discontinuations, regulatory changes, and supply chain risks.

The ideal candidate possesses strong engineering fundamentals, project management capabilities, and the ability to effectively communicate with customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to ensure product performance, regulatory compliance, and uninterrupted manufacturing operations.

Key Responsibilities

Product Engineering & Customer Support

  • Serve as the primary technical interface for customers regarding plain bearing design, application requirements, and product performance.
  • Collaborate with customers to develop bearing solutions that meet functional, environmental, regulatory, and manufacturing requirements.
  • Review customer drawings, specifications, and technical requirements to ensure manufacturability and compliance.
  • Support new product introduction (NPI) activities including design reviews, qualification testing, and first article approvals.
  • Prepare technical documentation, engineering reports, specifications, and customer presentations.
  • Investigate product performance issues and engage root cause analysis and corrective action activities.
  • Provide engineering support to manufacturing, quality, sales, and supply chain teams.
  • Participate in customer meetings, audits, and technical reviews as required.
  • Evaluate design changes and process modifications for impact on product performance, qualification status, and customer approvals.

Special Projects Leadership

  • Lead strategic projects involving material obsolescence, supplier discontinuations, process changes, and regulatory compliance requirements.
  • Identify and assess risks associated with discontinued raw materials, coatings, lubricants, chemicals, and manufacturing processes.
  • Develop qualification plans and validation strategies for replacement materials and processes.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams including Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Compliance, and Program Management.
  • Manage project schedules, milestones, budgets, and customer communications to ensure successful implementation.
  • Interface with suppliers to evaluate alternative materials, manufacturing technologies, and process capabilities.
  • Drive qualification and certification activities necessary to maintain aerospace approvals and customer requirements.
  • Monitor industry and regulatory developments that may impact materials, processes, or product compliance.
  • Develop mitigation plans to minimize operational disruption and customer impact resulting from obsolescence events.

Job Skills & Abilities:

  • Proficient with computer design systems (Solidworks, CAD) and Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.).
  • Ability to work independently to complete projects and assignments
  • Excellent Attention to Detail
  • Self-starter with team mentality
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills with employees at all levels; Ability to interface and build professional and cooperative relationships with the customer and external partners on behalf of NHBB
  • Creative problem-solver, with the ability to make timely decisions with consideration for both the customer and NHBB’s interests

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelors’ Degree in Engineering
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience in Design Engineering or closely related field

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people assigned to this classification. They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified.

title: Reservations Supervisor
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
Our client is an award-winning, family-owned luxury cruise line that has spent more than two decades quietly redefining small-ship travel. Their yachts carry roughly one hundred guests, which changes everything: crew learn names, guests come back year after year and ask for people by name, and the experience is built around the individual rather than the itinerary. The fleet is growing and a new commercial office is opening in West Palm Beach, so this is the rare chance to join an established luxury brand at the beginning of a new chapter.

They are hiring a Reservations Supervisor to lead the team in the new West Palm Beach office. This is a genuine leadership seat with room above it, not a senior agent title.

What you will do

  • Lead the day to day reservations operation, including coverage, scheduling and service standards across US and overseas team members
  • Coach the team on consultative selling, not order taking. Guests here are choosing between a yacht and a villa, and the conversation matters
  • Own the numbers: conversion, call and email response times, booking value and service levels, and report on them credibly
  • Handle the bookings that need a steady hand, including VIPs, repeat guests, travel advisor escalations and anything complicated
  • Tighten the process. Find the manual steps, the reporting gaps and the automation nobody has built yet, and fix them
  • Partner with Sales, Revenue Management and the onboard team so what is promised ashore is what happens on board
  • Hire, onboard and develop the team as the office and the fleet expand

What we are looking for

  • Supervisory or team lead experience in reservations, guest services, front office or a travel contact centre, ideally in luxury hospitality or luxury travel
  • A luxury service instinct. Five-star hotel, private club, yacht, villa, resort or luxury travel background all translate directly
  • Comfort with reporting and systems. You should like a dashboard, not tolerate one, and be strong in Excel and on a reservations or property management platform
  • Experience coaching people to a standard rather than simply managing a queue
  • Excellent written and spoken communication, and the judgment to know which is which
  • A second language is a plus, as is experience with overseas or remote team members

Why people take this job

Small-ship luxury is a different business from mass-market cruise. Roughly a hundred guests a voyage means fewer transactions handled with more care, and repeat bookings that prove it. You are joining as the office is being built, so how this function works is largely going to be how you decide it works.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Short- and long-term disability, life, and long-term care coverage
  • Paid time off, including vacation, sick and personal days, company holidays, floating holidays, and bereavement leave
  • 2 Weeks of yachting for you and a companion, per year
  • Friends and family sailing rates after six months of employment

title: Post-Doctoral Fellow – Montaner Lab (NK Immunotherapy)
description:
The Wistar Institute has an opening for a highly motivated Post-Doctoral Fellow to join the laboratory of Dr. Luis Montaner in the HIV Cure and Viral Diseases Center focused on advancing NK-based immunotherapy strategies. The Montaner lab combines virological and immune system-based research through long-standing community partnerships and clinical trials research, along with using laboratory models of virus infection.
The laboratory focuses on:

Regulation of NK and innate immunity.
Exploring interface between persistence of HIV reservoirs and immune detection.
Developing strategies for control of HIV-1 infection.

Further details on the Montaner Laboratory can be viewed on our website: https://www.wistar.org/our-scientists/luis-montaner/
Candidates should have a PhD or equivalent with a strong background in NK biology, HIV virology, cellular immunology, and molecular/cellular biology. Experience with bioinformatics, microscopy, and flow cytometry is a plus.
The Wistar Institute is a world leader in early-stage discovery science in the areas of cancer, immunology, and infectious disease with two large programs directed towards advancing an HIV cure (see beat-hiv.org, icure-hiv.org). Wistar is committed to accelerating research advances from bench to bedside through brilliant science and distinctive approaches to collaboration among scientific investigators and academic and industry partners.
The Wistar Institute is located in the University City area of Philadelphia, in the heart of the University of Pennsylvania Campus. Wistar provides resources to its faculty and staff that enable them to conduct cutting edge collaborative research and provides for outstanding intellectual environments and state-of-the-art facilities.
We offer a competitive salary and excellent benefits package.
For more information about The Wistar Institute visit our website at www.wistar.org.

title: Travel & Licensing Coordinator
description:
Position Summary

Hays Electrical Services is seeking a Travel & Licensing Coordinator to manage company travel arrangements and support electrical contractor licensing and permitting across multiple states and municipalities. This role requires someone highly organized, dependable, and resourceful, able to manage competing deadlines, exercise sound judgment, and communicate confidently with employees, vendors, and government agencies. Experience with corporate travel, licensing/permitting, construction, electrical contracting, property or housing coordination, or administrative operations is a plus; prior experience in both Travel and Licensing is not required.

Travel Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and book employee business travel, including airfare, hotels, rental vehicles, and ground transportation.
  • Monitor the Travel inbox and manage new requests, changes, cancellations, and time-sensitive travel needs.
  • Coordinate onboarding, project-related, and other company travel.
  • Assist with temporary and extended-stay housing, including hotels, apartments, and other accommodations.
  • Track housing dates, extensions, lease terms, move-ins, move-outs, and project-related housing needs.
  • Maintain accurate travel confirmations, itineraries, receipts, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with travel invoices, credits, refunds, reconciliation, and expense documentation.
  • Communicate company travel and housing policies and ensure requests are handled within established guidelines.
  • Work directly with airlines, hotels, rental car companies, property managers, and other vendors to resolve issues.
  • Assist travelers with disruptions or emergencies and identify solutions quickly while remaining cost-conscious.

Licensing & Permitting Responsibilities

  • Assist with obtaining and maintaining electrical contractor licenses, business licenses, registrations, and permits across multiple states and municipalities.
  • Prepare and submit applications, renewals, registrations, and required supporting documentation.
  • Track expiration and renewal dates and proactively address upcoming deadlines.
  • Communicate directly with state licensing boards, municipalities, permitting offices, and other government agencies.
  • Research licensing, registration, and permitting requirements for new jurisdictions and projects.
  • Follow up consistently on pending applications and work through delays, missing requirements, or other issues.
  • Coordinate with internal departments to obtain required signatures, insurance certificates, corporate documents, financial information, and other supporting materials.
  • Maintain accurate and organized records of licenses, permits, applications, fees, correspondence, and supporting documentation.

Schedule & After-Hours Expectations

The Travel function operates 24/7, so this position requires some after-hours availability. Nights, weekends, and holidays are reserved for emergencies only — routine travel requests, bookings, licensing work, and administrative responsibilities are handled during normal business hours.
The person in this role must be able to respond when a legitimate travel emergency occurs after hours, such as a flight cancellation, stranded traveler, hotel issue, transportation issue, or other unexpected disruption requiring immediate assistance.

What We're Looking For

We need someone who is highly organized, dependable, responsive, resourceful, and persistent, with strong follow-through and attention to detail. This person should be able to:
  • Manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Work independently and take ownership of assigned responsibilities without requiring constant direction.
  • Exercise good judgment and know when an issue needs to be escalated.
  • Communicate professionally and confidently with employees at all levels, vendors, and government agencies.
  • Be comfortable picking up the phone and following up until an issue is resolved.
  • Handle confidential employee and company information appropriately.
  • Follow and consistently apply established company policies.
  • Remain calm and solution-oriented when dealing with urgent travel situations or last-minute changes.
  • Be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly.

Preferred Experience

Experience with corporate travel, licensing/permitting, construction, electrical contracting, property/housing coordination, or administrative operations is a plus. Experience in both Travel and Licensing is not required.

title: Product Manager
description:
About us:

Napa Home & Garden is a wholesale home décor brand headquartered in Norcross, GA, and one in a family of highly regarded brands under C&F Enterprises. We design and source seasonal collections — furniture, décor, botanicals, and lifestyle accessories — for style-conscious independent retailers, designers, and specialty stores across North America.

Job Purpose:

Napa Home & Garden is evolving from a traditional buying organization into a strategic merchandising powerhouse — and we're looking for a Product Manager who thinks like a business owner, not just a purchaser. If you've built category strategy, owned a P&L, or driven growth through a blend of data and design instinct — in home, retail, or CPG brand management — this is a chance to bring that discipline to a design-forward wholesale brand at a real inflection point.

What You'll Own

  • Category strategy & assortment. Build 1 to 3-year category strategies grounded in consumer insight, trend data, and competitive intelligence. Execute the strategy into assortments that balance newness with core performance.
  • Brand & collection strategy. Give each seasonal collection a clear point of view and competitive position. The story carries through line sheets, look books, trade show presentations, and catalog/digital content. Partnering with Design and Marketing on execution.
  • The P&L. Own sales, margin, turns, and forecast for your categories. Build the launch business case and conduct post-launch performance analysis.
  • Product development partnership. Work with Design from concept through commercialization, writing product briefs that reflect real market opportunity and evaluating commercial viability at every stage. Execute a clear stage gate process, business case, samples, launch, post launch review, so all new introductions are evaluated and measured.
  • Vendor negotiation. Lead negotiations on cost, terms, MOQs, and exclusivity; build the global supplier relationships that give Napa a lasting competitive edge.
  • Cross-functional influence. Present category performance and strategy to senior leadership, and build alignment across Planning, Sales, Marketing, and Operations to launch products on time and on strategy.

Qualifications

  • 5–8 years in Buying, Merchandising, Category Management, Product Management, or Brand Management, with real accountability for a category.
  • Demonstrated experience owning brand positioning, product strategy, or go-to-market product launches.
  • A track record of turning data and consumer insight into commercial decisions, using trends, forecasting, POS data and competitive audits.
  • Strong analytical and Excel skills; comfort with ERP, PLM, or BI tools a plus.
  • A sharp eye for design and an instinct for what makes a product sell.
  • The confidence to challenge assumptions and the collaboration skills to bring people along with you.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Merchandising or related field or equivalent experience.

Bonus points: experience in home décor, furnishings, or lifestyle categories; international sourcing exposure; or a background bridging brand strategy with commercial execution.

Why Napa, Why Now

  • Own categories with real growth.
  • Help build Napa's merchandising playbook from the ground up, alongside new leadership.
  • Work inside a growing, design-driven brand backed by a stable family of companies.
  • Partner directly with senior leadership. Your work will be visible.

Physical requirements

  • Sitting, Standing, Walking
  • Prolonged use of computer involved; use of hands and finger coordination; specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision. Color vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus as needed.
  • Twice a year during Market periods, standing and walking for 8-12 hours each day

Benefits:

  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Employee assistance program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Health savings account
  • 401(k) and 401(k) matching
  • Company paid life insurance and long-term disability insurance
  • Voluntary Life Insurance
  • Voluntary Short-Term Disability
  • Paid time off

We engage, inform, and inspire people to learn about this historic capital, the events that occurred here, and the diverse peoples who helped shape a new nation.

title: Project Manager, Finance Transformation
description:
The Finance Transformation Project Manager leads and executes the systems and process transformation initiatives run out of the Office of the CFO. The role requires strategic planning, stakeholder management, and disciplined delivery of projects that align with the CFO's transformation agenda and the broader goals of the Rohit Group. The Project Manager oversees the full project lifecycle across finance systems and process change, driving efficiency, control, and digital enablement, and is responsible for planning, organizing, resourcing, and directing each project so that it meets its intended goals on time, on budget, and within scope and quality.

The Portfolio You Will Lead

Representative projects and the outcomes this role is accountable for delivering are below. The mix will evolve:

Project

What it is

Residential IPP Accounting Technology Transformation

Redesign of residential income producing properties accounting processes and controls, current to future state.

Finance Portal

A digital portal for internal and external self-serve reporting.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Project Management and Execution

  • Act as and model the behaviours of an exemplary project manager in leading all project management activities.
  • Lead delivery of finance systems and process transformation initiatives, including ERP, document management, reporting, and analytics solutions, within a complex multi-division structure.
  • Manage end-to-end delivery lifecycles, from gathering business requirements and defining roadmaps through execution, go-live, and post-implementation support.
  • Review and manage feasibility assessments, current and future-state process designs, solution designs, and design documentation.
  • Manage, monitor, and report milestone status through detailed plans and schedules, ensuring each project is on budget, on schedule, and within the defined scope and quality.
  • Identify risks, dependencies, and mitigation strategies, and manage them to closure to keep delivery on track.

Stakeholder and Change Management

  • Build trusted, customer-focused relationships across finance and the divisions; align teams to shared goals; raise issues; and schedule and facilitate the working and steering sessions that keep projects moving.
  • Act as the liaison between technical and solution-design teams and senior leadership, ensuring solutions align with strategic business and finance needs.
  • Develop and execute change management strategies, including stakeholder engagement, training, and communication plans that drive adoption of new systems and processes.
  • Guide teams through change and uncertainty, managing the people side of transformation alongside the technical delivery.

Technology and Innovation Leadership

  • Evaluate, recommend, and deliver finance technology initiatives (ERP such as Dynamics 365, document management and SharePoint, Power BI and Fabric analytics) to strengthen decision-making and operational efficiency.
  • Direct data integration, business intelligence, automation, and financial reporting initiatives that enhance the finance function's capabilities.
  • Provide informed technical input to guidelines and standards, working with solution-design teams to keep solutions fit for purpose.

Performance and Continuous Improvement

  • Establish project KPIs, track performance, and report progress to finance and enterprise leadership.
  • Optimize project management methodologies to improve efficiency, reduce cost, and streamline finance processes.
  • Conduct post-implementation reviews to assess impact and identify opportunities for enhancement and scalability.

This role requires a strategic mindset, stakeholder excellence, and technical fluency to manage and deliver the projects that advance the CFO's transformation agenda.

Key Accountabilities:

  • Release and deployment management: manage the release schedule, plan and execute deployments and cutovers, collaborate with stakeholders, ensure the agreed scope is delivered, and maintain risk-mitigation plans.
  • Processes and procedures: develop, execute, and continuously improve delivery and lifecycle-management processes and procedures for the transformation office.
  • Maintain approved project budgets, business cases, and benefits-realization documentation.
  • Develop detailed project plans and track progress against schedules, reporting variances early.

Essential Skills and Core Competencies:

Technical and Business Skills

  • Strong understanding of finance systems, ERP, data platforms, automation, and emerging technology relevant to a modern finance function.
  • Expertise in Agile, Scrum, and Waterfall project management methodologies.
  • Ability to analyze business and finance processes and align technology solutions to improve efficiency and control.
  • Proficiency in project management tools such as MS Project, Asana, Azure DevOps, or JIRA.

Leadership and Communication

  • Ability to drive change in a complex, multi-division environment.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills for engaging executives, finance teams, and vendors.
  • Negotiation and conflict-resolution skills to manage project challenges and hold stakeholders to commitments.

Problem-Solving and Decision Making

  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to navigate roadblocks.
  • Ability to make informed decisions under pressure while balancing multiple priorities.

Collaboration and Adaptability

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with finance, IT, the divisions, and external partners.
  • Flexibility to adapt to changing technology and business needs.

Travel:

  • Occasional local travel to Rohit offices, project sites, or vendor locations, approximately 10%.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Systems or Technology, Finance, Accounting, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. (Required)
  • PMP or equivalent project management certification. (Preferred)

Work Experience:

  • Leading systems and process transformation projects, with 10 or more years of experience. (Required)
  • Project planning, scheduling, budgeting, risk management, and governance. (Advanced)
  • Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid delivery methodologies and project management tools. (Advanced)
  • Stakeholder, vendor, communication, and change management. (Advanced)
  • ERP or finance systems implementation and process re-engineering. (Advanced)
  • Finance, accounting, or real estate domain experience. (Asset)

title: CNC Spring Up
description:
Position Summary:
Performs operation to prepare and spring up frames and/or sub assemblies for upholstered and exposed wood frames. Works on a variety of models as assigned performing preparation, changing set-ups, springing and tying off if required for correct sprung frame or sub assembly. Check the assembly, spring up and frame for level performing all duties necessary to ensure completion of work is to quantity and quality standards.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Roll built frame to work station (roll conveyor/skid or buggy)

Read frame ticket to see what is specified to be used in frame in regards to type of spring.

Clip all rails that require nosag clips. Install proper nosag springs into clips. Beat clips shut w/ hammer and shoot w/ clip gun to secure. Attach tie wire w/ clinch gun then cover springs w/ spring cover material.

Install propex or cardboard to in arms/ corners of frame – attach w/ staple gun.

Place spring units at station by spring clerk, spring up then installs correct springs into frame using a screw gun after attaching the spring insulator pad (if required). Springs are then covered w/ spring cover using a staple gun.

Roll/push the job off their line on the roller conveyor or slide the sprung frame to line-up.

Perform other duties/ special or non-routine assignments as instructed.

High School diploma or equivalent
Ability to read and follow directions (verbal and written).
Basic math skills: counting, adding, subtracting.
Must be open to cross training as needed
Must be able to work closely with team members
Teamwork/Communication is a must
Eye to hand coordination is a must
Must be able to complete job duties in timely manner
Ability to pay close attention to details
Effective verbal communication skills
Excellent attendance record and must maintain attendance
Ability to work and make decisions with minimum supervision
Overtime as required, including possible Saturday work as needed
Work standing/walking 8-9 hrs. a day
Must learn to read the frame ticket for appropriate spring applications

title: Beverage Director
location: New York, New York, United States
description:

Union Square Cafe—the flagship business that launched Danny Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group—has been one of the country’s most beloved restaurants for over 40 years. Who you are:

The Beverage Director is responsible for ensuring the excellence, creativity, brand promise, and profitability of the bar and beverage programs within the restaurant. You serve as a leader, educator, coach and mentor to the Bar and Service Teams by inspiring and teaching skills that will elevate the core values and mission of USHG. You work with Senior leadership to make decisions that impact the financial health of the business and do so in a way that is aligned with the culture and policies of the company.

What you’ll do:

  • Cultivate a culture of Enlightened Hospitality for all stakeholders that supports our business objectives and growth
  • Partner with the management team to lead the service staff in ensuring that USHG provides unparalleled hospitality for every guest
  • Endlessly look for opportunities for Beverage to open doors to Hospitality and dialogue between guests and businesses
  • Guide teams in discovering ways to ‘find the yes’ for guests in a manner that upholds the integrity of USHG operations
  • Use Beverage to actively drive cover counts and introduce new guests to our brand as well as encouraging existing guests to return
  • Consistently looks for internal and external opportunities to build our growing team
  • Fosters a positive, collaborative work environment for both the service and kitchen teams, ensuring clear communication at all times
  • Educate the Service Team on the beer, spirits, cocktail, and non-alcoholic beverage offerings for all beverage within the restaurant in a way that adds quality and value as well as enhancing guest experience while achieving and surpassing financial goals
  • Ensure that all end-of-period reports, inventories, and forecasts are completed accurately and on time
  • Ensure that all beverage changes are executed properly with necessary communication and with education in mind
  • Ensure that all POS systems, inventory systems, beverage lists and any other information related to the selling of beverage are understood by the team and remain accurate and up to date
  • Maintain key relationships with other beverage / wine managers and directors across USHG. Show commitment to sharing best practices and learning from a family of professionals
  • Perform all due diligence, utilize strategy and exercise exceptional judgment in order to ensure we are getting the best possible product for the most advantageous price possible

What we need from you:

  • 3+ years of restaurant beverage management experience
  • Excellent Beverage knowledge – including beer, wine and spirits
  • Excellent understanding of beverage inventory and cost management
  • Excellent knowledge of restaurant service team roles
  • Strong communication and people management skills

What you’ll get from us:

At Union Square Hospitality Group, we believe our people are our greatest ingredient. Joining our team means becoming part of a culture rooted in care, creativity, and growth. As a Beverage Director, you’ll enjoy:

  • Competitive pay and bonus potential: Annual compensation of $90,000 - $105,000 plus eligibility for a performance-based bonus, with consideration for your experience and impact

  • Time to recharge: Generous paid time off and paid parental leave to support life outside of work

  • Hospitality perks: Annual dining credit and a 51% dining discount across the entire USHG family of restaurants
  • Convenience & flexibility: Pre-tax commuter benefits for transit and parking
  • Growth and community: Opportunities for learning, mentorship, and collaboration with some of the most passionate people in hospitality.

Putting Enlightened Hospitality into Practice

Integral to our culture are our six behaviors. Our behaviors guide how we work together.

  • We play to win with humble swagger. Hospitality is a team sport where everyone deserves an opportunity to thrive and belong
  • Turn over the rocks and always be connecting dots to build uplifting experiences and relationships

  • Write a great next chapter. The road to success is paved with mistakes well-handled

title: Dockmaster
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Dockmaster is a senior waterfront operations position responsible for the safe planning, coordination, and execution of vessel docking, undocking, movement, berthing, drydock operations, and related waterfront activities at Hanwha Philly Shipyard (HPSI).

The position requires significant practical experience in shipyard docking and waterfront operations, including drydock preparation, docking plans, blocking and shoring arrangements, vessel movements, line handling, tug coordination, and management of personnel and resources involved in critical vessel evolutions.

In addition to supporting HPSI's current commercial and government vessel operations, this position will play a key role in developing HPSI's capabilities for future U.S. Navy and NAVSEA-regulated docking operations. The successful candidate is required to hold experience in NAVSEA-regulated docking operations at the time of hire; however, the individual should possess the experience, technical knowledge, and leadership capability necessary to support development of the shipyard's docking program toward applicable NAVSEA requirements when required by future contracts or operations.

The Dockmaster works closely with Operations, Production, Engineering, Planning, HSE, Fire & Emergency Services, Security, Project Management, shipwrights, waterfront personnel, tug operators, contractors, vessel representatives, and government/customer representatives.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

· Work to ensure that everyone inside the shipyard is safe and performing their work in accordance with HPSI’s core principles.

·Ensure that all HPSI safety procedures, rules and regulations are communicated, understood, and followed.

·Perform other related duties as required and assigned.

1. DOCKMASTER & DRYDOCK OPERATIONS

  • Plan, direct, and coordinate docking and undocking operations for commercial, government, and other vessels.
  • Provide operational leadership during all critical phases of docking and undocking evolutions.
  • Coordinate drydock preparation, including:
    • Dock layouts and docking plans
    • Blocking and cribbing arrangements
    • Shoring requirements
    • Vessel positioning
    • Line-handling requirements
    • Tug and marine-service requirements
    • Personnel and equipment requirements
    • Waterfront support
  • Review applicable vessel drawings, docking plans, hydrostatic information, calculations, procedures, and technical documentation.
  • Verify that docking blocks, shores, cribbing, and related support systems are properly positioned and inspected prior to docking.
  • Coordinate with Engineering, Production, HSE, vessel representatives, marine service providers, and other stakeholders during docking evolutions.
  • Maintain operational oversight throughout dock flooding, vessel entry, positioning, landing, pump-down, blocking, inspection, and undocking activities.
  • Monitor vessel position, dock conditions, water levels, lines, blocks, shores, stability considerations, and other critical conditions.
  • Coordinate required inspections following vessel landing and dock pump-down.
  • Direct or coordinate corrective actions for deficiencies identified during docking operations.
  • Stop, delay, or modify docking operations when unsafe conditions, inadequate resources, procedural deviations, or unacceptable operational risks are identified.

2. WATERFRONT & VESSEL MOVEMENTS

  • Plan and coordinate vessel movements throughout HPSI waterfront facilities.
  • Coordinate vessel movements between drydocks, piers, berthing areas, outfitting locations, construction areas, test areas, and other designated waterfront facilities.
  • Coordinate tugboats, line handlers, barges, cranes, pilots, and other marine support resources as required.
  • Verify adequate qualified personnel, equipment, communications, and resources are available before vessel movements.
  • Coordinate pier assignments, berthing arrangements, vessel arrivals, departures, shifts, docking, and undocking.
  • Identify and resolve conflicts between vessel movements, crane operations, construction activities, drydock operations, pier activities, and other shipyard operations.
  • Ensure vessel movement plans and critical operational requirements are effectively communicated to affected departments and organizations.

3. DOCKING PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT & NAVSEA READINESS

  • Serve as a technical subject-matter resource for the continued development of HPSI's docking and waterfront operations program.
  • Assist HPSI in evaluating existing docking procedures, personnel qualifications, facilities, equipment, documentation, and operational practices against anticipated future U.S. Navy and NAVSEA requirements.
  • Support development and implementation of procedures, controls, training, qualification standards, documentation, and organizational responsibilities necessary to mature HPSI's docking program.
  • Maintain familiarity with applicable NAVSEA docking requirements, technical manuals, standard items, Navy specifications, and other requirements relevant to future Navy docking operations.
  • Identify gaps between existing HPSI docking capabilities and anticipated Navy/NAVSEA requirements and recommend practical corrective actions.
  • Participate in development of a structured roadmap for achieving required Navy/NAVSEA docking capability when contractually or operationally required.
  • Support future Navy/NAVSEA assessments, reviews, audits, demonstrations, and qualification activities.
  • Assist in developing and mentoring additional shipyard personnel necessary to support a sustainable docking organization.
  • Maintain professional competency and pursue additional Navy/NAVSEA-related training or qualification as required by HPSI's future business needs.

This position is intended to build HPSI's future NAVSEA docking capability and does not require the incumbent to possess an HPSI-specific NAVSEA Dockmaster qualification upon hire unless subsequently required by contract or regulation.

4. GOVERNMENT & U.S. NAVY WATERFRONT SUPPORT

  • Support waterfront activities associated with U.S. Navy and other government vessels when assigned to HPSI.
  • Coordinate with Navy representatives, Ship's Force, government personnel, Project Management, Production, Engineering, Planning, HSE, and other departments.
  • Support vessel maintenance, modernization, repair, testing, inspection, and waterfront activities.
  • Coordinate pier-side services, utilities, access, logistics, marine services, and other operational requirements.
  • Participate in operational planning, readiness reviews, production meetings, pre-evolution briefings, and waterfront coordination meetings.
  • Identify operational risks or conflicts that could affect safety, schedule, quality, vessel availability, or customer requirements.

5. OPERATIONS PLANNING & RESOURCE COORDINATION

  • Participate in short- and long-range planning for shipyard docking and waterfront activities.
  • Coordinate personnel, equipment, drydock capacity, pier space, tug services, line handlers, and other resources required to support vessel operations.
  • Review vessel schedules, docking requirements, production priorities, emergent work, and resource requirements.
  • Identify schedule and resource conflicts and recommend solutions.
  • Provide Operations leadership with timely information regarding:
    • Docking and vessel movement requirements
    • Schedule risks
    • Resource limitations
    • Waterfront conflicts
    • Equipment requirements
    • Safety concerns
    • Emergent operational issues
  • Assist Operations leadership in establishing priorities when multiple projects compete for waterfront or drydock resources.

6. EMERGENT WORK

  • Serve designated short-duration, waterfront, high-priority, or emergent projects as assigned.
  • Coordinate multiple departments, contractors, personnel, and resources to accomplish project objectives.
  • Assist in developing work plans, schedules, manpower requirements, equipment requirements, and operational controls.
  • Monitor progress and resolve operational conflicts.
  • Maintain communication with Project Management and senior leadership regarding schedule, cost, manpower, safety, and resource impacts.
  • Ensure assigned work is safely integrated into ongoing shipyard operations.

7. SAFETY, HSE & REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

  • Demonstrate visible leadership and accountability for safety during docking, waterfront, and vessel movement operations.
  • Ensure operations are conducted in accordance with HPSI procedures, HSE requirements, applicable OSHA maritime standards, environmental requirements, customer requirements, and applicable government requirements.
  • Conduct or participate in inspections of drydock, waterfront, pier, and vessel-support operations.
  • Identify unsafe conditions and ensure appropriate corrective actions are initiated.
  • Exercise stop-work authority when an imminent hazard or unacceptable operational risk exists.
  • Coordinate with HSE and Fire & Emergency Services for high-risk operations.
  • Ensure activities involving hot work, confined spaces, hazardous materials, lifting and rigging, fall hazards, and other high-risk work are properly coordinated with the responsible departments.
  • Participate in incident investigations, corrective actions, lessons learned, and operational reviews as appropriate.

8. EMERGENCY RESPONSE

  • Serve as a key Operations representative during emergencies affecting vessels, drydocks, piers, or waterfront facilities.
  • Support operational response to vessel fires, flooding, severe weather, power outages, equipment failures, environmental releases, serious injuries, and other waterfront emergencies.
  • Coordinate with HSE, Fire & Emergency Services, Security, Emergency Management, vessel representatives, government representatives, and external emergency agencies as appropriate.
  • Participate in emergency preparedness exercises involving vessels, drydocks, and waterfront facilities.
  • Assist with restoration of safe operations following emergencies.

9. LEADERSHIP & PERSONNEL DEVELOPMENT

  • Provide leadership and technical direction to waterfront personnel, shipwrights, dock crews, assigned supervisors, and contractors.
  • Establish expectations for safety, operational discipline, quality, accountability, and professional conduct.
  • Assist in establishing training and qualification requirements for personnel involved in docking and vessel movement activities.
  • Mentor personnel in docking practices and waterfront operations.
  • Support manpower planning and resource allocation.
  • Promote effective communication between Operations, Production, Engineering, Planning, HSE, Project Management, and waterfront personnel.
  • Help develop organizational capability and succession depth for future Navy/NAVSEA docking operations.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

The successful candidate should possess:

· Minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible shipyard, dry dock, or marine operations experience.

· Minimum of five (5) years of direct NAVSEA/U.S. Navy ship docking and undocking experience in a Dockmaster, Assistant Dockmaster, or equivalent responsible docking position.

· The required five (5) years of NAVSEA docking experience must include direct involvement in the planning, preparation, execution, and/or supervision of docking and undocking evolutions conducted in accordance with applicable NAVSEA requirements and procedures.

· Demonstrated experience with docking plans, blocking arrangements, vessel stability and loading considerations, dry dock systems and operations, and coordination of personnel involved in docking evolutions.

· Current or previous NAVSEA Dockmaster qualification/certification is preferred.

  • Strong working knowledge of:
    • Drydock operations
    • Docking plans
    • Blocking and cribbing
    • Shoring
    • Vessel positioning
    • Vessel movements
    • Line handling
    • Tug operations
    • Waterfront operations
  • Demonstrated leadership experience during complex or high-risk maritime operations.
  • Ability to read and interpret vessel drawings, docking plans, specifications, technical documentation, and operational procedures.
  • Experience coordinating multiple departments, contractors, marine-service providers, equipment, and personnel.
  • Strong understanding of industrial and maritime safety requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound operational decisions during changing or time-critical conditions.

HIGHLY PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Preference will be given to candidates possessing one or more of the following:

  • Previous experience as a Dockmaster, Assistant Dockmaster, Docking Officer, Docking Supervisor, Ship Superintendent, Shipwright Supervisor, or comparable senior shipyard waterfront position.
  • Previous U.S. Navy shipyard, private-sector Navy ship repair, or NAVSEA-related experience.
  • Experience working under NAVSEA docking requirements or Navy docking procedures.
  • Previous NAVSEA-recognized Dockmaster, Docking Officer, or equivalent qualification or demonstrated experience working within a NAVSEA-qualified docking organization.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Navy shipbuilding, maintenance, modernization, overhaul, or repair.
  • Familiarity with Navy technical requirements, Standard Items, technical manuals, specifications, and shipyard procedures.
  • Experience participating in Navy/NAVSEA inspections, audits, assessments, readiness reviews, or qualification processes.
  • Experience developing docking procedures, qualification programs, training programs, or shipyard waterfront operating standards.

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Docking & Undocking
  • Drydock Operations
  • Docking Planning
  • Blocking, Cribbing & Shoring
  • Vessel Movement
  • Waterfront Operations
  • Pier & Berthing Management
  • Marine Services Coordination
  • Operational Risk Management
  • Shipyard Operations
  • Safety Leadership
  • Emergency Response
  • Production & Resource Planning
  • Contractor Management
  • Workforce Leadership
  • Technical Problem Solving
  • Cross-Department Coordination
  • Government & Customer Relations
  • Navy/NAVSEA Readiness
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Decision making/problem solving
  • Adaptability and organizational skills and understanding
  • Integrity
  • Conflict resolution
  • Strategic thinking
  • Stress management
  • Willingness and ability to work as a team member

AUTHORITY & ACCOUNTABILITY

The Dockmaster & Waterfront Operations Superintendent has significant operational authority and accountability for the safe planning and execution of vessel movements, docking, undocking, berthing, drydock operations, and associated waterfront activities within the responsibilities assigned by HPSI.

The position is expected to make independent operational decisions within established HPSI policies, procedures, regulatory requirements, approved docking plans, and customer requirements.

The Dockmaster has the authority and responsibility to stop, delay, or recommend modification of an operation when unsafe conditions, inadequate resources, procedural deviations, equipment deficiencies, or unacceptable operational risks are identified.

Significant operational concerns shall be promptly elevated to Operations leadership and other appropriate HPSI or customer representatives.

WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

The position routinely interacts with:

  • Executive and Operations Leadership
  • Project Management
  • Production
  • Engineering
  • Planning
  • HSE
  • Fire & Emergency Services
  • Security
  • Environmental
  • Quality Assurance
  • Shipwrights and Waterfront Personnel
  • Vessel Owners and Operators
  • U.S. Navy and Government Representatives
  • Ship's Force
  • Tug, Pilot, and Marine Service Providers
  • Contractors and Subcontractors

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is performed throughout Hanwha Philly Shipyard, including drydocks, piers, vessels, waterfront areas, construction areas, shops, and other heavy industrial work locations. The position may be exposed to noise, heat, cold, rain, wind, dust, fumes, welding and cutting operations, chemicals, heavy equipment, cranes, rigging operations, and other industrial hazards.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. A range of motion sufficient to perform general lifting, carrying, bending, stooping, climbing, working at heights, extended walking or standing, and working around vessels and heavy industrial equipment.

POSITION TYPE/EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK

This is an on-site, full-time, safety-sensitive position. Work outside normal business hours, including nights, weekends, holidays, and emergency call-in, may be required to support docking and undocking evolutions, vessel movements, emergent work, and other critical shipyard operations.

SUCCESS IN THIS POSITION

Success in this position requires the ability to:

  • Safely plan and execute complex docking and undocking operations.
  • Maintain disciplined and efficient drydock and waterfront operations.
  • Anticipate and manage operational risks.
  • Coordinate multiple departments, contractors, and marine-service providers.
  • Effectively manage drydock, pier, and waterfront resources.
  • Develop and mentor personnel involved in docking operations.
  • Make sound decisions during rapidly changing conditions.
  • Maintain strong working relationships with vessel owners, customers, government representatives, and shipyard departments.
  • Strengthen HPSI's docking procedures, organizational capability, and technical expertise.
  • Provide the experience and leadership necessary to progressively develop HPSI's docking program toward future U.S. Navy/NAVSEA qualification and operational requirements.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

OTHER DUTIES

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time or without notice.

Hanwha Philly Shipyard is committed to equal opportunity for all applicants. The recruitment, selection, employment, and training of employees during employment shall be without discrimination because of race, color, religion, national origin, gender or age-except that the applicant must meet the minimum age requirement. Hanwha Philly Shipyard does not, and will not, discriminate because of the disability of such an individual.

title: Sr. Market Risk Analyst (2021)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

Take a central role in analyzing and managing market risks on trading floors, conducting advanced stress testing, assessing exposure limits, and evaluating value at risk (VaR) to fortify risk management strategies. Contribute to the development of sophisticated risk models, offer strategic insights into market dynamics, and provide guidance to junior analysts in their daily responsibilities. Play a key role in facilitating informed decision-making and ensuring regulatory compliance across the organization.

KEY DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead daily risk control process and risk reports; working alongside with traders, operators and IT to manage market risk.
  • Ensure daily data integrity, validate positions and reconcile data inconsistences with traders.
  • Monitor and report daily price exposure, mark-to-market and P&L to management.
  • Lead advanced stress testing and scenario analysis to evaluate market risks accurately.
  • Assess exposure limits and evaluate value at risk (VaR) to fortify risk management strategies.
  • Develop and maintain sophisticated risk models tailored to the organization's trading floors.
  • Provide strategic insights into market dynamics and their impact on risk exposure.
  • Guide and mentor junior analysts in conducting market risk assessments and analyses.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to implement risk mitigation strategies effectively.
  • Stay updated on market trends, regulatory changes, and industry best practices.
  • Analyze complex financial data to identify emerging risks and opportunities.
  • Prepare and present comprehensive reports to senior management and stakeholders.
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies related to market risk management.
  • Collaborate on ad-hoc projects and tasks under the direction of senior analysts, fostering continuous improvement in market risk management practices.

COMMUNICATION

Internal Communication

  • Lead conversation with traders, operators and IT to produce accurate daily risk reports.
  • Collaborate with senior management to provide updates on market risk assessments and discuss strategic initiatives.
  • Engage with cross-functional teams to communicate risk management strategies and ensure alignment with organizational objectives.

External Communication

  • Interface with regulatory authorities or external auditors to provide insights into market risk management practices and ensure compliance.
  • Communicate with market data providers or industry experts to gather relevant information and insights for risk analysis and decision-making.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Education and Skills (Required, Preferred)

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, mathematics, or a related field.
  • Proficiency in statistical analysis tools such as Python, R, or MATLAB.
  • Strong understanding of financial markets, trading instruments, and risk management principles.
  • Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with a focus on problem-solving.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other relevant software for financial modeling and analysis.

Preferred

  • CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst) designation.
  • Experience with risk management software such as Bloomberg, MSCI RiskMetrics, or Reuters.
  • Knowledge of advanced statistical techniques and modeling methodologies.
  • Familiarity with regulatory frameworks such as Basel III, Dodd-Frank, or MiFID II.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for presenting complex risk analysis to stakeholders.

Experience and Knowledge (Required, Preferred)

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in market risk management or a related field.
  • Proven track record of developing and implementing risk models and methodologies.
  • Experience in stress testing, scenario analysis, and value at risk (VaR) calculations.
  • Strong understanding of financial derivatives, including options, futures, and swaps.
  • Knowledge of regulatory requirements and industry best practices in risk management.

Preferred

  • Previous experience in a leadership or supervisory role, overseeing junior analysts or team members.
  • Familiarity with energy commodities, including crude oil, natural gas, and electricity markets.
  • Experience with market risk measurement techniques such as historical simulation, Monte Carlo simulation, or parametric VaR
  • Understanding of market microstructure and its impact on trading and risk management.
  • Knowledge of emerging trends and technologies in risk management, such as machine learning and artificial intelligence.

Abilities and Specific Requirements (Required, Preferred)

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in data analysis and reporting.
  • Sound judgment and decision-making abilities in high-pressure environments.
  • Adherence to strict confidentiality and ethical standards in handling sensitive financial information.

Preferred

  • Strategic thinking and the ability to provide insights into long-term risk management strategies.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to navigate changing market conditions and regulatory requirements.
  • Effective problem-solving skills for addressing complex risk management challenges.
  • Ability to mentor and coach junior analysts, fostering their professional development and growth.

NO THIRD-PARTY CANDIDATES ACCEPTED

title: Concrete Estimator
description:
Morgan Corp. is seeking an experienced Concrete Estimator to join our Industrial Division Estimating Team in Duncan, South Carolina.
Our Industrial Division performs complex civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical construction for clients in the power generation, water/wastewater, marine, mining, manufacturing, and other industrial process markets.
The Concrete Estimator is responsible for developing complete estimates for self-performed structural concrete work and the associated scopes necessary to execute the work. The successful candidate should have a strong understanding of concrete construction means and methods and be capable of evaluating constructability, sequencing, access, production, equipment requirements, and project-specific risks.
This position is best suited for someone with meaningful concrete field experience who has transitioned into estimating, project management, or preconstruction and can apply that practical construction knowledge to the estimating process.

Work Environment:
This position is based in Morgan Corp.'s Duncan, South Carolina office. Limited travel is required for pre-bid meetings, project site visits, and other estimating or preconstruction activities.
The Concrete Estimator will independently develop detailed estimates from project drawings, specifications, site information, and other bid documents. Responsibilities include:
  • Perform detailed quantity takeoffs for concrete, formwork, reinforcing steel, embeds, grout, and other structural concrete components.
  • Develop labor crews, production rates, labor hours, material requirements, and equipment costs.
  • Evaluate construction means and methods, including forming systems, pour sequencing, reinforcing installation, concrete placement methods, access, lifting requirements, and temporary works.
  • Develop project schedules and evaluate how sequencing, production, access, and project constraints affect estimated costs.
  • Identify project risks, constructability concerns, scope gaps, and opportunities to improve execution or provide a competitive advantage.
  • Develop pricing for ancillary scopes associated with the concrete work, including excavation and backfill, structural embeds and fabricated components, trench drains, survey/layout, concrete demolition, coatings, waterproofing, specialty items, and other related work.
  • Develop scopes of work and solicit pricing from subcontractors, suppliers, and fabricators.
  • Review subcontractor and vendor proposals for scope coverage, exclusions, qualifications, and alignment with the bid documents.
  • Develop bid clarifications, assumptions, exclusions, and other proposal deliverables.
  • Participate in pre-bid meetings and site visits to evaluate existing conditions, access, logistics, and construction constraints.
  • Collaborate with the Estimating Manager and other discipline estimators to develop an integrated project estimate, schedule, and proposal.
  • Participate in estimate reviews and clearly communicate the basis of estimate, significant risks, opportunities, and proposed construction approach.
  • Support project handoff and preconstruction activities for successful bids to ensure estimating assumptions, commitments, risks, and planned means and methods are effectively transferred to the project team.
Preferred Experience
  • 5+ years of concrete construction field experience preferred, with experience involving structural cast-in-place concrete.
  • Experience estimating complex structural concrete work in industrial, heavy civil, power, water/wastewater, marine, manufacturing, or similar construction environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform detailed concrete quantity takeoffs and develop complete estimates.
  • Experience developing labor crews, production rates, equipment requirements, and construction means and methods.
  • Experience identifying and estimating ancillary scopes associated with structural concrete construction.
  • Experience developing scopes of work, soliciting subcontractor/vendor pricing, and evaluating quotations.
  • Working knowledge of construction safety requirements, scheduling, constructability, and project controls.
Software
Experience with the following is preferred:
  • PlanSwift or comparable takeoff software
  • Bluebeam Revu
  • Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office
  • Primavera P6 or comparable scheduling software
  • Construction estimating software
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage
  • 401(k) with company match
  • PTO, holidays, and a paid winter holiday
  • Professional development & career growth opportunities
  • Supportive team environment in a respected, growing company
  • Vehicle allowance
  • Cell phone reimbursement
