Burnside will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the entire recruitment, assessment, and selection process, as required. If you are a person with a disability and require an accommodation during these processes, please contact our Human Resources department.

Company Profile – More about us:

Founded in 1970, R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited is a growing values-driven Canadian employee-owned, led and operated Civil and Environmental Engineering Consulting Firm with over 450 professional, technical and support staff. Our consistent commitment towards investing in technology advancements and training, in addition to encouraging and promoting professional development, has enabled our firm to meet our ongoing and stated goal of continual improvement.

We actively seek to develop relationships with a broad and diversified client base in the Public, Private and Indigenous sectors. We work on a variety of projects throughout Canada, with 12 office locations (11 in Ontario and one in Manitoba).

Burnside has expertise in many technical disciplines beyond our core civil engineering focus including air and noise, asset management, bridges & culverts, building sciences, environmental planning and ecology, GIS, hydrogeology, land development, landscape architecture, municipal engineering, municipal drainage, solid waste, stormwater management, structures, traffic, transportation planning and design, water and wastewater and well drilling & diagnostics.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
description:
At Analogic, we develop technology that helps save lives and create a safer world. From advancing healthcare outcomes to securing critical environments, our innovations make a difference every day.

As we continue to expand globally, we are seeking a talented Cybersecurity Analyst to help protect our people, systems, and data from evolving cyber threats. This is a highly visible, hands-on role where you'll work with advanced security technologies, lead incident response efforts, strengthen security operations, and play a key role in safeguarding a growing global enterprise.

If you're passionate about cybersecurity, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want to make a meaningful impact, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Protect and Defend the Enterprise

  • Monitor, investigate, and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents across the organization.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for escalated alerts from Managed Detection and Response (MDR) providers.
  • Lead incident triage, containment, remediation, and recovery efforts to minimize business risk and operational disruption.

Manage Advanced Security Technologies

  • Administer and optimize a diverse portfolio of cybersecurity tools, including:
    • Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR)
    • Cloud Security (AWS & Azure)
    • Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
    • Privileged Access Management (PAM)
    • Data Protection Solutions
    • Vulnerability Management Platforms
  • Continuously evaluate and improve security controls to enhance organizational resilience.

Strengthen Security Operations & Processes

  • Develop and maintain incident response playbooks and procedures.
  • Participate in tabletop exercises and readiness assessments.
  • Recommend and implement process improvements that elevate security maturity and operational efficiency.

Drive Vulnerability & Compliance Initiatives

  • Coordinate network, server, cloud, and application vulnerability scanning activities.
  • Work closely with IT stakeholders to prioritize remediation efforts and reduce organizational risk.
  • Support compliance programs and audits aligned with frameworks such as NIST and other regulatory requirements.

Support Identity & Access Management

  • Assist with user provisioning, access reviews, and identity governance initiatives.
  • Help ensure secure access practices across enterprise systems and cloud environments.

Promote a Security-First Culture

  • Lead cybersecurity awareness training and phishing simulation programs.
  • Educate and empower employees to recognize and respond to evolving cyber threats.
  • Partner with business teams to strengthen security awareness across the organization.

Mentor and Collaborate

  • Provide guidance and support to junior cybersecurity professionals.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with IT, compliance, infrastructure, and business teams to drive enterprise security initiatives.

What You'll Bring

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field preferred.
  • Minimum of 5 years of IT experience, including at least 3 years focused on:
    • Cybersecurity Operations
    • Threat Hunting
    • Incident Response
    • Security Engineering

Certifications

  • Security+ certification required (or ability to obtain within six months of hire).
  • CySA+, CISSP, GIAC, or other advanced cybersecurity certifications are highly desirable.

Technical Expertise

  • Strong knowledge of:
    • Incident Response and Threat Detection
    • Network and Host-Based Intrusion Analysis
    • Malware Analysis and Remediation
    • Enterprise Security Architecture and Protocols
  • Experience with:
    • Windows and Linux operating systems
    • Active Directory and Microsoft Intune
    • Virtualization technologies
    • AWS and Azure cloud environments
  • Familiarity with:
    • PowerShell and Python scripting
    • MITRE ATT&CK Framework
    • Threat Intelligence and Security Analytics Platforms

Professional Skills

  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences.
  • Collaborative, customer-focused mindset and passion for continuous learning.

Why Join Analogic?

At Analogic, cybersecurity is a strategic priority. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside talented professionals, leverage leading-edge technologies, and make a measurable impact on a global organization.

What We Offer

  • 9/80 Work Schedule – Enjoy every other Friday off to recharge and spend time on what matters most.
  • Flexible Vacation Policy – Take the time you need with a culture that values work-life balance.
  • Comprehensive Healthcare – Medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and disability coverage.
  • HRA & HSA Contributions – Company contributions to help support your healthcare needs.
  • 401(k) with Company Match & Immediate Vesting – Start building your future from day one.
  • Tuition & Continuing Education Assistance – Invest in your growth and career development.
  • Innovative, Collaborative Culture – Work alongside talented engineers in an environment that encourages creativity, ownership, and technical excellence.

Ready to defend, innovate, and make a difference? Apply today and help us build a more secure future.

  • Meaningful work that supports healthcare and security technologies worldwide
  • Exposure to modern cybersecurity tools and cloud security platforms
  • Opportunities for professional growth and continuous learning
  • Collaborative, innovative, and mission-driven culture
  • Flexible hybrid work environment

Work Environment & Eligibility

Hybrid Work Schedule
This position combines remote flexibility with regular in-office collaboration at our corporate headquarters.

Work Authorization
Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements. Analogic is not sponsoring employment visas for this position.

Join Us

If you're ready to take your cybersecurity career to the next level and help protect technologies that improve lives and enhance global security, we invite you to apply and become part of the Analogic team.

Help us stay ahead of tomorrow's threats while enabling the innovations that matter most.

R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited (Burnside) is seeking a client-focused Structural Lead to join our Building Design Team. This is a high-impact role for someone who thrives on building client relationships, developing new business, and mentoring others while contributing to innovative and meaningful building projects across Ontario and Manitoba.

We already have strong technical talent on our team. What we’re looking for is someone who can connect with people, both clients and colleagues, and help us grow our presence through exceptional service, trusted advice, and leadership.

You’ll work directly with both public and private sector clients on a range of exciting structural projects, including industrial facilities, commercial and residential developments, public works buildings, and transportation-related infrastructure.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own client relationships, cultivate trust, identify opportunities, and maintain long-term partnerships.
  • Lead structural projects from concept through construction, serving as either Lead Engineer or Project Manager depending on scope and complexity.
  • Act as a strategic advisor to clients by understanding their needs and aligning solutions with their goals.
  • Drive business development by supporting proposal preparation and identifying new project opportunities.
  • Mentor and support junior engineers and designers, helping to develop the next generation of talent.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across Burnside offices to deliver successful, integrated project outcomes.
  • Conduct and review structural designs, drawings, reports, specifications, and construction phase services.
  • Prepare various documents including feasibility studies, condition assessments, and technical submissions.
  • Ensure project success by managing schedules, budgets, resources, and client communications.

What You Bring:

  • P.Eng. designation in Ontario and ideally 10+ years of experience in structural design and consulting.
  • We will also consider candidates with a strong technical background in structural design and consulting who may not hold a P.Eng. designation.
  • Proven experience in client management and business development in a consulting environment.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Structural Engineering or a related field.
  • Strong working knowledge of structural systems, building codes, and design standards.
  • Experience with condition assessments, design development, and project execution.
  • Proficiency with structural design software and Microsoft Office tools.
  • Strong understanding of municipal and provincial approval processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, communicate effectively, and manage competing priorities.
  • Excellent proposal and report writing skills.
  • A collaborative mindset with a proactive, solutions-oriented approach.

This is more than a technical role, it's a chance to influence how we grow, how we serve clients, and how we develop our people. If you're passionate about building structures and building relationships, we’d love to connect.

Salary Range: $115,000 - $130,000

The final compensation offered will be based on factors such as relevant experience, skills, internal equity, and market conditions.

Position Type: New Position

Why Choose Burnside?

Are you interested in working for an employer with a 5-decade track record of building a great reputation both internally with their staff and externally with their clients? The Burnside team is a supportive group of colleagues that work together to provide value and service to our clients, while extending care to each other. We know that our employees are our greatest asset, and thus we strive to provide a positive work/life balance.

We offer:

  • A collaborative culture where friendship, honesty and respect are part of our core values and practices
  • Flexible working hours, including hybrid working opportunities
  • A competitive compensation and benefits package
  • RRSP company matching plan
  • Career growth and professional development opportunities
  • Potential for performance-driven bonusing
  • Active social committees
  • A welcoming, positive, and inclusive work environment

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to valuing diversity in the workplace and we welcome resumes from all qualified candidates. Burnside will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the entire recruitment, assessment, and selection process, as required. If you are a person with a disability and require an accommodation during these processes, please contact our Human Resources department.

Company Profile – More about us:

Founded in 1970, R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited is a growing values-driven Canadian employee-owned, led and operated Civil and Environmental Engineering Consulting Firm with over 450 professional, technical and support staff. Our consistent commitment towards investing in technology advancements and training, in addition to encouraging and promoting professional development, has enabled our firm to meet our ongoing and stated goal of continual improvement.

We actively seek to develop relationships with a broad and diversified client base in the Public, Private and Indigenous sectors. We work on a variety of projects throughout Canada, with 12 office locations (11 in Ontario and one in Manitoba).

Burnside has expertise in many technical disciplines beyond our core civil engineering focus including air and noise, asset management, bridges & culverts, building sciences, environmental planning and ecology, GIS, hydrogeology, land development, landscape architecture, municipal engineering, municipal drainage, solid waste, stormwater management, structures, traffic, transportation planning and design, water and wastewater and well drilling & diagnostics.

title: Luxury Reservations Supervisor
location: West Palm Beach, Florida, United States
description:
Our client is an award-winning, family-owned luxury cruise line that has spent more than two decades quietly redefining small-ship travel. Their yachts carry roughly one hundred guests, which changes everything: crew learn names, guests come back year after year and ask for people by name, and the experience is built around the individual rather than the itinerary. The fleet is growing and a new commercial office is opening in West Palm Beach, so this is the rare chance to join an established luxury brand at the beginning of a new chapter.

They are hiring a Reservations Supervisor to lead the team in the new West Palm Beach office. This is a genuine leadership seat with room above it, not a senior agent title.

What you will do

  • Lead the day to day reservations operation, including coverage, scheduling and service standards across US and overseas team members
  • Coach the team on consultative selling, not order taking. Guests here are choosing between a yacht and a villa, and the conversation matters
  • Own the numbers: conversion, call and email response times, booking value and service levels, and report on them credibly
  • Handle the bookings that need a steady hand, including VIPs, repeat guests, travel advisor escalations and anything complicated
  • Tighten the process. Find the manual steps, the reporting gaps and the automation nobody has built yet, and fix them
  • Partner with Sales, Revenue Management and the onboard team so what is promised ashore is what happens on board
  • Hire, onboard and develop the team as the office and the fleet expand

What we are looking for

  • Supervisory or team lead experience in reservations, guest services, front office or a travel contact centre, ideally in luxury hospitality or luxury travel
  • A luxury service instinct. Five-star hotel, private club, yacht, villa, resort or luxury travel background all translate directly
  • Comfort with reporting and systems. You should like a dashboard, not tolerate one, and be strong in Excel and on a reservations or property management platform
  • Experience coaching people to a standard rather than simply managing a queue
  • Excellent written and spoken communication, and the judgment to know which is which
  • A second language is a plus, as is experience with overseas or remote team members

Why people take this job

Small-ship luxury is a different business from mass-market cruise. Roughly a hundred guests a voyage means fewer transactions handled with more care, and repeat bookings that prove it. You are joining as the office is being built, so how this function works is largely going to be how you decide it works.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Short- and long-term disability, life, and long-term care coverage
  • Paid time off, including vacation, sick and personal days, company holidays, floating holidays, and bereavement leave
  • 2 Weeks of yachting for you and a companion, per year
  • Friends and family sailing rates after six months of employment

title: HRIS Administrator - 200201E
description:
Information about the role and the office:
The Museum is going through transformational change as an institution and Human Resources is an essential partner in identifying, developing and implementing new strategies, policies and processes to support strategic plans and our people, the foundation of our work and future success.

Human Resources is seeking to hire a Human Resources Information System (HRIS) Administrator to bolster HR’s ability to support and maintain the institution’s HRIS to ensure efficient and effective HR Operations.

The HRIS Administrator will serve as the first point of contact for HRIS-related issues, implementing system improvements and system upgrades, ensuring data integrity and security, generating recurring and ad hoc reports for HR team members and senior leadership, and providing technical support to end-users.

The position is located in Washington, DC. This is a full-time, donated (non-federal), position paid with the Museum’s private funds. Salary is commensurate with experience.

Duties and Responsibilities for the role:

Administers the day-to-day operations of the Museum’s HRIS, ensuring that the system is configured and utilized effectively across all HR functions, including payroll, benefits, timekeeping, recruitment, compensation, onboarding, performance management, learning management, and compliance.

Serves as a representative and liaison between HR, IT, external vendors, and other stakeholders for HRIS design and implementation projects.

Continuously assesses, recommends, and implements HRIS features and functionality

optimizations to meet the evolving needs of the HR department and the Museum, including system improvements and upgrades, with the approval of the Chief Human Resources Officer.

Ensures HRIS data is accurately maintained, audited, updated, and complies with data security and privacy standards.

Maintains and manages permissions, access, and similar system operations and settings for HR staff and Museum system users.

Identifies opportunities for automation within all respects of HR processes and provides

recommendations to the Chief Human Resources Officer.

Generates reports and analyzes data to support decision-making, compliance, and performance metrics.

Provides training to HR staff and other HR system Museum users on the functionality and capabilities of the HRIS, ensuring users are fully equipped to utilize the system effectively.

Serves as the first point of contact for resolving system-related issues and troubleshooting.

Contributes to special projects.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications for the role:

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of work experience.

3+ years of experience administering HRIS platforms with a minimum of 1 year of experience with Dayforce.

In-depth knowledge of HR processes, including payroll, benefits, timekeeping, compliance, learning management and performance management. Strong technical proficiency in HRIS management, including system configuration, reporting, and troubleshooting.

Experience in system integration and data migration, particularly in the context of HR systems.

Exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to train and support HR team members and other system users.

Demonstrates strong critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills.

Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities; work under pressure with tight deadlines; and manage multiple projects at once.

Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines.

Demonstrated experience with general office productivity tools (i.e., Google, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Preferred Qualifications for the role:

Dayforce Administrator experience.

HRIS certification.

HR Analytics certification.

The application deadline for this position is October 23, 2026.
Interested applicants should apply with their resume and cover letter for consideration.

title: Person in Charge
description:

Position Purpose: Exemplifies and ensures strong customer service in all aspects of the job. Directs and controls the operation of the Front End in the absence of store management to achieve sales and profit objectives.

Job Description: As a primary contact for customers, the Grocery Fourth/Person In Charge (PIC) provides friendly, courteous, and helpful service. During the absence of the Store Manager and the First & Second Assistant Managers, the PIC is in charge of the store, with analogous authority to make necessary decisions to operate the store at maximum profit, efficiency, and superior customer service. All store employees during the absence of the Store Director or Assistant Store Director.

six-wheeled cart, grocery cart, box cutter, pens and pencils, spray bottle, rags, mops, broom, telephone/intercom, cash register, credit card scanner, computer, pallet jack, bailer

Our Facilities Associates are critical team members who are responsible for maintaining two of our gyms in a given region while also helping at other gyms on an as needed basis. They partner with the Director team to ensure that the gym is in excellent condition at all times and are expected to prioritize emergency repairs as needed. In addition, they also serve as the point of contact for larger capital projects and investments in their gym. This position will report to the Assistant Facilities Director for the DMV region.
Job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Meets bi-weekly with Gym management to prioritize and plan for each of the gyms they work in.
Performs general maintenance.
Uses project management software, Asana, to manage tasks.
Coordinates with Facilities Service Providers when projects or repairs require a trade skill (such as electrical, HVAC, plumbing, etc). While communicating progress to GD/AD via project software and direct communications
Maintains clear lines of communications with Regional Facilities Manager or Assistant Director as applicable
Coordinates monthly and annual maintenance calendar, and facilities requests from the gym, preparing schedule, timeline, costs and staffing needs proposal, then executing the proposal when approved.
Works with the Regional Facilities Manager or Assistant Director to develop maintenance procedures and ensures implementation.
Manages relationships with contractors and service providers (fitness equipment providers, pest control, etc.)
Keeps maintenance logs and reports on daily activities, keeping directors in the loop.
Monitors equipment inventory and places orders when necessary, seeking budget approval from Regional Facilities Manager or Assistant Director
Performs manual repairs and conducts (or coordinates) general upkeep procedures, such as landscaping, painting, light carpentry, foam padding repairs and replacement, etc.
Supervises and occasionally performs Rope and Anchors checks
Ensures that the employee work in the gyms is performed in a safe manner and complies with applicable safety requirements. This includes rope-access work as needed for repairs and inspections.
Responds to and addresses urgent maintenance needs per Movement Policy
Maintains info log and contact info for each gym on frequent repair service providers such as HVAC, Fire, Alarm, etc.

What success looks like:

Maintaining all building systems and equipment in a fully functional state
Proactively noticing problems and addressing them in a timely way so they don't become critical
Communicating facility project status effectively to directors and other stakeholders
Advocating for facility improvements

What you’ll bring with you

Gotta have:

Full time hours with a flexible schedule (ex: flex to work late nights, early mornings and weekends if work is needed to be done during non-business/busy hours)
Strong mechanical aptitude.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Excellent problem-solving skills.
Able to work independently, but in line with gym and director goals
Ability to safely use and supervise use of power tools and ladders.
Ability to keep track of and report on status of projects.
Organized and efficient, and able to meet deadlines.
Ability to perform Rope Access work and be comfortable working on ropes at height (training available).
Responds to emails and other inquiries by end of business day.
Supports and embodies Movement’s core values
Computer Skills (Word, Excel, Asana).
Ability to work on a ladder and lift 50lbs.
Have a drivers license and ability to travel to all region gyms

Bonus points for:

Experience maintaining rock climbing walls and climbing safety equipment
Working knowledge of climbing gym floor and wall systems.
Broad experience in facility maintenance including plumbing, carpentry, electrical, HVAC, and finish work.
Working knowledge of facilities machines and equipment, tools and devices.

title: Director of Culinary Services
description:
About Arvum Senior Living

At Arvum Senior Living, we proudly serve seniors through Assisted Living and Memory Care communities across eight states throughout the Gulf Coast and Midwest regions. Guided by our Pillars of Excellence, Arvum creates purpose-driven communities where residents receive compassionate care and Team Members experience meaningful careers, strong culture, and opportunities for continued growth.

As part of one of the largest senior living organizations in the country, Arvum communities have earned Great Place to Work® certifications from 2022–2026. We are committed to investing in our people through leadership development, training, and career advancement opportunities that empower our Team Members to thrive personally and professionally.

Discover Your Purpose with Us at Addington Place of Carroll!

As Director of Culinary Services, you’ll play an essential role in enriching the lives of seniors, creating meaningful connections, and making a difference every single day.

Your Role:

As the Director of Culinary Services, your role includes providing both strategic oversight and hands-on leadership of the Culinary Services Department. This includes responsibility for menu planning, staffing, food quality, safety, and budget performance. You’ll play a vital role in resident satisfaction by creating memorable dining experiences while ensuring operational excellence.

Position Highlights:

  • Status: Full Time
  • Schedule: Traditional leadership workweek with flexibility required based on business and operational needs that includes Manager on Duty hours as well as on call for emergency situations
  • Location: Carroll, IA
  • Rate of Pay: $55,000
  • Travel: N/A

Why You'll Love This Community:

Welcome to Addington Place of Carroll, offering Assisted Living and GLOW® Memory Care in a cozy community where the day feels familiar and easy to settle into. Share a warm meal, step outside to relax on the patio, and move through the morning at a comfortable pace with supportive moments close at hand.

Throughout the week, residents can join programs like gentle exercise, art workshops, cooking sessions, guest speakers, and weekend movies, with special touches like musical performances under the stars. Whether the day feels social or quiet, the rhythm here is designed to feel welcoming, steady, and genuinely livable.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead daily culinary operations while participating in meal preparation and service
  • Plan and execute menus that meet resident dietary guidelines and preferences
  • Monitor food quality, consistency, and presentation; implement improvements as needed
  • Ensure compliance with sanitation, safety, and dietary standards
  • Conduct food safety audits and quality assurance checks
  • Oversee purchasing, inventory control, and vendor contracts
  • Manage budgets, monitor costs, and take corrective action when needed
  • Manage, recruit, train, schedule, and evaluate culinary staff
  • Lead orientation and in-service training programs for team members
  • Engage with residents during mealtimes to ensure satisfaction and resolve concerns
  • Collaborate with Executive Director and department heads to align food services with community goals

Qualifications:

  • Minimum 5 years of culinary leadership in high-volume, high-standard environments (e.g., country clubs, resorts, cruise ships)
  • Hands-on experience leading kitchen operations, including cooking and staff oversight
  • Food Safety Certification required
  • Strong knowledge of sanitation, food handling, and loss prevention practices
  • Culinary training or certification preferred
  • Experience with menu engineering, cost controls, and vendor management
  • Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and kitchen management systems
  • Experience in senior living culinary services is a plus—but only if paired with demonstrated high service standards
  • Ability to work in kitchen environments
  • Oversight of food safety audits and inspections
  • Exposure to high-pressure operational deadlines
  • Ability to lift or assist with kitchen operations as needed
  • [Insert if applicable: Participation in rotating on-call schedule or Manager on Duty (MOD) responsibilities required]

Why Join Us

Discovery Senior Living Earned Coveted Great Place to Work Certification for 2025-2027!

A large part of what makes Discovery different from other companies in this industry is our willingness to embrace change. At Discovery Senior Living, we are constantly challenging how we are doing things to ensure the lifestyle we are offering our residents is absolutely the greatest value proposition in the marketplace. It’s just as important to us that the environment and culture for our team members are constantly refreshed. In addition, embracing and even encouraging change brings a never-ending supply of new energy to our business and our culture. That energy translates to other far-reaching positive impacts on our residents as well as our team members.

Find out what makes working at Discovery unique in the world of senior living. Discover Your Purpose!

Our Culture & Values

So often, what brings people together is deeply rooted in who we are and what we stand for. And at Discovery Senior Living, we’re unified by certain, core values, which we call our “Pillars of Excellence.” They make up the fabric of our company, and include TEAMWORK, INTEGRITY, PERFORMANCE, ACCOUNTABILITY, COMPASSION, HARD WORK and CREATIVITY.

Individually, they are our virtues, and together, they make up a roadmap which helps us foster innovation and success.

Benefits You’ll Enjoy

For eligible employees, we offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes competitive pay, medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance, paid time off and holidays, a 401(k) with employer match, paid training and career growth opportunities, wellness-related benefits, and additional support through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Equal Opportunity Employer

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all team members. EOE D/V

A Note to Applicants

This job description outlines the general nature and level of responsibilities for this role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties. Qualified individuals with disabilities, as defined by the ADA, must be able to perform the essential job functions with or without reasonable accommodation, as determined on a case-by-case basis.

Agency Policy

We do not accept unsolicited resumes from staffing agencies. Please refrain from contacting hiring managers directly.

Employment Scam Warning

We only post jobs on our official careers site and accept applications through that platform. We do not conduct interviews via text or social media or ask for personal or banking information.

Regulatory Compliance & Background Screening

Employment may be contingent upon successful completion of state-mandated and/or federally required background screenings, which may include criminal history checks, fingerprint-based screening, Level 2 background screening, registry verification, and other screenings required for healthcare and senior living roles with direct or indirect resident access.

Certain positions may be subject to additional requirements under federal programs, including CMS, Medicare, and Medicaid regulations, as well as state-specific licensing or regulatory agencies. title: Field Technician-2 Hours Weekly
description:
Get Paid to Drive Your Route. Work When It Works for You.

Field Technician — FreshPure Water Machines

1099 Independent Contractor | $27/hr. Memphis/Germantown, TN

If you like working independently, hate being stuck at a desk, and want a consistent route you can count on — this might be exactly what you’re looking for.

NWS operates water vending machines in retail stores across the country. We’re building a team of Field Technicians in Memphis/Germantown, TN to keep those machines clean, stocked, and running right. It’s straightforward work, it pays well, and you’re in charge of your own time.

What You’ll Actually Be Doing

Each week (or every two weeks, depending on the location), you’ll visit your assigned stores and:

• Clean and disinfect the FreshPure machine inside and out

• Take meter readings and log the data on your service report

• Snap photos of the machine condition at every visit

• Submit your completed report to the home office when you’re done

• Call in anything that looks off — damage, mechanical issues, anything unusual

That’s it. Each stop takes about an hour. Your total hours per week depend on how many stores are on your route.

What Makes This Different from Other Gig Work

• Consistent, scheduled route — not random job pickups

• Same stores every week, so you know exactly where you’re going

• $27/hr all-in — your mileage and travel are already baked into the rate

• Supplies provided — we give you everything you need to do the job

• Real support — a home office contact you can actually reach

This Is NOT a Repair Job

You’re not expected to fix anything. If a machine has a mechanical or technical issue, you flag it and we send a Service Technician. Your job is to keep things clean, documented, and reported — that’s where your value is.

What You Need to Get Started

• A reliable vehicle and a valid driver’s license

• A smartphone with a camera for photo submissions

• Attention to detail — you follow the checklist, every time

• You show up when you’re scheduled. That’s the most important thing.

No experience in water systems required. If you’ve done field services, retail merchandising, delivery routes, janitorial work, or anything similar — you’ll hit the ground running.

Who Thrives in This Role

This is a great fit if you’re already doing gig work and want something more predictable layered in, or if you’re looking for flexible part-time income that fits around your schedule. People who do well here tend to be:

• Self-starters who don’t need someone looking over their shoulder

• Detail-oriented — you notice things other people miss

• Reliable — your stores count on you showing up

• Good communicators — you keep the home office in the loop

How to Apply

Click “Apply Now” to be directed to our application. It only takes a few minutes to complete.

If we’re moving forward, you’ll hear from us by email. Interviews are conducted virtually via Microsoft Teams — we’ll send you a calendar invite with everything you need.

You can also view all open positions across our locations at:

freshpure.com/careers

title: WL - Production Planner
description:
Position Overview:The Planner is responsible for planning and scheduling all customer and inventory orders, including external vendor services such as plating and heat treating. This role ensures customer on-time delivery (OTD), maintains accurate system data, and optimizes resource capacity across internal manufacturing departments and external suppliers. The Planner works closely with Operations, Production, Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, and Customer Service to meet service, quality, and delivery objectives in alignment with Ward Leonard’s business goals.
In this function, you will:
Planning, Scheduling, and Order Management

Plan and schedule all customer and inventory orders, including outside services (plating, heat treating, and other vendor processes).
Maintain Customer On-Time Delivery by proactively monitoring order status and capacity.
Maintain and update all ship dates on Sales Orders to reflect current delivery commitments.
Review the Backlog Report, Open Orders, and Work-In-Process (WIP) status daily to ensure schedule integrity.
Review Shipping Reports to confirm on-time shipments and identify risks to delivery commitments.
Identify pull-in opportunities by reviewing Backlog Reports and, when permitted by the Sales Order and capacity, update VISUAL to ship early.
Check manufacturing capacity and, when feasible, reschedule orders in VISUAL for earlier completion and shipment.
Firm and release Work Orders (WO) in accordance with required release and want dates to ensure correct finish dates.
Create Work Orders in VISUAL MRP for all fabricated in-house parts, ensuring delivery dates meet Customer Sales Order requirements.
Plan and route RMA (Return Material Authorization) work, including creating WO’s for repairs and assigning internal repair work to the appropriate resources.

Capacity and Resource Management

Perform yearly, monthly, and ongoing capacity planning and drive capacity improvement initiatives.
Manage resource capacity by moving jobs to available resources, ensuring level loading and preventing bottlenecks.
Maintain spreadsheets and reports for Business Unit Director (BUD) and Sales to review WIP status and capacity.
Work closely with Production departments to track progress of Work Orders from release through shipment.

Supplier and Outside Services Coordination

Issue Requests for Quotation (RFQs) to vendors to obtain the best price, lead time, and terms for materials and services.
Issue Purchase Orders (POs) for materials and services required to support Work Orders, ensuring Supplier On-Time Delivery for all PO’s placed.
Schedule and coordinate outside services to meet internal production and customer delivery requirements.
Review Open Purchase Order Reports and MRB reports to identify outstanding parts and required actions.
Monitor vendor performance and follow up on overdue items to minimize impact to production and customer delivery.

Data Accuracy and Continuous Improvement

Ensure Item Master data (including lead-times, cost, and related planning parameters) is accurate, complete, and up to date.
Participate in pre-production meetings and review Bills of Material (BOMs) to support proper planning and scheduling of production Work Orders.
Support continuous improvement in planning, scheduling, and data integrity to enhance OTD, lead-time, and inventory performance.

Communication and Collaboration

Report OTD delays and schedule risks to Customer Service (for OEM and RMA) and other stakeholders as needed.
Collaborate with Quality and Manufacturing Engineering to resolve planning-related issues that affect schedule adherence.
Provide clear and timely communication to Operations, Sales, and other internal customers regarding order status and schedule changes.

Basic (Required) Qualifications:

U.S. Citizenship required due to government contracts.
High school diploma, GED, or trade school certificate.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in planning within an ERP/MRP-managed manufacturing environment.
Experience working in an ISO-certified environment (ISO 9001:2008 or ISO 9001:2015).
Working knowledge of an ERP/MRP system; experience with Infor VISUAL or equivalent strongly preferred.
Ability to interpret Sales Orders, Work Orders, BOMs, and related manufacturing documents.
Strong attention to detail with proven ability to maintain accurate planning and item master data.

Preferred Qualifications:

Associate’s degree in a technical, business, or related field.
Experience in a job-shop or engineer-to-order manufacturing environment.
Demonstrated experience in capacity planning and load leveling across multiple work centers.
Prior experience coordinating outside services and vendor-managed processes.

Position Criteria:

Strong organizational and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems and standard office software (e.g., Excel, Outlook, Word).
Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to collaborate across functions and levels.
Proven ability to work independently while maintaining alignment with Operations and business objectives.
Commitment to data integrity, schedule adherence, and continuous improvement.

Work Environment:

Work is primarily performed in an office setting with regular interaction with the manufacturing floor.
May require periodic visits to production areas and warehouses to review WIP, material status, and workflow.
Must comply with all site safety practices and requirements whenever in manufacturing or warehouse areas.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to sit at a desk for extended periods performing standard office work, including computer and phone use.
Ability to stand and walk in office and manufacturing environments as needed.
Must wear and comply with all required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) when in production areas, including but not limited to eye protection and safety shoes.
Must follow all applicable safety rules and procedures as defined in Company policies and posted instructions.

title: Senior Business Systems Analyst (InEight)
description:
Our Technology Solutions group is currently looking to add a Senior Business Systems Analyst (InEight) to our growing team, based in Edmonton, AB.

Reporting to the Director, AI & Business Transformation, we are seeking an experienced business systems professional with hands-on InEight construction project controls platform experience to own the platform's technical side. Working alongside the Project Manager for the InEight rollout, this position is the lead technical expert across all of InEight's modules; configuring, testing, and supporting the system as it expands across the business. It will also be expected to pick up ownership of other business applications over time as our systems portfolio grows.

Please Note: This position will require occasional travel between Valard's Edmonton and Calgary offices (up to 10% of time).

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Own the technical/application side of InEight end to end for the life of the platform: initial rollout of new modules, ongoing configuration, and the changes and platform support that follow, working in partnership with the InEight module business owners rather than in place of them. Once a module is established, routine user setup moves to the support team; training and onboarding new teams stays in scope
  • Serve as the lead technical expert across all InEight modules, handling configuration and testing alongside Valard's project manager for the InEight rollout
  • Work with Valard's integrations team to help understand and scope InEight's data and integration requirements, translating business and process needs into what each integration actually needs to do
  • Act as the primary point of contact for InEight across the business, answering questions from project teams, business leads, and the technology steering committee directly
  • Help shape the sequencing and design of InEight's module rollout
  • Take on ownership of additional business applications as they come up: this seat is expected to grow beyond InEight, not stay boxed to it
  • Rapidly build proficiency across InEight's full module set (Schedule, Document, Control, Plan, Progress, and others as they roll out), including starting from limited experience in a given module

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience configuring or administering InEight
  • Experience with a comparable construction/EPC platform (e.g. Procore, Aconex), in an IT administrator or implementation capacity, not just as an end user, may be considered
  • Background in a technical or IT-facing role (e.g. business systems analyst, application support, systems/platform administration, or software implementation)
  • Experience running UAT and training sessions with non-technical users, and translating business needs into system requirements
  • Proven ability to take at least one module or platform from configuration through testing and UAT to go-live
  • Demonstrated experience with IT change management, access governance, and documentation standards
  • Experience with AI tools like Claude (for configuration, documentation, and testing)

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive and competitive total rewards package that incorporates a complete range of employee benefits, including a 5% RRSP matching program, to ensure you have the tools necessary to manage, maintain, and improve your health and wellbeing.

Valard Construction is Canada’s premier utility contractor providing comprehensive EPC+ (engineering, procurement, construction) and maintenance services to utilities, independent power producers, mining, oil and gas industries and rural electric associations. We have the capabilities, knowledge, and resources to take on any project, any size, any complexity, anywhere. title: Senior Oncology Scientist
description:
About Clear Labs

Clear Labs builds an end-to-end, FDA-cleared next-generation sequencing (NGS) diagnostics platform. Our system, Clear Dx, combines automated sample-to-report workflows with an assay menu spanning oncology and infectious disease testing. We're a hands-on team building hardware, software, and wet-lab science together, and we're looking for senior scientists who want to own real customer and partner relationships, not just advise on them.

Position Summary

We're hiring a Senior Oncology Scientist to serve as Clear Labs' internal oncology subject matter expert — advising our assay development, automation, and systems integration teams on oncology biology, genomics, and clinical relevance as we build out our oncology assay menu. This is primarily an internal scientific role: shaping internal decisions on assay design and clinical relevance comes first, with select customer, partner, and conference-facing science as a secondary part of the role.

Reports to: COO & Chief Scientific Officer

Location: San Carlos, CA

Travel: Occasional travel required.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Serve as the internal oncology subject matter expert, advising Assay Development, Automation, and Systems Integration on oncology biology, genomics, and clinical relevance as new panels and workflows are developed.
  • Stay current on oncology genomics literature, competitive assays, and clinical guidelines, and translate that knowledge into internal scientific recommendations.
  • Provide scientific input on assay design, panel content, and evidentiary requirements for oncology offerings (e.g., companion diagnostics, comprehensive genomic profiling, MRD).
  • Serve as an internal bridge between R&D/assay science and other functions, helping translate technical work into language that lands with clinical, commercial, and partner audiences.
  • Support customers and partner reference laboratories with oncology assay application science and protocol troubleshooting as needed (secondary responsibility).
  • Represent Clear Labs' oncology science with key opinion leaders and at a select set of key conferences, and provide scientific input during partner evaluations (secondary responsibility).

Requirements

  • PhD (or equivalent industry experience) in oncology genomics, molecular pathology, or a closely related field.
  • Prior experience as an internal scientific advisor, subject matter expert, or R&D scientist supporting assay or product development in oncology genomics.
  • Comfortable advising cross-functional technical teams on oncology biology and translating that into practical assay and product decisions.
  • Prior experience with companion diagnostics, comprehensive genomic profiling, or MRD assay workflows strongly preferred.
  • Some prior experience in an Applications Scientist, Field Application Scientist, or Medical Science Liaison-type role is a plus, but not the primary focus of this position.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; occasional travel for key conferences and partner engagements — this is not a majority-travel role.

Benefits

  • Salary range: $145,000 - $185,000
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer-Sponsored Basic Life/AD&D, Long Term Disability
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Discretionary Time Off
  • Stock Option Plan
  • Lunch stipend for days at headquarters

For more information, please review the E-Verify Participation Poster (English/Spanish) and the Right to Work Poster (English/Spanish).

title: Production Lead
description:
Job Summary:

As our Production Lead, you will have accountability and responsibility for performance optimization of all CO2 and on-site nitrogen plants in the region that are not directly operated from the Messer Remote Operations Centre.

Activities include responding to known deficiencies, responding to current issues, proactively identifying and resolving performance gaps and reporting on plant performance on a periodic basis.

Why Messer?

Messer is the world’s largest privately held industrial gases company and what we do matters because it is woven into every part of life, from the medical gases that patients rely on to the essential elements needed to safely and sustainably produce the goods our communities depend on.

The true strength of Messer is our people—at every level and in every role.

Join us and take pride in the impact you will make by providing solutions essential to our world and lives. Reach your highest potential at our stable, inclusive company with diverse opportunities in a growing industry, supported by people who care.

title: Temporary Counselor
description:
Temporary Counselor

Full-time

Pinnacle’s Voice: A Tale of Transformation & Recovery

“I found myself like a lot of people in a position I never thought I would be in. I needed help bad… It all started with a call… one of the easiest and hardest things I’ve ever done. Every day I wake up and think how good it feels and how lucky I am to have found this place.”

-Patient, Pinnacle Treatment Centers

About Us: Pinnacle Treatment Centers is a leading provider of comprehensive addiction treatment services, committed to transforming lives through compassionate care. Our approach is rooted in evidence-based practices, focusing on the holistic well-being of our patients, and treating our teammates with the same level of individualized compassion and empathy. We believe in providing a supportive and inclusive environment for both our patients and our dedicated team of professionals. Pinnacle transforms the lives of more than 35,000 individuals daily resulting in a network of care spanning across the country.

Position Overview: As a Counselor, you will play a crucial role in the recovery journey of our patients. Pinnacle’s unique approach combines compassionate care with innovative treatment methods to address the diverse needs of individuals seeking help for substance use disorders. Join us in making a positive impact on the lives of those we serve.

Teammate Appreciation Benefits: At Pinnacle Treatment Centers, we value our teammates and offer a variety of benefits to support their personal and professional growth.

1. Variable Pay Structure: Competitive compensation based on experience, education, and licensure.

2. Defined Career Pathing: Clear advancement opportunities through our Counselor Tier Program, designed to reward achievement in education, licensure, and credentials.

3. Bonus Incentives: Recognizing and rewarding quality patient care with monthly performance-based bonuses.

4. STAR LRP Eligibility: 90% of our facilities are eligible for the Student Loan Repayment Program. This federal program selects applicants to forgive 100% of their student loans.

5. Continuing Education: Free access to over 600 CEU courses to enhance your skills and knowledge.

6. Paid Time Off: 18 days of PTO, sick leave, and 8 paid holidays to maintain a healthy work-life balance.

7. Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Initiatives: Be part of a workforce that reflects the diversity of our patient population.

8. Free Clinical Supervision: Available based on licensure and availability to support your professional growth.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provides orientation to new patients to the programs’ rules, policies, procedures, and patients' rights.
  • Conduct Intakes, Discharge Planning, Initial Assessments, and Initial Treatment Plans professionally and within time guidelines as required by applicable federal and state regulation, CARF guidelines and Pinnacle Policies.
  • Involve patients in the assessment, treatment planning, and intervention aspects of treatment, which provides the patient with a sense of entitlement to their own recovery.
  • Administer the biopsychosocial assessment, which evaluates all areas of patients' lives, including their addictions, medical and mental health history, socioeconomics, legal, etc. at intake and on an ongoing basis.
  • Recognize and utilize patients’ Strengths, Needs, Ability, and Preferences (SNAP), to develop and implement individualized Treatment Plans that effectively help patients to meet their short & long-term goals. • Determine the clinical necessity of counseling services based on the clinical assessment and evaluation of the patients.
  • Monitor closely, and document any change of circumstances with the patients, especially as it relates to matters that may affect their recovery, identifying and addressing relapse indicators to promote relapse prevention interventions in an early stage.
  • Comply with and implement the Medical Q.A (Quality Assurance) and Clinical Risk Management Policies, including:
    • Evaluate the patients for any high-risk conditions (e.g., liver failure, pregnancy, overdose, bipolar, schizophrenia, etc.), which may endanger the patient (suicidal) or other parties (homicidal).
    • Administer the BAM-R, C-SSRS, GAD-7, and PHQ-9 screening tools to determine the severity of the patient's mental/emotional status.
    • Evaluate the risk factors concerning each such case, considering the appropriateness of, and professionalism in treating such individuals in an OTP in comparison to treatment in a residential facility or other treatment modalities.
    • Review and ask about other practitioners' involvement in the treatment of these high-risk conditions. Recommend immediate referral to such a specialist in case of need. Request the patient sign a waiver for release of information which will allow communication with the other practitioner in case of need (e.g., deterioration of the patient’s condition).
    • Flag high-risk patients to the Medical Directors, Physician Extenders, and Regional Clinical Leadership (RCL) and highlight the conditions concerned.
    • Refer such patients to the Medical Directors, Physician Extenders or RCLs (Regional Clinical Leadership) based on the urgency, utilizing the informal Referral Policy or the scheduled Treatment Team/Case Conference session.
    • Review physician notes, following the Medical Directors or Physician Extenders’ session with the patient, verifying that they noted and addressed the high-risk factor, or otherwise bring it immediately to the attention of the supervising counselor, as well as the clinic manager, until the matter’s proper and professional handling by the physician or physician extender.
    • Advise, in writing, other staff members (including the clinic manager, supervising counselor, dispensing nurse and front office) of high-risk patients and their condition. Maintain and circulate minutes from treatment team/case conference sessions to the other staff members.
  • Provide professional counseling and referral services by:
    • Addressing patients’ clinical and special needs by maintaining referrals to specialized (“second tier”) services rendered by physicians, physician extenders and counselors within Aegis, as well as referrals to Keys to Recovery (or other twelve-step) support groups, and other community resources (e.g., agencies and practitioners outside of Aegis), acting as a liaison to these agencies, as necessary.
    • Providing individual and group counseling as clinically necessary, to address the problem issues identified in the Initial Assessment and Treatment Plans. The counseling service will include protocols for the treatment of Relapse Prevention, Peer Pressure, Anger Management, Domestic Violence, Parenting, Family Preservation, Vocational Rehabilitation, etc.
    • Utilizing advanced counseling techniques such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, etc.
    • Scheduling regular counseling sessions with patients; issue patient appointment cards and record scheduled or rescheduled sessions in EHR scheduler.
    • Documenting counseling entries, including signature and date, as required by applicable federal and state regulations, CARF guidelines and Pinnacle policies.
    • Engaging in Community Relations and Outreach efforts.
    • Attending all recommended training including Physician Training of Counselors, RCL training, and case conferences with the program physicians and physician assistants.
    • Collecting research data when requested.
    • Observing the collection of patients’ urine samples when required
    • Attend team meetings and complete all training courses timely as required.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Counselor I: $20/hour to $22/hour

  • Possess an associate degree in relevant field and has the registration/credentials necessary to provide counseling services to our patient population.
  • Kern County requires a bachelor’s degree or High school diploma/GED with 75% certification education.

Preferred
Possess a bachelor's degree or higher

Counselor II: $22/hour to $25/hour

  • Possess an associate degree in a relevant field or a majority of approved counselor certification courses, license, or certification necessary to provide counseling services to our patient population. Kern County requires a bachelor's degree or 75% of required counselor certification courses)
  • Possess counselor registration/certification by a “Certifying Organization: recognized by the Department of Alcohol and Drug Programs. Proof of registration is required immediately once employed with a California Alcohol and Drug Program certifying body. Employees must be registered prior to providing any counseling services per the DHCS (Department of Health Care Services).
  • 2-5 years of experience OR Master level

Counselor III: $25/hour to $28/hour (Certified) & $28/hour - $31/hour (Licensed)

  • Degrees must include being licensed, licensed eligible, or certified. Clinical skills must be effective in complex cases. Along with the below:
  • Possess certification as an Alcohol and Other Drug Counselor with a CA approved certification agency or current credentials as licensed or license-eligible with the Board of Behavioral Sciences or the Board of Psychology. If license-eligible, must maintain the Board’s requirements to be able to practice including receiving the necessary amount of clinical supervision by a Board approved supervisor.
  • Proof of licensure or certification by a State approved regulatory agency is required immediately once employed. Employees must be credentialed prior to providing any counseling services per the DHCS (Department of Health Care Services).

Join our Team & Start Saving Lives Today

title: Junior Civil Technologist, Onsite Wastewater Team
description:
Are you ready to apply your technical expertise to projects that protect public health and the environment in rural communities?

We’re looking for a Civil Engineering Technologist to join our Onsite Wastewater Group within Burnside’s Environmental sector. This role is based in our Mississauga office, with flexibility to work from other Burnside offices depending on candidate fit. You’ll support the delivery of practical, field-informed onsite wastewater solutions and play a hands-on role in projects from site investigation through design and regulatory approval.

This is an opportunity to work closely with experienced engineers and technologists on technically complex projects where your contributions directly impact real-world outcomes.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you’ll support and contribute to the successful delivery of onsite wastewater and rural servicing projects by:

  • Preparing design-ready drawings and technical documentation for septic and small to medium-scale onsite wastewater systems in support of permitting and approvals
  • Assisting with and participating in field investigations, including test pits, site evaluations, and construction reviews, applying sound judgment and attention to detail
  • Translating field data and design concepts into accurate drawings using AutoCAD and Civil 3D
  • Coordinating with engineers, fellow technologists, clients, and regulators to help move projects from concept through approval
  • Supporting project schedules and budgets through effective time management and organized work practices
  • Reviewing drawings, reports, and calculations to ensure quality, accuracy, and compliance with applicable standards
  • Contributing to a collaborative team environment and supporting other project needs as required

What You’ll Bring

Education & Credentials

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering Technology or a related discipline
  • Eligibility for or current membership with OACETT
  • Valid Ontario driver’s licence and access to a reliable vehicle

Technical Skills & Experience

  • Proficiency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D
  • Experience or strong interest in onsite sewage systems and rural wastewater servicing
  • Ability to integrate field observations and data into clear, accurate designs
  • Familiarity with the Ontario Building Code is considered an asset

You’re Likely a Great Fit If You:

  • Enjoy applying technical skills to real-world, field-driven projects
  • Are comfortable balancing office-based design work with field activities
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with team members, clients, and stakeholders
  • Take pride in accuracy, quality, and delivering practical solutions
  • Manage your time effectively and take ownership of your deliverables

Salary Range: $60,000 - $75,000

The final compensation offered will be based on factors such as relevant experience, skills, internal equity, and market conditions.

Position Type: New Position

Why Choose Burnside?

Are you interested in working for an employer with a 5-decade track record of building a great reputation both internally with their staff and externally with their clients? The Burnside team is a supportive group of colleagues that work together to provide value and service to our clients, while extending care to each other. We know that our employees are our greatest asset, and thus we strive to provide a positive work/life balance.

We offer:

  • A collaborative culture where friendship, honesty and respect are part of our core values and practices
  • Flexible working hours and office locations, including hybrid working opportunities
  • A competitive compensation and benefits package
  • RRSP company matching plan
  • Career growth and professional development opportunities
  • Potential for performance-driven bonusing
  • Active social committees
  • A welcoming, positive, and inclusive work environment

We are an equal opportunity employer committed to valuing diversity in the workplace and we welcome resumes from all qualified candidates. Burnside will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the entire recruitment, assessment, and selection process, as required. If you are a person with a disability and require an accommodation during these processes, please contact our Human Resources department.

Company Profile – More about us:

Founded in 1970, R.J. Burnside & Associates Limited is a growing values-driven Canadian employee-owned, led and operated Civil and Environmental Engineering Consulting Firm with over 450 professional, technical and support staff. Our consistent commitment towards investing in technology advancements and training, in addition to encouraging and promoting professional development, has enabled our firm to meet our ongoing and stated goal of continual improvement.

We actively seek to develop relationships with a broad and diversified client base in the Public, Private and Indigenous sectors. We work on a variety of projects throughout Canada, with 12 office locations (11 in Ontario and one in Manitoba).

Burnside has expertise in many technical disciplines beyond our core civil engineering focus including air and noise, asset management, bridges & culverts, building sciences, environmental planning and ecology, GIS, hydrogeology, land development, landscape architecture, municipal engineering, municipal drainage, solid waste, stormwater management, structures, traffic, transportation planning and design, water and wastewater and well drilling & diagnostics.

title: Coordinator, Prevention Services
description:

title: Director of Communication
description:
Network Health’s success is rooted in its mission to create healthy and strong Wisconsin communities. Network Health is seeking a Director of Communications to lead how we communicate internally, externally and at the executive level. This highly visible role will serve as a strategic communications advisor to the CEO and senior leadership team and help shape Network Health’s voice with employees, members, media, owners, boards and other key stakeholders.

The Director will bring exceptional writing, sound judgment and communications leadership to a growing and increasingly visible organization—creating an integrated communications strategy across audiences and channels while partnering effectively across Marketing, Human Resources, Legal, operational teams and external agency partners.

Location: Candidates must reside in the state of Wisconsin for consideration. This position is eligible to work on-site at our corporate office in Brookfield or in Menasha. Regular travel between the offices is expected.

Hours: 1.0 FTE, 40 hours per week, 8am-5pm Monday through Friday

Check out our 2025 Community Report to learn a little more about the difference our employees make in the communities we live and work in. As an employee, you will have the opportunity to work hard and have fun while getting paid to volunteer in your local neighborhood. You too, can be part of the team and making a difference. Apply to this position to learn more about our team.

Job Responsibilities:

Executive Communications

  • Serve as a trusted communications advisor and writing partner to the CEO and senior leadership team.
  • Develop executive-level communications including speeches, remarks, talking points, presentations, key messages and interview preparation materials.
  • Learn and authentically write in the CEO’s voice, supporting a highly active executive presence across boards, speaking engagements, community leadership and local, regional and national media opportunities.
  • Prepare and support the CEO and other executives for media interviews, public appearances and high-profile engagements, including attending select interviews and engagements as a communications advisor.
  • Support the development of President’s Reports, Board of Directors presentations and other executive-level communications, translating complex business information into clear, concise and compelling narratives.
  • Partner with the CEO and senior leadership to identify and shape priority updates for Network Health’s owners, owner boards and other key stakeholders.

Internal & Employee Communications

  • Develop and lead an enterprise-wide employee communications strategy that defines how Network Health informs, engages and connects employees across channels, audiences and locations.
  • Own the communications strategy and editorial direction for InNetwork, Network Health’s employee intranet, ensuring it serves as a relevant, timely and useful destination for organizational news, leadership communication, resources and employee engagement.
  • Establish an intentional channel strategy for employee communications, clarifying the role of InNetwork, email, newsletters, leadership communications, employee forums and other platforms so employees receive the right information through the right channel at the right time.
  • Serve as the primary communications partner to Human Resources and senior leadership for employee-facing communications.
  • Lead the planning and execution of Network Health’s quarterly employee forums, including agenda development, executive messaging, presentations, content coordination and overall program flow.
  • Develop and manage recurring leadership communications, including monthly leadership talking points and tools that help leaders communicate consistently across the organization.
  • Lead the development and management of the internal Marketing newsletter, identifying stories and content that showcase the work, impact and priorities of the Marketing team.
  • Continually evaluate employee communications effectiveness and recommend improvements based on engagement, feedback and organizational needs.

Member & Enterprise Communications Strategy

  • Help develop an integrated communications strategy that connects employee, member and stakeholder communications while recognizing the distinct needs, channels and objectives of each audience.
  • Partner with member communications, Marketing and operational teams to improve clarity, consistency, relevance and coordination of communications across the member journey.
  • Serve as a strategic communications consultant for Network Health’s member and email newsletter programs, providing guidance on content strategy, messaging, editorial approach, audience relevance and overall communications effectiveness.
  • Identify opportunities to improve communications governance, channel strategy and audience experience across the organization.

External Communications, Media Relations & Reputation

  • Serve as the central point of contact for all media inquiries and external communications requests.
  • Manage inbound media requests, determine appropriate organizational response and coordinate with subject matter experts, executive leadership, Legal and agency partners.
  • Lead Network Health’s relationship with its external PR/communications agency, setting priorities and ensuring agency resources are strategically deployed.
  • Develop proactive earned media strategies and identify compelling opportunities to tell Network Health’s story across local, regional and national outlets.
  • Lead crisis and issues communications planning and response, bringing calm, speed, judgment and consistency to high-stakes situations.
  • Develop media preparation materials, key messages and anticipated questions, and provide real-time counsel to leaders during sensitive or high-profile situations.
  • Help protect and strengthen Network Health’s reputation by ensuring external communications are timely, accurate, coordinated and aligned.

Content & Editorial Governance

  • Serve as a member of the content/editorial governance team for Network Health’s print publications, helping establish editorial standards, messaging priorities, voice and consistency across member- and stakeholder-facing materials.
  • Help establish and maintain communications standards, voice and editorial discipline across channels while partnering with channel owners and subject matter experts.
  • Bring an enterprise communications perspective to major print, digital and email communications to ensure content is clear, coordinated, audience-centered and aligned with Network Health’s brand.

Owner & Stakeholder Communications

  • Support proactive communications with Network Health’s ownership organizations and their boards regarding organizational priorities, accomplishments, developments and issues of strategic importance.
  • Partner with executive leadership to determine which organizational stories and updates should be elevated to owners and key stakeholders.
  • Ensure owner and stakeholder communications are proactive, concise, strategically relevant and aligned with broader organizational messaging.

Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, or a related field
  • 7+ years of experience in corporate communications, public relations, or media relations

Network Health is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

May assist in all phases of the projects, from procurement through close out.

  • Create, maintain and/or control all project documentation. Coordinate the distribution of job documents to both internal and external parties, as necessary or as appropriate per company procedures.

title: Planner (Temporary 18Months)
description:
Position Summary
This is an entry- to mid-level professional Planning position that, with progressive experience, requires an increasing degree of project management responsibility, and the implementation of planning strategies, statutory documents, and municipal policy. The position requires a thorough knowledge of related Acts and Regulations and the Alberta planning process. The Planner primarily works independently working with applicants and stakeholders, and in preparing reports and presentations to Council.
Core Accountabilities

Interact with the public on an ongoing basis through telephone and written enquiries as may be required to convey Planning information to citizens and other individuals and groups.
Review, process and manage redesignation, subdivision, and occasional development permit files for compliance with policy, regulations, and technical requirements. Files are typically of a low- to moderate- complexity, with the occasional requirement to process more complex applications.
Support the Manager, Supervisor and Senior Planners on department projects and significant planning files through research, engagement and other work.
Prepare and present reports to Council, County committees, and to appeal boards as required.
Interpret and implement relevant regional, intermunicipal, and County policies, standards and legislation and formulate administrative recommendations for approving authority.
Review and respond to referrals from internal departments and government agencies.
Assist in the monitoring and amendment of the County’s Land Use Bylaw to ensure development regulations and processes are up to date.
Participate in internal department process improvement initiatives.
Mentor more junior staff from time-to-time and act as a resource for other team members according to expertise within the department.
Assist in the preparation of municipal policy plans, including Intermunicipal Development Plans, Municipal Development Plans, and Area Structure Plans.
Monitor and review Municipal and Intermunicipal Planning Legislation, policy, processes, plans, and initiatives.
Prepare and present reports, materials, and opinions as a representative of Rocky View County to other government and non-government agencies and committees as required.
Work in accordance with the requirements established by the RVC Health and Safety Program and the Alberta OHS Act, Regulation and Code.
Take reasonable care to protect their health and safety and other people at or in the vicinity of the worksite while they are working.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Position Requirements
A bachelor’s degree in planning or related field is required along with a minimum of 2 to 4 years of demonstrated professional experience in Planning or a related field is required (consideration for Land Use certificate and 2+ years of Planning experience). This is in combination with a demonstrated track record of working collaboratively in a team environment, and a record of successfully completed assignments. Scope of the experience should include a demonstrated awareness and knowledge of municipal planning, and a working knowledge of the provincial planning and legislative framework.

Understands and applies provincial and municipal planning policies, legislation, processes, procedures, and statutory Planning documents.
Interprets and applies relevant municipal/provincial policy to the processing of applications and the development and preparation of planning documents with no major oversights.
Works independently or as part of a team to seek out and synthesize information resources in a clear and concise fashion in the processing of applications.
Demonstrates strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills with attention to detail and accuracy.
Demonstrates knowledge, interpretation, and application of subdivision design, site planning and environmental planning concepts and their applications in the processing of planning applications.
Works collaboratively with and communicates effectively and positively with other team members, departments, and external municipal and provincial government personnel.
Possess and exhibit strong skills in presentations to Council, community associations and government departments as required.
Manages time effectively to juggle multiple deadlines and tasks and is required to work within irregular and tight time frames.
Takes initiative to identify and resolve problems regarding planning applications that may be unique and complex.
Makes sound decisions by using rational and logical judgment that reflects an understanding of the consequences of decisions.
Able to manage time-sensitive and politically sensitive matters and to think and react quickly and effectively to problems that may arise from time to time.
Eligibility for Full Membership with the Canadian Institute of Planners (CIP) is considered an asset.
Previous related experience particularly in a public sector environment is preferred.
Proficient in MS Office suite.
Possess a valid class 5 driver’s license.
