title: Quality Technician - 2nd Shift
description:
Quality Technician - 2nd Shift Hourly + Differential

Monday - Friday 2:30 p.m. - 11:00 p.m.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Quality Technician will examine materials for flaws and deviations from original product specifications. This role will inspect, accept, or reject products for durability, function, customer satisfaction, and overall quality. The Quality Technician will perform various quality control related inspection and verification activities on raw material, in-process products, and final products to ensure the product meets required safety and quality standards as required in stay in compliance with ISO/IATF standards. This position will work with and communicate to all various functions including but not limited to distribution, engineering, purchasing, production, quality, and suppliers as required.

CORE FUNCTIONS

· Issue In-Process Check Sheet to areas producing OEM and Aftermarket programs.

· Complete 2-hour monitoring of process, visual inspection and measurement data collection for critical characteristics, document results into statistical software and maintain runs charting.

· Support Internal and External audits.

· Report trends, shifts, and jumps in process to Quality Assurance Management.

· Inspect and test raw materials and in-process products, and final products.

· Monitor testing procedures, interpret results, capture data into program software, report out on inspection results,

· Administer data and Document Control responsibilities in compliance with ISO/IATF standards.

· Perform process layered, product and/or dispatch audits – document and report results.

· Perform MSA studies, recall and calibration on instruments used to ensure product quality per MSA, recall, and calibration schedule.

· Participate in creation of PPAP packages – specifically dimensional layouts, IMDS inputs, quarantine management and in-coming inspection (if applicable).

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS

Education and Experience

· High school diploma, GED, or equivalent experience is required.

· 3-5 years in a quality or manufacturing related position is required.

· 2 years of ISO and/or IATF experience required.

· Injection molding machine experience preferred; minimum of 1 year.

Required Licenses

· Valid driver’s license preferred.

Skills, Abilities, and Knowledge

· Skilled in auditing and computer skills.

· Skilled in general PC operation/navigation and application-specific experience including SharePoint and Microsoft Office 365 applications (MS Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint). Minitab or other Statistical Software and AIAG documents.

· Ability to understand the importance of standards.

· Ability to distinguish between normal and abnormal conditions and react/report accordingly.

· Demonstrated ability to read, analyze, and interpret measurement data points – Statistical Process Control (SPC).

· Ability to effectively recognize a trend, shift and/or jump in data points and react/report accordingly.

· Knowledge of ISO and/or IATF auditing experience preferred.

Travel

title: Senior Director, Cloud Platforms
description:
About the Role
The Senior Director, Cloud Platforms will own Magnit's migration from on-premise infrastructure into the public cloud and build the cloud platform that our engineering organization runs on. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will set the strategy, then work shoulder-to-shoulder with your teams in the code, the pipelines, and the Kubernetes manifests. You will own the data center exit roadmap, the AWS-first landing zones underneath it, and the paved-road developer platform (GitLab CI/CD, Argo CD, EKS, Terraform) that makes doing the right thing the easy thing for product teams. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, you will partner across Engineering, Security, Data, and Operations to move Magnit to an API-first, cloud-native architecture while improving reliability, security posture, and unit economics along the way.

What You Will Do
Cloud Migration & Data Center Exit

Own the end-to-end on-premise to public cloud migration roadmap — wave planning, sequencing, readiness validation, cutover, and stabilization — with clear milestones, exit criteria, and success metrics.

Lead application portfolio assessment and disposition (rehost, replatform, refactor, retire, retain), building the business case and target architecture for each wave.

Design and operate secure, multi-account cloud foundations: landing zones, identity, networking, compute, storage, and Kubernetes.

Act as the integration layer across infrastructure, application engineering, security, networking, finance, and vendor partners to keep migration waves on schedule and de-risked.

Retire on-premise footprint on a committed timeline, and report progress, risk, and dependencies to executive leadership in plain business terms.

Platform Engineering & Developer Experience

Run the cloud platform as an internal product with product teams as its customers — not as a ticket queue.

Deliver golden paths for service creation, CI/CD, secrets, observability, and security through reusable templates, modules, and self-service tooling, with sensible escape hatches for teams with genuine edge cases.

Own GitLab-based source control and CI/CD standards, Kubernetes manifests, and GitOps delivery via Argo CD.

Drive infrastructure as code and policy as code as the only way infrastructure changes, eliminating manual configuration and drift.

Advance containerized microservices and serverless patterns on AWS (EKS, Lambda, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, ALB/NLB) as the default for new standalone services.

Measure and improve developer experience using DORA metrics, time-to-first-deploy, platform adoption, and direct developer feedback.

Partner with the enterprise workflow effort to shift manual, human-in-the-loop processes to software-defined workflows (Temporal), removing people from steps that do not need them.

Reliability, Observability & Operations

Establish the SRE charter: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, incident response, blameless postmortems, and disaster recovery with tested RTO/RPO targets.

Consolidate fragmented monitoring into a unified observability platform across metrics, logs, traces, and alerting, standardizing instrumentation on OpenTelemetry and structured logging.

Lead observability platform direction and rationalization (New Relic as the strategic direction alongside existing Datadog usage), including agent fleet management, telemetry governance, and cost control.

Move the organization from reactive monitoring to proactive, data-driven observability across business uptime, engineering excellence, and digital experience, with dashboards that serve both engineers and executives.

Drive down MTTD and MTTR, and tie reliability goals directly to customer experience and business KPIs.

Security, Networking & Resilience

Embed security and compliance by design: least-privilege IAM, secrets management, encryption in transit and at rest, and continuous control monitoring.

Own cloud network architecture end to end — VPC design, segmentation, transit connectivity, private link patterns, DNS, and native load balancing (ALB/NLB).

Operate edge protection with Cloudflare for WAF, DDoS mitigation, bot management, and DNS, in partnership with the security organization.

Integrate enterprise identity into platform access patterns (Okta for external user authentication, Microsoft Entra for internal).

Partner with the CISO organization on cloud security posture, audit readiness, and operational risk management.

FinOps & Vendor Management

Establish cloud cost transparency, tagging discipline, showback/chargeback, and forecasting the business can trust.

Build unit economics (cost per workload, per environment, per client) and run a standing optimization backlog that lowers total cost of ownership as consumption grows.

Manage cloud, observability, and tooling vendor relationships, contracts, commitments, and renewals.

Leadership & Influence

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing global organization spanning cloud engineering, platform engineering, SRE, and network engineering.

Set the engineering bar through architecture review, code review, and hands-on participation — credibility at this level comes from doing the work, not describing it.

Define clear ownership boundaries between platform and product teams, and the engagement model for prioritization, funding, and decision-making.

Translate complex technical trade-offs for technical, non-technical, and executive audiences, including CIO and CDTO staff.

Champion adoption of AI-assisted engineering and AI-driven operations, and ensure the platform supports enterprise AI, GenAI, and analytics workloads.

What You Will Need

12+ years of progressive experience in cloud, infrastructure, or platform engineering, with at least 5 years leading engineers and engineering managers.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred, equivalent professional experience considered.

Demonstrated success leading a large-scale on-premise to public cloud migration or data center exit in a complex, matrixed organization — owned it, not adjacent to it.

Proven experience building or operating an internal developer platform at scale, with real adoption to show for it.

Genuinely hands-on: you can still read and write the Terraform, the pipeline config, and the Kubernetes manifests — and in this role you will.

Deep expertise in Kubernetes (EKS strongly preferred) and GitOps delivery patterns.

Strong cloud networking depth — VPC architecture, segmentation, native load balancing, DNS, and hybrid connectivity.

Experience with cloud security and edge protection, including WAF and DDoS prevention.

Track record of driving adoption and non-trivial organizational change, with comfort operating in ambiguity.

Ability to convey complex technical information to technical, non-technical, and executive audiences.

Preferred tech stack experience includes:

Cloud: AWS-first (not AWS-only); Azure for internal IT and Power BI workloads

Containers & Orchestration: Kubernetes/EKS, Argo CD, Helm, serverless patterns (Lambda)

CI/CD & IaC: GitLab source control and CI/CD, Terraform, policy as code

AWS Services: DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, ALB/NLB, IAM, S3, CloudWatch

Networking & Edge: Cloudflare (WAF, DDoS, DNS), VPC design, transit and private connectivity

Data: PostgreSQL (relational standard), Snowflake (enterprise data warehouse), Power BI

Observability: New Relic, Datadog, OpenTelemetry

Workflow & Integration: Temporal, API-first service design, ServiceNow

Identity: Okta (external), Microsoft Entra (internal)

Languages: Python primary; polyglot where the use case warrants

Compensation: Salary range is $220,000-$230,000 USD annually.
Salary rates are based on experience, skills, and geographic location.

title: Associate Programmatic Buyer
description:
About the role

The Associate Programmatic Buyer is a foundational contributor and key support lead on the digital media buying team, responsible for assisting media leads with the planning, trafficking, and platform execution of client campaigns across programmatic channels.

This role serves as an entry-to-mid level launchpad to build hands-on expertise in digital media operations and programmatic execution—learning campaign setup across Demand-Side Platforms, assisting with campaign maintenance, and taking on increasing ownership over time under the direct guidance of Senior Media Buyers and leads. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, brings a solutions-first mindset to task execution, and approaches their work with exceptional attention to detail, radical accountability, and an eagerness to learn.


Time Zone Requirement: Must be able to work standard business hours in PT, MT, CT, or ET


Key Responsibilities

Planning & Buying Support

  • Assists Senior Media Buyers in drafting client-focused digital media plans, gathering partner forecast/abilities, and entering finalized plans into campaign management systems with accuracy.
  • Leads end-to-end planning, execution, and strategy for accounts or test budgets, taking full ownership of campaign lifecycle management under light supervision.
  • Maintains campaign budget tracking files, updates rolling opportunity logs, and organizes media specs across active accounts.
  • Supports buying and rate negotiations led by senior team members, learning negotiation techniques and agency pricing benchmarks over time.
  • Gains foundational exposure to programmatic strategy, learning how targeting parameters, bid strategies, and inventory selection function within DSP platforms.

Campaign Execution, DSP Setup & Trafficking

  • Serves as the primary operational support for campaign trafficking—reviewing creative specs, generating tracking parameters/pixels, and performing launch QA across platforms.
  • Executes hands-on platform setup in DSPs (e.g., The Trade Desk, DV360) under supervisor review—uploading creative assets, configuring targeting parameters, and linking deal IDs.
  • Monitors and owns daily campaign pacing and performance fluctuations. Ability to proactively make pacing adjustments and work up to performance optimizations and insights to support Sr. Buyers.
  • Assists with mid-campaign and wrap-up performance reporting, pulling data from platforms and organizing insights for client presentations.
  • Handles ad hoc operational tasks with flexibility and a can-do attitude to support overall media team efficiency.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience in-platform bidable media, including ownership of pacing, making recommendations and optimizations.

  • Baseline familiarity with digital media channels (streaming audio, display, video, programmatic) or ad tech platforms is a plus.

  • Comfortable operating in a cross-functional team environment, collaborating with accounts, client stakeholders and Supporting Sr. Buyers..

Our Team Culture

title: Men's Community Life Lead
description:
OVERVIEW

Portland Rescue Mission is seeking a Men’s Community Life Lead. This gifted servant will personify relationship, order, responsibility, and community building, as they join a Christ-centered team with an award-winning culture and a commitment to serving others.

Are you ready to transform and be transformed as you lead men recovering from homelessness and addiction towards healthy relationships with God and others leading towards long-term success? If so, we invite you to thoughtfully consider this unique opportunity.

EMPLOYMENT DETAILS

  • How to apply: We ask all applicants to apply through the Portland Rescue Mission online application form found on our careers page:

    https://portlandrescuemission.hiringthing.com/job/1062305/men-s-community-life-lead

  • Status: Full-Time, Nonexempt
  • Hours: Saturday and Sunday: alternating AM and PM shifts. Monday-Wednesday: 2:00pm-10:30pm.
  • Pay Rate: $20.70-$23.00 an hour
  • Benefits: Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, 3 weeks PTO, 10 paid holidays and matching retirement opportunities.
  • Location: The Harbor - 10336 NE Wygant St.
    • Virtual Tour:

THE PLACE

The Harbor is a community of refuge and restoration that cultivates understanding, healing and purpose in the lives of men who have suffered from homelessness, addiction and other life traumas. The one-year, Christ-centered residential program integrates addiction recovery, life skills training, vocational development and spiritual growth in a safe, highly relational environment. The ministry team of staff and volunteers serves to model Christ-like living to support the up to 36 participants in achieving lasting transformation.

THE POSITION

The Men's Community Life Lead contributes to Portland Rescue Mission’s ministry outcomes by overseeing and contributing to the team that provides coverage in the evenings and weekends, maintaining a Christ-centered ministry environment, supporting program participants life skills development, recovery progress and discipleship growth.

THE ESSENTIALS

  • Supervise, equip and mobilize the Community Life team to provide 24/7 coverage (including appropriate overnight coverage) so that program participants experience a consistently safe, purposeful, engaging and supportive environment.
  • Provide The Harbor (TH) program participants with a consistent programmatic care and experience in the evenings and weekends by maintaining program purposes, guidelines, and tone resulting in continued growth of all participants
  • Support TH program participants growth in spiritual formation, relationships and addictions recovery through one-on-one conversations, compassionate care, consistent invitations to participate and use of applicable growth tools for accountability as needed
  • Assist Director of Men’s Recovery in three key areas: equipping and coordinating Harbor volunteers; overseeing dynamic group events that encourage spiritual growth and retention, including weekly Community Life meetings, graduations, and retreats; and
  • overseeing men during post-graduation phases of their program
  • Maintain program and facility operations to PRM standards through supporting a variety of activities such as Urinalysis (UA’s), Med Call, Facility Lock Up and walk-thru, evening meal, vocational duties, visitations, and attendance accountability
  • Collaborate with TH daytime Program Staff on participant behaviors through Evening Shift Report, effective database communication and consistent use of growth tools.
  • Train and support Community Life Staff Interns to effectively serve program participants while growing in their own ministry skills and abilities

BACKGROUND AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • A passionate relationship with Jesus Christ and a testimony of continued growth in faith
  • A calling to serve men impacted by homelessness and addiction
  • Agreement with Portland Rescue Mission’s Statement of Faith and Code of Ethics
  • A personal ethos and work ethic that reflects Portland Rescue Mission’s ministry culture – Highly Relational, Christ-Centered, Joyful Servant
  • Experience working in teams and supervising people is preferred
  • General awareness and knowledge of chemical dependency, addiction recovery and discipleship
  • Good understanding and experience in relational development, facility operations and community building
  • Proficient in documentation, organization, scheduling and activity planning
  • Experience in Mac and Microsoft Windows software
  • Ability to lift at least 50 lbs. unassisted


MISSION AND DISTINCTIVES

OUR MISSION

We exist to transform the lives of people experiencing homelessness or addiction by sharing the word of God and demonstrating the love of Christ

OUR UNIQUE APPROACH

From the first sandwich that was shared in 1949, to today's fully integrated emergency, recovery, and training services, Portland Rescue Mission is a highly relational ministry. The Mission builds supportive and caring communities, meets people at their point of need, equips them, and provides a path forward. In-depth partnership with churches and volunteers, multiple tiers of services and a focus on growing Christian disciples is fundamental to Portland Rescue Mission’s success.

OUR SUCCESS

New Life Ministries consistently sees an 80+% success rate of men and women who graduate the one-year comprehensive, New Life program.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
About the role

RADICL is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join our platform team. You'll design and build API integrations and highly scalable data processing pipelines that power our security data ingestion, handling both structured and unstructured data from diverse security tools and log sources. You'll be integrating log collectors and forwarders (Fluentd, Fluent Bit, Vector, Logstash, Elastic Beats) and working with data from EDR platforms, cloud providers, compliance tools, and other security data sources. Your work will directly impact how quickly and accurately we onboard new data sources and how effectively our AI-powered virtual SOC delivers threat detection and compliance capabilities. You will also be a key part of implementing our agentic automation for parsing and mapping dynamic data sources.


If the above excites you, RADICL Defense is seeking high performing, motivated individuals to join our mission. As an early member, you will work closely alongside an experienced founding team and realize the life-changing experience of building a company. You will work with the latest technologies in software, cybersecurity, and cloud and will have a significant impact on the formation of our platform and offering.

About You
You enjoy fast-paced environments, bring a positive attitude, and excel at getting things done. You enjoy being part of a high performing team and are also able to self-direct and self-start. You consider yourself to be top tier talent and are eager to help others raise their game. You enjoy working with customers, are an excellent communicator, and able to engage and interact with people of various backgrounds and skill levels. You want your work to have meaning, to be important. You want to be part of creating something great.

As a RADICL Senior Software Engineer, you will:

  • Cloud-native, distributed systems — reliability, performance, and security in AWS, GCP, or Azure; microservices; Docker and Kubernetes; CI/CD (e.g. GitHub Actions).
  • Architecture and quality — help shape how systems connect; code review, testing, documentation, and clear tradeoffs in multi-tenant, mission-critical environments.
  • Design and build API integrations for ingesting security data from third-party tools (EDR, cloud providers, compliance platforms, and other security data sources)
  • Develop log parsing and data mapping pipelines to normalize structured and unstructured log formats into our unified schema
  • Integrate with log collectors and forwarders (e.g., Fluentd, Fluent Bit, Vector, Logstash, Elastic Beats)
  • Create and maintain data mappings between source schemas and our internal data model
  • Optimize ingestion performance and ensure data quality, completeness, and timeliness
  • Document integration specifications and support internal and external stakeholders with technical guidance
  • Contribute to the design of our emerging agentic parsing pipeline (LLM-powered extraction for complex formats)

Your skillset/experience should include:

  • Data integration fundamentals: ETL design, RESTful API development, data mapping, and schema design
  • Log parsing and normalization: Experience with regex, Grok-style patterns, or similar; comfort with both structured (JSON, CEF, syslog, CSV) and unstructured log formats
  • Log collection/forwarding tools: Experience with one or more of Fluentd, Fluent Bit, Vector, Logstash, Elastic Beats (Filebeat, Winlogbeat), OpenTelemetry Collector, rsyslog, or syslog-ng
  • Security data platforms: Familiarity with security data ingestion patterns; experience with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Graylog, Sumo Logic, Google Chronicle, IBM QRadar, or similar platforms is valuable
  • Programming: Strong proficiency in Go, Kotlin, and/or TypeScript
  • Data modeling: Ability to design schemas for security/observability data; familiarity with Elasticsearch and Elastic Common Schema or similar is a plus
  • Cloud and infrastructure: Experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP; familiarity with Kafka or streaming pipelines is a plus
  • Security domain awareness: Understanding of SIEM concepts, security tooling (EDR, firewalls, cloud logs), and compliance data (CMMC, NIST) is highly valued
  • Agentic/AI pipelines: Interest or experience with LLM-based data extraction (nice-to-have)
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, data engineering, or related field—or equivalent professional experience (typically 3–6+ years)

About the Workplace
At RADICL, we prioritize our culture and believe the strongest teams are built through daily, side-by-side collaboration and experiential sharing. We also value individual freedom and flexibility. For this reason, we have a hybrid work model. As a team, we are in office M/W/Th with work-from-home on Tuesdays and Fridays. For remote positions, periodic travel to Boulder will be expected to participate in company events and meaningful side-by-side collaboration opportunities.

RADICL offices are in downtown Boulder, Colorado with easy-to-access employee parking provided by the company. We offer comprehensive, competitive benefits including health, dental, and vision as well as 401K and a responsible PTO plan.


We encourage motivated, talented, mission-oriented, and fun people to apply. Let’s do this!

Develop commercial glazing shop drawings, fabrication drawings, elevations, plans, sections, details, and production documentation.

Coordinate with Project Managers and Operations on scope, system selections, schedules, material releases, fabrication priorities, and installation sequencing.
Translate approved information into fabrication packages that clearly communicate what the shop must cut, machine, assemble, label, and package.
Maintain disciplined document/revision control and identify conflicts, missing information, and constructability concerns before release.

CNC PROGRAMMING & FABRICATION SUPPORT

Develop CNC programs for architectural aluminum, including cuts, holes, slots, notches, routes, weeps, fastener locations, and hardware preparation.
Verify profile orientation, dimensions, offsets, tooling, machining locations, and tolerances before release.
Generate and coordinate cut lists, fabrication drawings, labels, and production information by project and installation sequence.
Troubleshoot programming/fabrication issues with shop personnel and support first-piece verification for new or complex work.
Maintain organized CNC program libraries, standardized machining templates, and repeatable fabrication processes.

GLAZING SYSTEM KNOWLEDGE

Apply working knowledge of storefront, curtain wall, window wall, interior framing, entrances, aluminum doors/frames, sill flashing, pressure plates/covers, glazing pockets/adapters, gaskets, hardware preparation, brake metal, and related accessories.
Interpret manufacturer catalogs, fabrication manuals, engineering information, system limitations, and project-specific requirements.

PROJECT & BIM COORDINATION

Coordinate glazing with architectural, structural, adjacent construction, field conditions, and approved system requirements.
Work with Project Managers to resolve dimensional discrepancies, design conflicts, incomplete information, and fabrication questions.
BIM modeling and coordination experience is a plus, particularly using 3D building models to coordinate glazing systems, identify clashes, and support shop drawing/fabrication development.
Use model information, when available, to improve constructability, dimensional accuracy, and communication between project and production teams.

Salary range: $59,500 – $80,000 annual salary plus non-guaranteed annualized bonus program.

FABRICATION RELEASE & QUALITY CONTROL

Confirm current approved drawings, dimensions, field measurements, profiles, glass requirements, door/hardware information, and fabrication details before release.
Perform self-checks of critical dimensions, calculations, machining logic, and CNC programs before issuing work to production.
Prevent obsolete drawings or programs from reaching the shop through strong revision control and file management.
Investigate drafting/programming errors, determine root causes, and update standards or processes to prevent recurrence.
Operate with the expectation that fabrication issues should be identified digitally before aluminum is cut.

MATERIAL OPTIMIZATION & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Support material optimization, efficient cut planning, fabrication batching, and production sequencing.
Develop reusable details, CNC templates, system libraries, and standardized processes for repetitive work.
Reduce unnecessary machine setups, manual fabrication, material waste, and production rework.
Seek feedback from shop and field personnel and apply lessons learned to improve detailing and programming.

QUALIFICATIONS

3+ years of commercial glass and glazing drafting/detailing experience preferred; glazing fabrication experience is highly desirable.
Strong knowledge of commercial storefront, curtain wall, entrances, doors, and architectural aluminum systems.
Ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, specifications, shop drawings, manufacturer information, and fabrication requirements.
Proficiency with AutoCAD or comparable CAD software; strong mathematical, dimensional, and problem-solving skills.
Experience programming CNC equipment used for architectural aluminum fabrication preferred.
Strong attention to detail, organization, communication, and ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.

PREFERRED TECHNICAL EXPERIENCE

AutoCAD, Revit, Bluebeam Revu, and related digital detailing tools.
BIM modeling and coordination experience, including use of 3D models to support glazing coordination, shop drawings, and fabrication.
CNC programming software, manufacturer-specific fabrication software, cut-list optimization, ERP/production systems, and digital fabrication workflows.
Experience with architectural aluminum CNC equipment such as Emmegi, FOM, Elumatec, or similar equipment is highly desirable.

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

Shop drawing accuracy and on-time completion; on-time fabrication releases; CNC programming accuracy and first-piece success.
Fabrication error/rework rate, material waste, revision accuracy, fabrication-package completeness, and responsiveness to shop/field questions.
Development of standardized details/programs, reduction in manual fabrication, and support of overall project and production schedules.

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Accuracy First
Correct before production.

Think Like a Fabricator
Clear, practical, buildable information.

Plan Ahead
Stay ahead of release schedules.

Communicate Early
Surface conflicts before impact.

Own the Release
Take responsibility for completeness.

Standardize & Improve
Build repeatable processes.

Create a seamless technical connection between design, project management, fabrication, and field
POSITION OBJECTIVE installation by delivering accurate, efficient, fabrication-ready drawings and CNC programs that allow quality glazing systems to be produced correctly the first time and on schedule.

title: Track and Field- Field Events Coach
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
Harlem Children’s Zone (HCZ)—a world-renowned education and poverty-fighting organization based in New York—seeks an enthusiastic, dedicated, and mission-aligned Track & Field Field Events Coach.

The Track & Field Field Events Coach will bring a strong commitment to Harlem Children’s Zone’s mission of breaking the cycle of intergenerational poverty through comprehensive, on-the-ground programming that creates opportunities for children and families to thrive in school, work, and life.

We are seeking an experienced Track & Field Field Events Coach to lead and develop scholar-athletes competing in field events across our elementary, middle, and high school programs. The Field Events Coach will be responsible for providing high-quality instruction, developing scholar-athletes’ technical, physical, tactical, and mental skills, preparing athletes for competition, and strengthening the overall Track & Field program.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a passion for HCZ’s mission, an understanding of and respect for the Harlem community, and experience working with youth in a school-based or community-based setting. The successful candidate will use athletics as a platform to promote academic achievement, leadership, accountability, teamwork, discipline, resilience, and personal growth.

For more information, check out Want to Work at Harlem Children's Zone? Here's 7 Things You Need to Know.

Requirements

• High school diploma or GED required, bachelor’s degree preferred.

• At least three years of experience coaching track and field field events, preferably at the middle school, high school, collegiate, club, or elite competitive level.

• Demonstrated experience developing and coaching athletes in one or more field-event disciplines, including jumps, throws, or other applicable field events.

• Strong knowledge of track and field rules, regulations, event-specific techniques, training methodologies, competition strategy, and athlete development.

• Demonstrated knowledge of appropriate training progressions for field events, including strength, power, speed, mobility, coordination, technique, and event-specific conditioning.

• Demonstrated ability to design and implement progressive training programs appropriate for youth and adolescent athletes.

• Experience coaching and supporting youth and adolescent populations.

• Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, mentor, and retain scholar-athletes.

• Commitment to the mission, values, and programs of Harlem Children’s Zone.

• Strong leadership, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, and meet established deadlines.

• A positive, enthusiastic, collaborative, flexible, and solutions-oriented mindset.

• Ability to work effectively with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, HCZ colleagues, community organizations, and external partners.

• CPR and First Aid certification, or the ability to obtain certification within the required timeframe.

• Ability to travel to away meets, invitationals, tournaments, championships, and other athletic events.

• Ability to work evenings, weekends, and extended hours as required by the athletic schedule.

Who You Are

The Track & Field Field Events Coach is responsible for the development and performance of scholar-athletes competing in field events while contributing to the overall success and culture of the HCZ Track & Field program.

The Field Events Coach will design and implement age-appropriate training plans, lead practices, prepare athletes for competition, evaluate performance, and provide individualized coaching and feedback. The coach will work closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leadership, and other coaching staff to ensure consistency in training, expectations, athlete development, and program operations.

The successful candidate understands that coaching extends beyond athletic performance. They will serve as a mentor and role model who promotes academic accountability, positive behavior, leadership, teamwork, discipline, resilience, and long-term scholar development.

The Field Events Coach must understand the importance of developing technical skills, strength, power, coordination, mobility, and event-specific abilities progressively and safely. They should be able to balance competitive expectations with appropriate training loads, recovery, injury prevention, and the individual needs of developing athletes.

What You’ll Do

Field Events Program Leadership and Training

• In collaboration with the Head Track & Field Coach and Athletic Leadership, develop and implement a comprehensive field-events development program for elementary, middle, and high school scholar-athletes.

• Design and implement age-appropriate, progressive training plans that develop technical proficiency, strength, power, speed, mobility, coordination, balance, body control, and overall athletic performance.

• Lead daily practices and field-event-specific training sessions in accordance with the overall Track & Field program schedule.

• Develop individualized training plans based on athlete ability, experience, event specialization, competition schedule, and developmental needs.

• Prepare scholar-athletes for field events, including long jump, triple jump, high jump, shot put, discus, javelin, and other applicable events within the program.

• Teach proper event-specific mechanics, body positioning, approach patterns, takeoff and landing techniques, throwing mechanics, implement control, and competition strategy.

• Develop appropriate drills and technical progressions to improve event-specific performance.

• Incorporate appropriate strength, power, speed, mobility, flexibility, coordination, conditioning, and injury-prevention strategies into field-event training.

• Collaborate with Strength & Conditioning staff, Athletic Trainers, medical personnel, and other coaches when appropriate to support athlete health and performance.

• Evaluate athlete performance through practices, competitions, technical assessments, video analysis, testing, and other appropriate measures.

• Use performance data to establish goals and adjust training plans.

• Identify and develop scholar-athletes with potential to compete at higher levels of competition.

Competition and Meet Preparation

• Prepare scholar-athletes for league meets, invitationals, championships, tournaments, and other sanctioned athletic events.

• Develop individualized competition plans based on event, athlete strengths, competition level, and meet conditions.

• Prepare athletes to effectively execute event-specific techniques, approaches, attempts, warm-ups, competition routines, and strategic adjustments.

• Attend and actively coach assigned competitions and provide real-time instruction, support, and feedback.

• Maintain accurate records of athlete marks, personal records, placements, qualifying standards, and other relevant performance data.

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with meet entries, athlete selection, event assignments, competition logistics, and scheduling.

• Help scholar-athletes understand competition rules, attempt procedures, event etiquette, equipment requirements, and appropriate conduct.

• Promote sportsmanship, professionalism, accountability, and appropriate conduct before, during, and after competitions.

Scholar-Athlete Development and Accountability

• Recruit, evaluate, develop, and retain scholar-athletes interested in field events.

• Provide individualized instruction and feedback to support each scholar-athlete’s athletic development.

• Create a positive, inclusive, disciplined, and high-performing training environment.

• Promote sportsmanship, teamwork, leadership, resilience, accountability, discipline, and respect.

• Establish and communicate clear expectations regarding attendance, participation, behavior, academic performance, training standards, and team responsibilities.

• Hold scholar-athletes accountable for meeting HCZ academic, school attendance, and after-school programming standards.

• Collaborate with school staff, CCLR, Zone site staff, families, and other HCZ colleagues to identify and support scholars experiencing academic, attendance, behavioral, or engagement challenges.

• Reinforce the expectation that academic responsibilities and required school or after-school programming take priority over athletic participation.

• Teach scholar-athletes the importance of goal setting, time management, discipline, consistency, preparation, recovery, and responsible decision-making.

• Recognize and celebrate academic achievement, leadership, positive behavior, personal growth, and athletic accomplishments.

Athlete Health, Safety, and Wellness

• Prioritize the health and safety of all scholar-athletes during practices and competitions.

• Implement appropriate warm-up, cool-down, mobility, recovery, hydration, and environmental safety practices.

• Ensure that field-event training areas and equipment are properly inspected and used in accordance with established safety procedures.

• Provide appropriate instruction and supervision when using throwing implements, jumping equipment, pits, runways, standards, landing areas, and other field-event equipment.

• Monitor athletes for signs of excessive fatigue, overtraining, injury, dehydration, heat-related illness, or other health concerns.

• Follow all HCZ, school, league, and athletic safety policies and procedures.

• Immediately report injuries, incidents, behavioral concerns, and other relevant matters through established protocols.

• Collaborate with Athletic Trainers, school nurses, Strength & Conditioning staff, and other appropriate professionals regarding scholar-athlete health and readiness.

• Promote healthy training habits and educate scholar-athletes on the importance of recovery, nutrition, hydration, sleep, and injury prevention.

Program Operations

• Support the Head Track & Field Coach with the day-to-day operation of the Track & Field program.

• Maintain accurate records related to athlete participation, attendance, performance, eligibility, competition results, and program outcomes.

• Support the management and maintenance of Track & Field equipment, uniforms, implements, jumping equipment, throwing equipment, supplies, and other program resources.

• Ensure equipment is properly maintained, safely stored, inventoried, and returned following practices and competitions.

• Assist with scheduling practices, competitions, transportation, facilities, and other program logistics.

• Support the planning and execution of Track & Field events, clinics, showcases, camps, community events, and other program activities.

• Maintain a clean, organized, safe, and professional training environment.

• Provide timely updates regarding program needs, athlete concerns, equipment, facilities, competitions, and other operational matters.

Collaboration and Organizational Alignment

• Collaborate closely with the Head Track & Field Coach, Assistant Athletic Director, Director of Athletics, school leaders, and other coaches to ensure program alignment.

• Support the implementation of HCZ policies, procedures, organizational initiatives, and strategic priorities.

• Participate in required meetings, professional development sessions, trainings, family engagement activities, and organizational events.

• Maintain consistent and professional communication with scholars, families, coaches, school leaders, and external partners.

• Collaborate with CCLR to integrate college, career, leadership, and readiness opportunities into the scholar-athlete experience.

• Collaborate with Wealth Builds to support financial literacy, long-term planning, and economic empowerment opportunities for scholar-athletes and families.

• Build relationships with local Track & Field organizations, clubs, colleges, athletic programs, leagues, governing bodies, and community partners to expand opportunities for scholar-athletes.

• Support a strong, inclusive, collaborative, and mission-aligned Track & Field culture across HCZ.

Compliance and Data-Informed Decision-Making

• Ensure all coaching activities comply with HCZ policies, school requirements, league regulations, and applicable athletic governing-body standards.

• Maintain accurate records of scholar participation, attendance, academic eligibility, performance, competition results, and development.

• Use performance data to inform training plans, event assignments, athlete development, competition preparation, and program improvements.

• Monitor scholar-athletes’ academic eligibility and readiness for collegiate athletic opportunities.

• Research and identify appropriate field-event competitions, invitationals, showcases, camps, clinics, and collegiate exposure opportunities.

• Support scholar-athletes who demonstrate the potential and interest to pursue collegiate athletics.

• Ensure scholar participation in external competitions and opportunities aligns with applicable school, league, organizational, and NCAA requirements.

Schedule

The Track & Field Field Events Coach must be available to work:

Fall/Spring

  • Monday–Friday, 1:00 p.m.–8:00 p.m.
  • Saturday, 10:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m. is required depending on the sport & game schedule.

Summer

  • 1:00 PM - 7:00 PM

The position may also require attendance at administrative meetings, professional development sessions, athletic events, competitions, invitationals, championships, cross country meets, family engagement activities, and other organizational responsibilities outside of the standard work schedule.

Benefits

As a member of the Harlem Children's Zone team, you will join a supportive and inclusive community dedicated to helping children, families — and our staff — thrive.

Please take a look at our Part-Time benefits below.

Our exceptional Part-Time benefits include:

  • Career Advancement
  • Paid sick leave
  • Employee referral bonus
  • Physical wellness discounts
  • Commuter benefits
  • Additional Benefits (Discounts on flights, hotels, theme parks, concert tickets, and more.)

The salary range for this position is $25-$30 per hour. To be considered, interested applicants should apply directly through the posting. No telephone inquiries or recruiters, please. Replies will only be sent to qualified applicants. Harlem Children's Zone and Promise Academy Charter Schools does not provide work visas for candidates who require employer sponsorship to ensure work authorization in the United States. Harlem Children’s Zone is an EOE.

title: Wax - Inject Mold Mach Operator 2nd shift
description:
Job Summary
We’re looking for a Wax Injection Mold Machine Operator to operate wax injection molding equipment used to produce precision wax patterns, gating, sprues, and related components for aerospace manufacturing. This role supports production by setting up and operating molding equipment, inspecting finished parts, and ensuring quality, safety, and process standards are met.

Work That Matters
At Chromalloy, your work directly supports aviation safety and reliability. Our teams repair and manufacture critical aerospace components used across the global aviation industry. What you do here has real-world impact—every day.

Shift: 2nd shift, Monday-Friday 1:30p-9:30p
Shift Differential: $2.00
Training: New hires are required to attend New Hire Orientation (Monday, 9:00 a.m.-1:00 p.m.) and first-week training (Tuesday-Friday, 7:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.). Additional training outside the assigned shift schedule may be required based on business needs or availability. Upon successful completion of training, employees will transition to their assigned shift.

What You’ll Be Doing

Set up and operate wax injection molding machines following engineering practices and work instructions.
Prepare and install dies, cores, and tooling for production runs.
Load materials and monitor machine settings, including temperature, pressure, and cycle parameters.
Produce wax patterns, sprues, gating, and related components to quality standards.
Inspect finished parts for defects and perform minor cleaning or deflashing as needed.
Obtain and verify x-ray results for cored patterns when required.
Complete production paperwork and sign off on routers.
Perform daily TPM checks and maintain equipment and work areas.
Transfer completed parts to the next operation and communicate quality concerns or production issues.
Follow all safety, quality, and standard work requirements.

What We’re Looking For

High school diploma, GED, or equivalent experience.
3+ months of manufacturing, machine operation, production, or related experience preferred.
Ability to clearly communicate in English, including speaking, reading, writing, and understanding work instructions.
Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to safely operate machinery and tooling.
Knowledge of production processes and quality standards.
Ability to monitor machine performance and recognize process issues.
Strong attention to detail and ability to perform visual inspections.
Good hand dexterity and ability to perform repetitive, precision tasks.
Ability to work safely, follow procedures, and work effectively in a team environment.
Commitment to quality, safety, and continuous improvement.

Nice to Have

Injection molding experience.
Experience operating manufacturing equipment in a production environment.
Experience working with precision components, tooling, or inspection processes.
Experience reading engineering practices or manufacturing instructions.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

Manufacturing environment with moving machinery, moderate noise, and occasional exposure to fumes or airborne particles.
Regular standing, walking, bending, and use of hands for machine operation and inspection activities.
Ability to lift, push, pull, and move up to 25 lbs regularly and up to 50 lbs occasionally.
Close vision, color recognition, depth perception, and focus adjustment required for inspection and defect identification.
Required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including hearing protection, safety glasses, hand protection, and safety-toed shoes.

description:

Support Regional Portfolio Managers with accurate portfolio information and administrative reporting.
Collaborate with site teams and other internal departments to ensure timely and accurate information flow.

Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work accurately in a process-driven environment.

Experience with Yardi Voyager or a comparable property management platform is an asset.
Experience with accounts receivable, collections, or resident account administration is an asset.
Familiarity with the Alberta Residential Tenancies Act and RTDRS process is an asset.

Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across teams.

Our Culture & Benefits
At Strategic Group, we’re committed to helping you build a career you’re excited about. If you’re passionate about working with a dynamic, motivated team in a fast-paced environment, please submit your resume and cover letter today, and join us in making an impact.

title: Development Technician II
description:
Position Summary
Reporting to the Supervisor of Development Support Services, the Development Technician II is an important role in delivering the County’s integrated development approvals service, contributing to the streamlined processing of Planning and Building applications while supporting customers with clear advice. The role requires excellent customer service skills with an emphasis on providing an efficient and solution-based approach when processing a high volume of development-related applications and inquiries.
The Development Technician II will be supported in acquiring a broad knowledge of planning, development permit and building permit application processes to help customers navigate between these separate approval steps. A key focus of the role will be to process simple building permit applications in accordance with the Alberta Safety Codes Act and other applicable legislation, acting as the file manager from application intake to permit issuance.
The Development Technician II is required to undertake regular research of legislative, policy and bylaw requirements in processing permit applications and undertaking other tasks such as Real Property Report reviews, Land Use Bylaw reviews, and exempt development approvals Proficiency in the use of technology is required in administering the County’s increasingly digital service.
Core Accountabilities
Technician Duties

Process a high volume of less complex residential building permit applications, ensuring compliance with the Alberta Safety Codes Act and all other applicable legislation.
Efficiently review all other types of applications, plans, permit documents, and other pertinent information to verify accuracy and completeness of planning, development, building, plumbing, gas, electrical, and private sewage permit applications to current applicable codes and standards, including the National Building Code -Alberta Edition
Adopt an innovative and creative approach to customer service by suggesting process improvements and finding solutions for customers.
Take a practical approach in ensuring planning, development and building applications meet the requirements of permit regulations, the Safety Codes Act, the Land Use Bylaw, and statutory plans.
Support customers in navigating between planning, development permit, and safety code approvals by case managing development proposals and offering clear advice.
Process and issue exempt development approvals, minor development permits, minor building, plumbing, gas, electrical, and private sewage permits, when authorized, and meet with applicants as necessary.
Review and accept documentation related to ongoing building permit files when authorized.
Participate in pre-application meetings with developers/applicants to discuss proposed applications, as required.
Support the department’s digital transformation towards e-permitting and automated solutions by guiding the customer through use of these systems and effectively integrating technology within Technician tasks.
Prepare a variety of notices and correspondence required by the Safety Codes Quality Management Plan (QMP).
Prepare monthly statistical reports relating to various development related applications, verify outlying data and submissions.
Issue Certificates of Compliance and Confirmations of Land Use upon ensuring that all details have been thoroughly reviewed and are accurate.
Administration and file management of issued permits, ensuring that projects are monitored, and appropriate timelines are adhered to, including investigating violations to County regulations and conditions of approval.
Undertake site visits and complete related inspection reports for the purposes of development applications.
Provide appropriate information to the public in-person, by phone, and in writing, noting applicable processes and regulations. Provide assistance to the various processes, including research of historical information, and other relevant assignments.
Tend to all customer concerns and questions with respect and professionalism.
Perform other administrative duties and special projects as assigned.
Write Orders under the Safety Codes Act.
Review Alternative Solution Proposals for conformance to legislation.

General

This position requires excellent organizational and time management skills.
Perform routine office tasks including data entry, file management, copying, etc.
Assist in the preparation of statistical or internal department reports, correspondence, planning maps, and presentation materials.
Supply internal assistance/discussions with other departments regarding Land Use Bylaw issues.
Provide ongoing dialogue with applicants to ensure conditions are met prior to issuing permits.
Work in accordance with the requirements established by the RVC Health and Safety Program and the Alberta OHS Act, Regulation and Code.
Take reasonable care to protect their health and safety and other persons at or in the vicinity of the worksite while they are working.
Provide support to the section and department as required.
Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.

Position Requirements
Safety Codes Officer certification - Building residential and Building part 9 – Safety Codes Council
Completion of one of the following combinations of education and experience:

A Journeyman carpenter, plumber, electrician, sheet metal worker or bricklayer certification recognized in Alberta and 3 years of relevant experience in the building construction industry after receiving that journeyman certification, OR
A 2 year technology diploma in a related field and 3 years of relevant experience in the building construction industry after receiving that diploma, OR
An Engineering or Architecture degree and 3 years of relevant experience in the building construction industry, at least 1 of which must be completed after obtaining that degree.

Familiarity with Municipal Government Act and Safety Codes Acts sections and requirements relevant to the position will be considered an asset
Ability to demonstrate excellent organizational, prioritizing, time management skills and problem-solving skills.
Ability for attention to detail, legibility, accuracy, and timeliness of activities.
Proficient in reading construction blueprints and related construction documents.
Knowledge of construction plans, construction terminology, construction practices
Be fully competent in reviewing plans and applications for completeness and compliance with Land Use Bylaw, and related Statutory Plans.
Familiar with legal land descriptions.
Possess a pleasant personality with an ability to maintain harmonious relations with employees and external customers.
Highly developed communication skills, with excellent telephone manners.
Show initiative to assist customers to meet their needs.
Ability to develop a working knowledge of the Development Support Services department’s functions.
Proficient in MS Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, and Power Point)
This position is eligible for remote work on an ad hoc basis.

description:
It’s an exciting time to be at Hanscom Federal Credit Union!

As a member of our Residential Lending Department, you will join a dynamic team of purpose-driven individuals committed to delivering exceptional service to our members.

Who we are – Hanscom Federal Credit Union

  • Members-first – our members are our top priority. We make business decisions with our members at the top of mind.
  • Integrity – we’re honest and committed to doing what’s best for our members and our company. What is right isn’t the same as what is easy.

  • Innovation – we identify new ideas for processes or products that will lead to positive changes and take the initiative to implement the changes.
  • Empathy – we understand that communication starts by listening, understanding diverse perspectives, and caring about others’ sustained success.

What we offer

$24.65/hr to $30.82/hr

Compensation for this position will be determined based on the candidate's experience, skills, and qualifications. Final pay may vary depending on factors such as prior experience, expertise, and specific requirements of the role. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and will discuss the final pay rate with candidates should an offer be made.

  • A full-time, permanent position that will reward you through an annual bonus program
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA, 401(k), Student Loan Paydown, and paid Sick and Vacation time benefits.
  • A flexible hybrid work schedule environment.
  • We are committed to fostering career growth and development – when you join our organization it’s not just a job.
  • We look to develop your skills aligned to our business needs and help you progress in your career.

Who you are – Senior Residential Loan Processor/Closer

You are a dynamic, detail oriented, intuitive person with the ability to develop relationships, build rapport and become a trusted team member. You are able to provide everyone you assist or support with a high level of service, have strong organization and multi-tasking skills, and are searching for a rewarding career where you are valued and respected.

What you'll do

  • Maintain the integrity of the loan data from time of application to closing.
  • Review new loan package for completeness of borrower information, and review and highlights potential issues on credit report such as undisclosed HELOC/2nd mortgage, fraud detection, red flag alerts, report comments, OFAC, public records, and date of 1st mortgage. Review and investigate red flags and fraud alerts from credit bureau or/or DU, and document findings.
  • Obtain pertinent documentation as directed by the Residential Loan Processing Team Lead or Underwriter. Ensure all documentation is uploaded to Image Flow paperless system within MortgageBot.
  • Upon receipt of loan file from loan officer, review application data, update all fees and send Initial Disclosure package to borrowers according to regulatory deadlines. Collect appropriate fees from borrower for application deposit. Prepare Rate Lock and Change of Circumstance disclosures when needed. Throughout the process, keep borrowers informed regarding the status of the loan, both by phone and email.
  • Respond in a timely manner to borrowers’ and third-party agents’ (i.e. closing agents, appraisers, realtors etc.) inquiries during the mortgage process.
  • Utilize MortgageBot reports to manage their pipeline, track the timely return of all required documentation (appraisals, titles, verifications, approval conditions, etc.). Keep up to date on financing date and closing date on purchases.
  • Analyze all documents to ensure loan packages are complete and accurate. Reviews documents for possible identity fraud, etc. Forward the file to underwriting for approval.
  • Once approval is issued, responsible for tracking and collection of documentation to ensure conditions are satisfied. Once complete, generate Clear to Close form, update fees and submit to underwriting for final approval.
  • Assist Residential Loan Processing Team Lead in scheduling of mortgage and home equity closings.
  • Prepare mortgage and home equity closing documents, including verifying all conditions are met, reviewing all documents for completeness and accuracy, ensuring timely delivery and accuracy of the preliminary Closing Disclosure, and issuing the closing package and funds in a timely manner.
  • Provide backup on the quality review on post-closing files to confirm all notes, mortgages and other required documentation have been completed correctly, and figures are accurate.
  • Act as mentor to the Residential Loan Processor / Closers and other team members within HFCU. Identifies training needs for Residential Processing Team Lead when necessary.
  • Represent the credit union in a professional manner; provide quality service to members and internal customers. Cross-sell CU products and services where applicable.
  • Perform other related duties as required.

Knowledge/Skills/Experience Required:

  • 3 – 5 years mortgage servicing and/or closing experience.
  • A high school degree or equivalent
  • Must have good organizational, analytical and customer service skills.
  • Mortgage computer skills.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
Is able to bend, sit, and stand in order to perform primarily sedentary work with limited physical exertion and occasional lifting of up to 10 lbs. Must be capable of climbing / descending stairs in an emergency situation. Must be able to operate routine office equipment including computer terminals and keyboards, telephones, copiers, facsimiles, and calculators. Must be able to routinely perform work on computer for an average of 6-8 hours per day, when necessary. Must be able to work extended hours or travel off site whenever required or requested by management. Must be capable of regular, reliable and timely attendance.

WORKING CONDITIONS
Must be able to routinely perform work indoors in climate-controlled shared work area with minimal noise.

MENTAL AND/OR EMOTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
Must be able to perform job functions independently or with limited supervision and work effectively either on own or as part of a team. Must be able to read and carry out various written instructions and follow oral instructions. Must be able to complete basic mathematical calculations, spell accurately, and understand computer basics. Must be able to speak clearly and deliver information in a logical and understandable sequence. Must be capable of dealing calmly and professionally with numerous different personalities from diverse cultures at various levels within and outside of the organization and demonstrate highest levels of customer service and discretion when dealing with the public. Must be able to perform responsibilities with composure under the stress of deadlines / requirements for extreme accuracy and quality and/or fast pace. Must be able to effectively handle multiple, simultaneous, and changing priorities. Must be capable of exercising highest level of discretion on both internal and external confidential matters.

** Must be authorized to work in the US **

title: Senior Power Electronics Researcher
description:
Priority may be given to the following designated employment equity groups: women, Indigenous Peoples* (First Nations, Inuit and Métis), persons with disabilities and racialized persons*.

* The Employment Equity Act, which is under review, uses the terminology Aboriginal peoples and visible minorities.

Candidates are asked to self-declare when applying to this hiring process.

City: Hamilton

Organizational Unit: Automotive and Surface Transportation

Classification: RO

Tenure: Term

Duration: Two (2) years

Language Requirements: English

Work arrangements: Due to the nature of the work and operational requirements, this position will require full-time physical presence at the NRC work location identified.

Note: This is a two (2) year term position with possibility of extension or conversion to indeterminate.

The role

We are looking for a Senior Power Electronics Researcher to support our e-Auto Challenge Program hosted by the Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.


The e Auto Challenge Program aims to strengthen the competitiveness of Canadian auto industry on the world stage by accelerating and de-risking novel Canadian Zero Emissions Vehicle (ZEV) solutions innovation. Specifically, this initiative focuses on advancing, integrating and deploying advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications to enable higher power density, more efficiency, reliable and lower cost traction drives, battery systems, and charging infrastructures.


The Senior Power Electronics Researcher is a technical leader who will play a key role in shaping and delivering the Power Electronics theme for the e-Auto Challenge program, bridging advanced research with product ready solutions in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across industry, academia and government to achieve technical excellence and commercial success.


This position calls for a visionary researcher with demonstrated expertise in automotive power electronics development, system integration and validation for industrial applications.


The activities in support of program area objectives may include:

  • Research and Development: Conduct cutting-edge research in advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications related to zero-emission vehicles (ZEV).
  • Experimental Design and Execution: Design and execute novel experiments to assess feasibility of cyber-physical systems, introduce or improve instrumentation and data collection, and validate applications for machine learning.
  • Technology Assessment: Evaluate emerging technologies, instrumentation devices and other tools related to power electronics for electric vehicles applications.
  • Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support interdisciplinary research projects.
  • Documentation and Reporting: Prepare technical reports, presentations, and publications for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Intellectual Property (IP): Contribute to the development and protection of IP through invention disclosures, patent applications, and technology transfer activities.
  • Continuous Learning: Stay current to trends in metal additive manufacturing through conferences and professional development activities.
  • Client Engagement: Support the business development function as a scientific discipline leader. Assist in identifying client requirements and prepare technical scope of project proposals.

Screening criteria

Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:

Education

Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a field relevant to the position.

A Master’s Degree in Engineering combined with experience in research or technology development relevant to the position may also be considered.

For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency

Experience

  • Extensive** and recent*** experience in the design, architecture and implementation of high power, high efficiency inverter, converter or controller topologies using Silicon carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) technologies.
  • Significant* experience in systems-level electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces optimization to meet performance, cost, and manufacturability targets.
  • Significant* experience in switching behavior, losses, and electromagnetic interference mitigation strategies for high frequency operation.
  • Significant* experience in developing compact, thermally robust packaging solutions for high-voltage automotive environments.
  • Significant* experience in design-for-reliability, design-for-manufacturing, and cost optimization practices.
  • Significant* experience leading and delivering research projects.

The following experience criterion would be considered an asset:

  • Experience working in an industrial research and development (R&D), product development and/or product deployment environment within the automotive, clean tech or defence sector.


* Significant experience is defined as experience of three (3) to six (6) years.
** Extensive experience is defined as experience of at least seven (7) years.
*** Recent experience is defined as experience acquired within the last two (2) years.

Condition of employment

Reliability Status

For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.

Language requirements

English

Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests

Assessment criteria

Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:

Technical competencies

  • Expert knowledge in the design of power converters and multi-level inverters for electric vehicle (EV) powertrain and charging systems.
  • Expert knowledge of SiC and GaN devices multi-physics application for high power-density design.
  • Solid knowledge of high-voltage design, insulation coordination, dielectric materials, creepage/clearance, and partial discharge phenomena.
  • Solid knowledge of electromagnetic compatibility, electromagnetic interference mitigation, and automotive electromagnetic compatibility standards compliance.
  • Solid knowledge of motor control integration, drivetrain efficiency, and system-level architecture of EV powertrains.
  • Knowledge of project management principles and practices.

Behavioural competencies

  • Research - Communication (Level 2)
  • Research - Creative thinking (Level 3)
  • Research - Partnering (Level 2)
  • Research - Results orientation (Level 3)
  • Research - Teamwork (Level 2)

Competency Profile(s)

For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research.

View all competency profiles

Compensation

The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the AsRO/AcRO level, which is an early-career level position with a salary range of $83,985 to $139,608.

NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).

NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.

Discover the possible

Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!

As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.

At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

Notes

title: Analyst, Analytics
description:
company Overview

Union Maritime Limited has experienced exceptional growth over the last five years, and as part of this expansion we are building our analytics capability in Lagos. The Analytics Analyst is an entry-level role within our dynamic and rapidly expanding Analytics team, based in our Lagos office. It offers an excellent opportunity for a motivated graduate or early-career professional to learn the business from the ground up and contribute directly to Union Maritime's continued growth.

Role summary

The Analytics Analyst will work closely with the wider team, supporting the analysis behind key commercial and strategic decisions. The role involves building and maintaining analytical and financial models, using AI tools to work faster and more accurately, and gaining hands-on exposure to the fast-paced world of international shipping and maritime investment.

Key responsibilities

Working under the guidance of senior team members, the Analytics Analyst will:

· Build and maintain financial and analytical models that support the evaluation of commercial opportunities, including:

· Vessel sales and purchases.

· Vessel financing and refinancing.

· Profit-sharing and commercial agreements.

· Investment in new maritime technologies.

· Use AI tools throughout the modelling process: to gather and structure data, draft and check formulas, test assumptions and scenarios, and summarise results, while validating every AI-generated output for accuracy.

· Collect, clean and analyse data from internal systems, market sources and industry databases.

· Help automate routine data preparation and reporting tasks, making use of AI-assisted and low-code tools.

· Prepare clear presentations and summaries of analysis for internal stakeholders and senior management.

· Maintain up-to-date records for market research and business intelligence, so the team has reliable data for decision-making.

· Support the review of term sheets and commercial documents by preparing the underlying analysis and summarising key terms.

· Assist with the coordination of commercial projects, tracking actions and deadlines to keep work on schedule.

· Work with colleagues across departments to gather information and keep projects aligned.

Requirements

Required qualifications

· Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics or a related field.

· 2+ years of relevant experience

· Strong MS Excel and MS PowerPoint skills, with the ability to analyse data and present it clearly.

· Practical experience of using AI tools (such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or similar) for analysis, modelling or research, and a strong interest in developing these skills further.

· An understanding of the limitations of AI, with the judgement to check, verify and take ownership of AI-assisted work.

· Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret data and draw practical insights.

· Meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.

· A curious, can-do attitude and an eagerness to learn quickly in a fast-paced environment.

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

· Ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.

· Strong work ethic and respect for confidentiality, given the sensitive nature of the projects handled.

· An interest in shipping, commodities or financial markets.

Benefits

This is a unique opportunity to be part of a high-impact team at the heart of the business. The role offers exposure to strategic decision-making and the potential for career progression within the organization.
